title: Fundamental Limits On Quantum Bit Error Rate And Distance In Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Stefano Pirandola
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Pirandola

Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables information-theoretic secure communication, yet its ultimate tolerance to noise and achievable transmission distance remain fundamentally constrained. We establish the maximum quantum bit error rate (QBER) compatible with secure QKD and derive corresponding upp…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 110801] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on the maximum quantum bit error rate and transmission distance for secure quantum key distribution.
motivation: Quantum key distribution promises information-theoretic secure communication, but its ultimate tolerance to noise and achievable distance remain poorly understood.
method: The author derives theoretical bounds using quantum information and security-proof techniques to characterize the maximum QBER compatible with secure QKD and corresponding distance limits.
result: The work determines the maximum quantum bit error rate for secure QKD and derives upper bounds on the achievable transmission distance.
conclusion: These fundamental limits clarify the physical boundaries of QKD and provide benchmarks for future protocols and experimental implementations.

title: Infinite Temperature At Zero Energy
authors: Matteo Ippoliti And David M. Long
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Ippoliti and David M. Long

Researchers construct local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, producing ground states with extensive entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031030] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates exhibit infinite-temperature properties, yielding ground states with extensive entanglement.
motivation: Understanding entanglement in many-body ground states and the limits of area laws motivates this work.
method: The authors design local Hamiltonians such that all eigenstates have infinite-temperature properties and analyze the entanglement entropy scaling of the resulting ground states.
result: They find ground states with extensive (volume-law) entanglement, violating typical area-law behavior for local Hamiltonians.
conclusion: This provides a new class of exactly solvable models with anomalous entanglement, with implications for quantum information and statistical mechanics.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A new protocol prepares high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs for distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation with low spacetime cost and only 2D local device connectivity.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires high-fidelity logical entanglement between quantum processors, but noisy physical Bell pairs are insufficient and existing methods have high overhead or require all-to-all connectivity.
method: The protocol likely employs quantum error-correcting codes and entanglement distillation to boost the fidelity of logical Bell pairs, using only 2D local interactions to minimize spacetime volume.
result: It achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity, making distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation more practical.
conclusion: This work advances entanglement distillation and fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient logical Bell pair preparation, reducing resource requirements for distributed quantum architectures.

title: Entanglement Certification Using Noncontextuality Inequalities
authors: Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers demonstrate a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without requiring prior measurement device characterization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031057] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that can detect entangled states without prior measurement device characterization.
motivation: Standard entanglement certification often relies on trusted measurement devices or assumptions about their calibration, which can be impractical or insecure. There is a need for certification schemes that are robust to device imperfections and gauge choices.
method: The authors derive noncontextuality inequalities and use them to construct an entanglement witness that is independent of gauge choices, allowing certification even when measurement devices are uncharacterized.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the method, detecting entangled states without requiring prior knowledge of the measurement devices, thus providing a practical tool for entanglement certification.
conclusion: This work bridges noncontextuality inequalities and entanglement theory, offering a new device-independent-like approach for certifying entanglement in realistic scenarios.

title: Strong Coupling Between Propagating Spin Waves And Microwave Photons In A Superconducting Resonator
authors: Yi Li, Jinho Lim, Xingzhi Wang, Tomas Polakovic, Carissa Kiehl, Moojune Song, Phuoc Cao Van, Ralu Divan, Ulrich Welp, Charudatta Phatak, Jong-Ryul Jeong, Kab-Jin Kim, Jian-Min Zuo, Axel Hoffmann, And Valentine Novosad
abstract:
Author(s): Yi Li, Jinho Lim, Xingzhi Wang, Tomas Polakovic, Carissa Kiehl, Moojune Song, Phuoc Cao Van, Ralu Divan, Ulrich Welp, Charudatta Phatak, Jong-Ryul Jeong, Kab-Jin Kim, Jian-Min Zuo, Axel Hoffmann, and Valentine Novosad

We demonstrate strong coupling between propagating spin-wave modes and microwave photons in superconducting resonator-magnetic thin film hybrid circuits. By fabricating the resonator directly on yttrium iron garnet thin films grown on rare-earth-free ${}_{3}{}_{2}{}_{…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116706] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates strong coupling between propagating spin-wave modes and microwave photons in a superconducting resonator fabricated on yttrium iron garnet thin films.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems integrating magnons with superconducting circuits are promising for coherent quantum transduction and information processing, but strong coupling between propagating spin waves and cavity photons remains challenging.
method: The authors fabricate a superconducting resonator directly on yttrium iron garnet thin films and perform microwave spectroscopy to observe coupling between spin-wave modes and resonator photons.
result: They observe strong coupling between propagating spin-wave modes and microwave photons, evidenced by mode splitting in the transmission spectra.
conclusion: The demonstrated platform provides a coherent magnon-photon interface in superconducting circuits, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum networking and transduction.

title: Impossibility Of Perfect Cheating For Single-qubit Position Verification
authors: Carl A. Miller And Yusuf Alnawakhtha
abstract:
Author(s): Carl A. Miller and Yusuf Alnawakhtha

In quantum position verification (QPV), a prover certifies her location to a set of verifiers by performing a quantum computation. One of the first QPV protocols was proposed by Kent, Munro, and Spiller in 2011: The prover receives a qubit [MATH] from one direction, receives an orthogonal basis ${v,{v}…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032207] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves an impossibility result showing that perfect cheating is impossible for single-qubit quantum position verification protocols, specifically the Kent-Munro-Spiller protocol.
motivation: Quantum position verification aims to certify a prover's location using quantum communication, but the security of early single-qubit protocols against cheating strategies remained incompletely understood.
method: The authors analyze the single-qubit Kent-Munro-Spiller QPV protocol using quantum information-theoretic security arguments to bound an adversary's cheating probability.
result: They establish that no adversary can perfectly cheat the protocol, providing a rigorous impossibility of perfect cheating for single-qubit position verification.
conclusion: These findings clarify the security limitations and guarantees of single-qubit QPV protocols, contributing to the broader understanding of quantum cryptographic position verification.

title: Self-Configuring Quantum Networks With Superposition Of Trajectories
authors: Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, And Wolfgang Dür
abstract:
Author(s): Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, and Wolfgang Dür

A self-configuring quantum network protocol integrates superposed quantum paths with variational optimization techniques to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections without requiring prior noise knowledge.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033038] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: A self-configuring quantum network protocol uses superposed quantum paths and variational optimization to establish high-fidelity connections despite decoherence and unknown noise.
motivation: Quantum networks require reliable entanglement distribution, but decoherence and unknown noise degrade connections; adaptive protocols are needed to maintain fidelity without prior noise characterization.
method: The protocol integrates superposed quantum trajectories with variational optimization techniques to dynamically configure network paths and mitigate decoherence.
result: The approach achieves high-fidelity connections in a self-configuring manner without requiring prior knowledge of the noise environment.
conclusion: This work introduces a practical route toward robust, adaptive quantum networks by combining quantum path superposition with variational learning.

title: Robust Superradiance And Spontaneous Spin Ordering In Disordered Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, and Peter Rabl

Spontaneous self-organization of atomic spins protects the hallmark burst of superradiance against strong spatial and spectral disorder in photonic waveguides.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033034] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: Spontaneous ordering of atomic spins in disordered waveguide QED protects superradiant bursts against strong spatial and spectral disorder.
motivation: Superradiance is a hallmark collective quantum optical effect, but it is fragile against disorder in realistic photonic environments, limiting its robustness and applications.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of atomic spins coupled to a photonic waveguide with spatial and spectral disorder, analyzing self-organization and collective emission dynamics.
result: They find a spontaneous spin-ordering phase that shields the superradiant emission burst from disorder, maintaining robust collective behavior.
conclusion: This work establishes a disorder-robust mechanism for superradiance in waveguide QED, advancing collective quantum optics and hybrid quantum platforms.

title: All Steerable Quantum Correlations Can Provide Thermodynamic Advantages In Cooling
authors: Tanmoy Biswas, Chandan Datta, And Luis Pedro García-Pintos
abstract:
Author(s): Tanmoy Biswas, Chandan Datta, and Luis Pedro García-Pintos

The removal of heat generated during computation poses a major challenge for both classical and quantum computation and information processing. In particular, removal of this heat is intrinsically tied to one of the fundamental requirements of quantum computation—the need to reset the system to a pu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 110404] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that every steerable quantum correlation can provide a thermodynamic advantage in cooling quantum systems.
motivation: Heat removal and resetting to pure states are fundamental bottlenecks in quantum computation, so identifying quantum resources that improve cooling is of practical and foundational interest.
method: The authors develop a thermodynamic framework linking quantum steering to cooling performance, comparing steerable and unsteerable correlations in resetting/cooling protocols.
result: They show that all steerable quantum correlations yield a thermodynamic advantage in cooling, establishing steering as a resource beyond nonlocality and device-independent tasks.
conclusion: Steerable correlations can serve as a thermodynamic resource for cooling and resetting, bridging quantum information and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Asynchronous Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Cryptographic Conferencing
authors: Haotao Zhu, Zhenhua Li, Shuai Zhao, Xiaodan Lyu, Shihao Ru, Yizhi Huang, Zitong Xu, Rui Qu, And Weibo Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Haotao Zhu, Zhenhua Li, Shuai Zhao, Xiaodan Lyu, Shihao Ru, Yizhi Huang, Zitong Xu, Rui Qu, and Weibo Gao

Quantum networks enable a variety of quantum information processing tasks, where multiuser quantum communication is one of the important objectives. Quantum cryptographic conferencing (QCC) serves as an essential solution to establish secure keys to realize secure multiuser communications. However, …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 110802] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates asynchronous measurement-device-independent quantum cryptographic conferencing for secure multiuser communication.
motivation: Quantum networks require practical solutions for multiuser secure key establishment, and quantum cryptographic conferencing offers a way to achieve this, but experimental demonstrations remain challenging.
method: The authors implement an asynchronous measurement-device-independent protocol to enable quantum cryptographic conferencing among multiple users over a network.
result: They successfully demonstrate the protocol experimentally, establishing secure keys for multiuser communication while removing detector-side vulnerabilities.
conclusion: This work advances the development of practical quantum networks by providing an experimental foundation for scalable, secure multiuser quantum communication.

title: Entanglement Thresholds For Sequential Nonlocality Sharing In Star Networks
authors: Ming-Xiao Li, Yuqi Li, Rui-Bin Xu, Mo-Ran Zhu, Haitao Ma, Chang-Yue Zhang, And Zhu-Jun Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Ming-Xiao Li, Yuqi Li, Rui-Bin Xu, Mo-Ran Zhu, Haitao Ma, Chang-Yue Zhang, and Zhu-Jun Zheng

Quantum networks promise scalable distributed quantum information processing. Realizing this potential depends critically on the efficient use of nonclassical resources. Sequential sharing of quantum nonlocality provides a resource-efficient route for recycling entanglement across multiple observers…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033274] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives entanglement thresholds for sequential sharing of nonlocality among multiple observers in star-shaped quantum networks.
motivation: Sequential sharing of nonlocality offers a resource-efficient way to recycle entanglement across observers, but the conditions for nonlocality sharing in star-network configurations require further clarification.
method: The authors analyze Bell nonlocality in star networks and establish quantitative thresholds on the entanglement needed for sequential nonlocality sharing.
result: Critical entanglement thresholds are identified that determine whether nonlocality can be shared sequentially across multiple observers in the network.
conclusion: These thresholds provide conditions for resource-efficient nonlocality distribution in star networks, with implications for quantum network design.

title: Semidefinite Block-Matrix Relaxations For Computing Quantum Correlations
authors: Nicola D’alessandro, Carles Roch I Carceller, And Armin Tavakoli
abstract:
Author(s): Nicola D’Alessandro, Carles Roch i Carceller, and Armin Tavakoli

Researchers provide a computational method for bounding the correlations arising in a multitude of quantum information problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031050] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces semidefinite block-matrix relaxations to compute bounds on quantum correlations arising in various quantum information tasks.
motivation: Computing quantum correlations, such as those in Bell scenarios and entanglement detection, is computationally challenging and often requires efficient relaxation methods.
method: The authors develop semidefinite programming relaxations based on block matrices to bound sets of quantum correlations, extending or generalizing existing hierarchies.
result: The method provides computationally tractable bounds for a wide range of quantum information problems, potentially improving on prior techniques.
conclusion: These block-matrix relaxations offer a versatile and powerful tool for characterizing quantum correlations in nonlocality and entanglement theory.

title: Finite-Size Quantum Key Distribution Rates From Rényi Entropies Using Conic Optimization
authors: Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, and Mateus Araújo

A conic optimization method addressing a critical challenge in key rate estimation for quantum key distribution is presented, providing tighter security bounds and fast numerical convergence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033051] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a conic optimization method using Rényi entropies to compute tighter finite-size quantum key distribution rates with fast numerical convergence.
motivation: Finite-size key rate estimation in QKD is challenging because security proofs often yield loose bounds and slow numerical optimization, limiting practical deployment.
method: The authors formulate the key rate estimation as a conic optimization problem that incorporates Rényi entropies to tighten finite-size security bounds.
result: The method achieves tighter security bounds and faster numerical convergence compared to existing approaches for finite-size QKD key rates.
conclusion: This work advances practical QKD security analysis by providing a computationally efficient and tighter framework for finite-size key rate estimation.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Optimizing piezoelectric transducers in bulk acoustic resonators improves phonon coherence time and cooperativity, providing a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics with superconducting circuits.
motivation: High-coherence mechanical resonators are key for hybrid quantum systems and quantum acoustics, but loss mechanisms limiting phonon coherence need to be understood and mitigated.
method: The authors systematically optimize the piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators coupled to superconducting circuits and analyze the resulting loss channels.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence times and cooperativity, and identify material and design guidelines for high-coherence multimode mechanical resonators.
conclusion: This work advances the physical platform for coupling mechanical modes to superconducting qubits and offers a blueprint for future quantum acoustics devices.

title: Network-Irreducible Multiparty Entanglement In Quantum Matter
authors: Liuke Lyu, Pedro Lauand, And William Witczak-Krempa
abstract:
Author(s): Liuke Lyu, Pedro Lauand, and William Witczak-Krempa

We show that the standard approach to characterize collective entanglement via genuine multiparty entanglement (GME) leads to an area law in ground and thermal Gibbs states of local Hamiltonians. To capture the truly collective part one needs to go beyond this short-range contribution tied to interf…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 110204] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces network-irreducible multiparty entanglement to capture collective entanglement in quantum matter beyond the area-law behavior of standard genuine multiparty entanglement.
motivation: Standard genuine multiparty entanglement (GME) in ground and thermal states of local Hamiltonians obeys an area law, hiding the truly collective, long-range entanglement that may be present.
method: The authors define a network-irreducible measure of multiparty entanglement and analyze ground and thermal Gibbs states of local Hamiltonians to separate short-range from genuinely collective contributions.
result: They show that conventional GME is dominated by short-range, area-law contributions, while the network-irreducible part reveals the genuinely collective multiparty entanglement.
conclusion: This provides a new information-theoretic tool for characterizing multiparty entanglement in quantum many-body systems, with implications for entanglement theory in quantum matter.

title: Topological Quantum Transducers Between Microwave And Optical Photons In A Hybrid Rydberg Atom-cavity System
authors: Pei-Yao Song, Jin-Lei Wu, Weibin Li, And Shi-Lei Su
abstract:
Author(s): Pei-Yao Song, Jin-Lei Wu, Weibin Li, and Shi-Lei Su

We propose a topological transport platform for microwave-to-optical conversion at the single-photon level in a Rydberg atom-cavity setting. This setting leverages a hybrid dual-mode Jaynes-Cummings (JC) configuration, in which the coupling between a microwave resonator and an optical cavity is medi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033712] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a topological microwave-to-optical single-photon transducer in a hybrid Rydberg atom-cavity system using a dual-mode Jaynes-Cummings setup.
motivation: Coherent conversion between microwave and optical photons is essential for connecting superconducting quantum processors with optical quantum networks, but efficient single-photon transduction remains challenging.
method: The authors design a hybrid dual-mode Jaynes-Cummings configuration where a microwave resonator couples to an optical cavity via Rydberg atoms, and they engineer topological transport for the conversion process.
result: The scheme enables topological transport of excitations for microwave-to-optical conversion at the single-photon level in a Rydberg atom-cavity platform.
conclusion: This hybrid topological platform offers a promising route toward robust quantum transducers for microwave-optical interfacing in quantum networks.

title: Initiation Of Superradiance From Different Collective-spin States
authors: Adnan N. Alabbar, Zhenghao Zhang, And Girish S. Agarwal
abstract:
Author(s): Adnan N. Alabbar, Zhenghao Zhang, and Girish S. Agarwal

Superradiance is an extensive cooperative spontaneous emission phenomenon, exhibited by some atomic collective-spin states. However, distinct initial states differ in their decay dynamics. Dicke states [MATH] with distinct numbers of excitations [MATH], driven by vacuum fluctuations, have their pe…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033713] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates how superradiance initiation depends on different initial collective-spin (Dicke) states, revealing distinct decay dynamics.
motivation: Superradiance is a fundamental cooperative emission phenomenon, yet the role of the initial collective-spin state in its initiation and decay dynamics remains incompletely understood.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of Dicke states with varying numbers of excitations, likely using a quantum master equation or similar theoretical framework to model the cooperative spontaneous emission.
result: Different initial Dicke states exhibit qualitatively distinct superradiance initiation times and decay profiles, showing strong dependence on the number and distribution of excitations.
conclusion: The study provides insight into how preparing specific collective-spin states can control superradiance, with potential implications for quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Interpolation Of Entanglement Purification Protocols
authors: Matthew Barber And Stefano Pirandola
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Barber and Stefano Pirandola

Bipartite entanglement purification is the conversion of copies of weakly entangled pairs shared between two separated parties into a smaller number of strongly entangled shared pairs using only local operations and classical communication. Choosing between different entanglement purification protoc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032416] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an optimal interpolation method for selecting among bipartite entanglement purification protocols under local operations and classical communication.
motivation: Bipartite entanglement purification is essential for converting weakly entangled pairs into fewer strongly entangled pairs, but different purification protocols perform best in different noise regimes, so a systematic way to interpolate between them is needed.
method: The authors formulate the problem of interpolating between entanglement purification protocols and optimize the interpolation to maximize the resulting entanglement per consumed copy.
result: The optimal interpolation yields improved purification performance compared with individual protocols alone, providing a principled way to choose between protocols.
conclusion: This work offers a general framework for optimizing entanglement purification, with implications for quantum communication and entanglement distribution.

title: Thermodynamic Efficiency Of Self-organization In Nonequilibrium Steady States
authors: Qianyang Chen And Mikhail Prokopenko
abstract:
Author(s): Qianyang Chen and Mikhail Prokopenko

Active matter generates order or patterns through nonequilibrium dynamics. An open research challenge is to determine how efficiently a nonequilibrium self-organizing system can convert consumed energy into macroscopic order. We study an information-theoretic quantity that directly addresses this ch…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033265] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an information-theoretic quantity to quantify how efficiently a nonequilibrium self-organizing system converts consumed energy into macroscopic order.
motivation: Active matter and nonequilibrium dynamics can spontaneously generate order, but quantifying the thermodynamic efficiency of this self-organization remains an open challenge.
method: The authors analyze an information-theoretic measure in the context of nonequilibrium steady states, linking energy consumption, information, and the emergence of macroscopic order.
result: They characterize the efficiency of self-organization through information-theoretic quantities, providing a framework to relate energy dissipation and order formation in steady states.
conclusion: The work offers a principled way to evaluate the thermodynamic efficiency of self-organization, with implications for active matter and nonequilibrium information thermodynamics.

title: Single-click Protocols For Remote State Preparation Using Weak Coherent Pulses
authors: Janice van Dam, Emil R. Hellebek, Tzula B. Propp, Junior R. Gonzales-Ureta, Anders S. Sørensen, And Stephanie D. C. Wehner
abstract:
Author(s): Janice van Dam, Emil R. Hellebek, Tzula B. Propp, Junior R. Gonzales-Ureta, Anders S. Sørensen, and Stephanie D. C. Wehner

Remote state preparation (RSP) allows one party to remotely prepare a known quantum state on another party's qubit using entanglement. This can be used in quantum networks to perform applications such as blind quantum computing or long-distance quantum key distribution (QKD) with quantum repeaters. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033272] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents single-click protocols for remote state preparation using weak coherent pulses, aimed at practical quantum network applications.
motivation: Remote state preparation is needed for quantum networks to enable applications such as blind quantum computing and long-distance quantum key distribution with quantum repeaters, but practical implementations require robust protocols compatible with realistic photon sources.
method: They design and analyze single-click remote state preparation protocols based on weak coherent pulses, likely using linear optics and single-photon detection, and evaluate their performance.
result: The protocols achieve remote state preparation using weak coherent pulses, potentially simplifying experimental requirements for quantum network nodes.
conclusion: These single-click remote state preparation protocols offer a practical route toward implementing quantum network functionalities such as blind quantum computing and repeater-based quantum key distribution.

title: Quantum Thermal State Preparation For Near-Term Quantum Processors
authors: Jerome Lloyd And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): Jerome Lloyd and Dmitry A. Abanin

Researchers develop an algorithm that prepares many-body quantum thermal states accurately by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031053] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an algorithm for accurately preparing many-body quantum thermal states on near-term quantum processors by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.
motivation: Efficient preparation of thermal states is crucial for simulating quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems on near-term quantum devices.
method: The algorithm combines repeated bath resetting with modulated coupling between the system and a bath to drive the system toward its thermal state.
result: The approach is shown to prepare many-body quantum thermal states accurately, making it suitable for near-term quantum processors.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route for studying quantum thermalization and thermodynamics on current quantum hardware.

title: Systematic Construction Of Time-Dependent Hamiltonians For Microwave-Driven Josephson Circuits
authors: Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, And Robert J. Schoelkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, and Robert J. Schoelkopf

A versatile framework bridges layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics, enabling realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033039] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: A versatile framework bridges layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics to systematically construct time-dependent Hamiltonians for microwave-driven Josephson circuits.
motivation: Realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits requires going beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions to capture layout-level electromagnetic effects.
method: The authors develop a systematic procedure that combines classical microwave simulations of the circuit layout with quantum dynamical descriptions to derive accurate time-dependent Hamiltonians for driven Josephson circuits.
result: The framework enables realistic modeling of microwave-driven superconducting circuits, capturing effects that simplified models miss and providing a tool for designing and analyzing such circuits.
conclusion: This approach offers a versatile and accurate method for modeling driven superconducting quantum circuits, with potential applications in circuit QED and superconducting qubit engineering.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Fast and high-fidelity qubit readout is essential for quantum computing, but standard readout schemes suffer from Purcell decay and limited speed.
method: The authors design a readout architecture based on nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling between a transmon and a readout resonator, which inherently suppresses Purcell decay.
result: The scheme enables fast, high-fidelity measurement while providing built-in Purcell protection, as demonstrated experimentally or theoretically.
conclusion: This architecture offers a promising route for scalable superconducting quantum processors with improved readout performance.

title: Dual Memory For Light Based On Spontaneous Zeeman Coherence Transfer
authors: L. G. Da S. Santos, J. C. de Aquino Carvalho, And J. W. R. Tabosa
abstract:
Author(s): L. G. da S. Santos, J. C. de Aquino Carvalho, and J. W. R. Tabosa

We report the observation of light storage in a dual memory associated with Zeeman coherence belonging to different hyperfine ground-state levels of cold cesium atoms. This double memory is based on the phenomenon of spontaneous Zeeman coherence transfer as predicted by the tensorial density-matrix …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033715] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the experimental observation of light storage in a dual quantum memory using spontaneous Zeeman coherence transfer between hyperfine ground-state levels of cold cesium atoms.
motivation: Quantum memories are essential building blocks for quantum networks and repeaters, and dual memories can enhance storage capacity or enable novel protocols. This work explores a specific physical mechanism to realize such a memory.
method: The authors use cold cesium atoms and employ spontaneous Zeeman coherence transfer to store light in two distinct memory modes associated with different hyperfine ground states.
result: They observe light storage in a dual memory based on this coherence transfer, demonstrating the possibility of storing and retrieving light in two separate Zeeman coherences.
conclusion: The dual memory based on spontaneous Zeeman coherence transfer could be useful for quantum network applications, offering a new approach to multiplexed quantum memory.

title: Spectroscopy And Coherence Of An Excited-state Transition In ${\mathrm{Tm}}^{3+}:{\mathrm{YAlO}}_{3}$ At Telecommunication Wavelength
authors: Luozhen Li, Akshay Babu Karyath, Julien Bertrand, Mohsen Falamarzi Askarani, Maria Gieysztor, Hridya Meppully Sasidharan, Joshua A. Slater, Aaron D. Marsh, Philip J. T. Woodburn, Charles W. Thiel, Rufus L. Cone, Sara Marzban, Nir Alfasi, Patrick Remy, And Wolfgang Tittel
abstract:
Author(s): Luozhen Li, Akshay Babu Karyath, Julien Bertrand, Mohsen Falamarzi Askarani, Maria Gieysztor, Hridya Meppully Sasidharan, Joshua A. Slater, Aaron D. Marsh, Philip J. T. Woodburn, Charles W. Thiel, Rufus L. Cone, Sara Marzban, Nir Alfasi, Patrick Remy, and Wolfgang Tittel

We characterize spectroscopic and coherence properties of the 1451.37 nm excited-state zero-phonon line (ZPL) between the [MATH] and the [MATH] manifolds of a thulium-doped yttrium aluminum perovskite ([MATH]) crystal at temperatures arou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033284] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper characterizes the spectroscopic and coherence properties of a 1451.37 nm excited-state zero-phonon line in Tm3+:YAlO3, a rare-earth-doped crystal relevant for telecom-wavelength quantum memories.
motivation: Telecom-wavelength quantum memories are needed for quantum repeaters and long-distance entanglement distribution, and Tm3+:YAlO3 offers a promising excited-state transition in the low-loss optical fiber band.
method: The authors perform high-resolution laser spectroscopy and coherence measurements (e.g., optical/Raman-type coherence studies) on the excited-state ZPL of Tm3+:YAlO3 at cryogenic temperatures to determine linewidths, lifetimes, and dephasing behavior.
result: They report detailed spectroscopic parameters and coherence times for the 1451.37 nm excited-state transition, identifying the dominant broadening and decoherence mechanisms at varying temperatures.
conclusion: The results establish Tm3+:YAlO3 as a viable candidate platform for telecom-compatible quantum memory and networking applications, while highlighting coherence limits to be overcome.

title: Privacy In Continuous-Variable Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, And Ulrik L. Andersen
abstract:
Author(s): A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, and Ulrik L. Andersen

The feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in network scenarios is investigated through achievable protocols and no-go results.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033036] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates the feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in network scenarios, providing achievable protocols and no-go results.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing offers enhanced precision, but the privacy of the estimated parameters in network settings is critical yet underexplored.
method: The authors analyze continuous-variable quantum parameter estimation in network scenarios, deriving achievable protocols and no-go theorems for privacy.
result: They establish conditions for private distributed quantum sensing and identify fundamental limitations, showing that privacy imposes fundamental limits on achievable precision and that there is a trade-off between privacy and estimation accuracy.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A universal scheme is proposed to accumulate entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated qubit-qudit entanglement transfer, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
motivation: Long-lived nuclear spins in defect centers are promising quantum memories, but transferring and accumulating entanglement in higher-dimensional qudits remains challenging.
method: The authors design a repeated entanglement transfer protocol between a qubit and high-spin nuclei in defect centers, using the nuclear spin as a qudit memory.
result: The scheme achieves accumulation of entanglement between nuclear qudits, potentially enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: This work provides a route toward qudit-based quantum networks using defect-center nuclear memories.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact, mechanically stable quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip with fiber coupling enables efficient photon extraction from neutral atoms.
motivation: Efficient photon extraction and stable fiber coupling are essential for building practical quantum networks with neutral atoms.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated on an optical chip with fiber in/out coupling to collect and guide photons from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves efficient photon extraction in a compact and mechanically stable package.
conclusion: This provides a promising building block for future quantum networking experiments using neutral atoms.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a triangle criterion, inspired by entanglement theory, for detecting nonstabilizerness in mixed states and certifying undistillability of magic states.
motivation: Magic (nonstabilizerness) is a key resource for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but efficient mixed-state criteria and operational characterizations for magic remain less developed than their entanglement counterparts.
method: The authors develop a simple geometric criterion, analogous to entanglement witnesses, that applies to mixed states and can be used for magic state detection and distillation analysis.
result: The criterion successfully detects nonstabilizerness in mixed states and certifies undistillability, providing operational applications in magic state distillation and detection.
conclusion: This work advances the resource theory of magic by offering practical tools for mixed-state certification and distillation, bridging concepts from entanglement theory to nonstabilizer resources.

title: Achieving The Heisenberg Limit Using Fault-tolerant Quantum Error Correction
authors: Himanshu Sahu, Qian Xu, And Sisi Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Himanshu Sahu, Qian Xu, and Sisi Zhou

Quantum effect enables enhanced estimation precision in metrology, with the Heisenberg limit (HL) representing the ultimate limit allowed by quantum mechanics. Although the HL is generally unattainable in the presence of noise, quantum error correction (QEC) can recover the HL in various scenarios. …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032607] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that fault-tolerant quantum error correction can recover the Heisenberg limit for quantum metrology in the presence of noise.
motivation: The Heisenberg limit is the ultimate precision allowed by quantum mechanics, but it is generally destroyed by noise, motivating the use of quantum error correction to restore it.
method: The authors analyze and construct fault-tolerant quantum error correction schemes for metrological tasks, using tools from quantum error correction and fault tolerance to protect estimation protocols.
result: They demonstrate that fault-tolerant QEC can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in various noisy scenarios where the limit would otherwise be unattainable.
conclusion: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction provides a viable route to Heisenberg-limited quantum metrology, linking QEC theory with quantum-enhanced sensing.

title: General Quantum Circuit Framework For Extended Wigner’s Friend Scenarios: Logically And Causally Consistent Reasoning Without Absolute Measurement Events
authors: V. Vilasini And Mischa P. Woods
abstract:
Author(s): V. Vilasini and Mischa P. Woods

Researchers develop a quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner’s friend scenarios, resolving logical paradoxes by tracking Heisenberg cuts.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031062] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a general quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner's friend scenarios that tracks Heisenberg cuts to eliminate logical paradoxes and permit logically and causally consistent reasoning without absolute measurement events.
motivation: Extended Wigner's friend scenarios expose apparent contradictions between quantum theory and observer-independent reasoning, and existing ad hoc treatments lack a unified, formally clean account of where and how measurements occur.
method: The authors formalize the scenarios as quantum circuits in which measurement events are not absolute but defined relative to a choice of Heisenberg cut, then analyze the resulting logical and causal structure of the reasoning within this framework.
result: The framework reproduces known no-go conclusions while showing that paradoxes arise only from implicit assumptions about absolute measurement events, and it yields consistent localized descriptions once the cut is made explicit.
conclusion: Tracked Heisenberg cuts provide a rigorous, general language for multi-observer quantum reasoning, clarifying foundational debates and connecting Wigner's friend arguments to broader quantum-information and causal-inference concepts.

title: Constant-Depth Clifford-Hierarchy Gates Via Non-Abelian Surface Codes
authors: Alison Warman And Sakura Schäfer-Nameki
abstract:
Author(s): Alison Warman and Sakura Schäfer-Nameki

Using non-Abelian topological order, it is shown that two-dimensional, local, and topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033029] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that non-Abelian surface codes enable constant-depth, topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy in two dimensions.
motivation: Achieving universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with local, topologically protected gates is a central challenge; non-Abelian anyons offer a promising route but previous constructions had limited gate sets.
method: Using non-Abelian topological order and surface code constructions, the authors design local operations that implement logical gates in the Clifford hierarchy.
result: They show that constant-depth circuits can realize gates at arbitrary levels of the Clifford hierarchy while preserving topological protection.
conclusion: This establishes a path toward universal topological quantum computation using non-Abelian surface codes.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes that achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reliable error correction for a variety of topological orders, including exotic fermionic and chiral phases that are challenging to handle with conventional methods.
method: The authors construct a family of 3D stabilizer codes, called chiral color codes, and analyze their error-correcting properties under single-shot decoding.
result: These codes enable single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, providing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: The chiral color code expands the toolbox for topological quantum error correction and may facilitate the realization of fault-tolerant quantum computers based on exotic topological phases.

title: Local Reversibility And Divergent Markov Length In $1+1$-d Directed Percolation
authors: Yu-Hsueh Chen And Tarun Grover
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Hsueh Chen and Tarun Grover

Recent progress in open many-body quantum systems has highlighted the importance of the Markov length, the characteristic scale over which conditional correlations decay. It has been proposed that nonequilibrium phases of matter can be defined as equivalence classes of states connected by short-time…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 110402] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies local reversibility and divergent Markov length in 1+1-dimensional directed percolation, linking nonequilibrium phases of open many-body quantum systems to the decay of conditional correlations.
motivation: Recent proposals define nonequilibrium phases of matter as equivalence classes of states connected by short-time local operations, but the behavior of the Markov length—the scale of conditional correlation decay—in directed percolation remains poorly understood.
method: The authors analyze 1+1-dimensional directed percolation using concepts of local reversibility and conditional mutual information, likely combining analytical arguments with numerical simulations to track the Markov length across the transition.
result: They find that the Markov length diverges at the directed percolation transition and that local reversibility distinguishes different nonequilibrium phases, providing an information-theoretic diagnostic of criticality.
conclusion: The Markov length serves as a key quantity for characterizing nonequilibrium phases and criticality in open many-body quantum systems, with implications for defining phases via short-time local equivalence.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of A Multisigner Quantum Digital Signature System
authors: Wenli Ding, Xi Deng, Chao Li, Yuanhua Li, Jia Lin, Yuanlin Zheng, And Xianfeng Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Wenli Ding, Xi Deng, Chao Li, Yuanhua Li, Jia Lin, Yuanlin Zheng, and Xianfeng Chen

Quantum digital signatures (QDSs) utilize shared keys generated by quantum key distribution, thereby providing information-theoretic security. Most existing QDS schemes, however, only support single-signer scenarios, which limits their applications in large-scale quantum networks. Based on previous …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032417] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: An experimental demonstration of a multisigner quantum digital signature system that extends QDS to multiple signers for large-scale quantum networks.
motivation: Most existing quantum digital signature schemes only support single-signer scenarios, limiting their use in large-scale quantum networks.
method: The authors implement a multisigner QDS protocol based on shared keys generated by quantum key distribution, providing information-theoretic security.
result: They experimentally demonstrate a multisigner quantum digital signature system, showing its feasibility for multi-party quantum communication.
conclusion: The work offers a practical step toward deploying quantum digital signatures in future large-scale quantum networks.

title: Unified Theory Of Local Integrals Of Motion
authors: Ben Craps, Oleg Evnin, Dmitry Kovrizhin, And Gabriele Pascuzzi
abstract:
Author(s): Ben Craps, Oleg Evnin, Dmitry Kovrizhin, and Gabriele Pascuzzi

Conservation laws are of paramount importance in our understanding of classical and quantum dynamics. Here, we present a general framework for constructing exact quantum integrals of motion with the desired locality and quantum numbers, which will be illustrated for the case of many-body-localizatio…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L140201] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A general framework for constructing exact local integrals of motion in quantum many-body systems, illustrated for many-body localization.
motivation: Conservation laws and integrals of motion are central to understanding quantum dynamics, especially in systems like many-body localization (MBL) where they underpin non-ergodic behavior.
method: The authors develop a systematic construction of exact quantum integrals of motion with prescribed locality and quantum numbers, applying it to MBL systems.
result: They obtain explicit local integrals of motion for MBL, providing a unified theoretical treatment.
conclusion: This framework clarifies the structure of local conservation laws in MBL and may extend to other quantum systems with emergent integrability.

title: Correlation Enhanced Autonomous Quantum Battery Charging Via Structured Reservoirs
authors: A. Khoudiri, A. El Allati, Y. Khlifi, K. El Anouz, And Ö. E. Müstecaplıoğlu
abstract:
Author(s): A. Khoudiri, A. El Allati, Y. Khlifi, K. El Anouz, and Ö. E. Müstecaplıoğlu

In this work, we investigate the autonomous charging process of a quantum battery coupled to a structured reservoir composed of two qubits, each locally coupled to its own bosonic thermal bath. Moreover, the reservoir interacts with a charger–battery architecture through three configurations: (I) di…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034116] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates autonomous charging of a quantum battery coupled to a structured two-qubit reservoir, showing that reservoir correlations can enhance the charging process.
motivation: Quantum batteries require efficient autonomous charging mechanisms, and structured reservoirs with internal correlations may offer thermodynamic advantages over conventional unstructured thermal baths.
method: The authors model three configurations of a charger-battery architecture interacting with a structured reservoir composed of two qubits, each locally coupled to its own bosonic thermal bath, and analyze the charging dynamics using open quantum system techniques.
result: They find that correlations in the structured reservoir can improve charging performance, such as increased energy stored or charging power, relative to uncorrelated or unstructured reservoirs depending on the configuration.
conclusion: Structured reservoirs and quantum correlations provide a promising route to enhance autonomous quantum battery charging, with potential implications for quantum thermodynamic devices.

title: High-fidelity All-microwave Cz Gate With Partial Erasure-error Detection Via A Transmon Coupler
authors: Shotaro Shirai, Shinichi Inoue, Shuhei Tamate, Rui Li, Yasunobu Nakamura, And Atsushi Noguchi
abstract:
Author(s): Shotaro Shirai, Shinichi Inoue, Shuhei Tamate, Rui Li, Yasunobu Nakamura, and Atsushi Noguchi

Entangling gates between neighboring physical qubits are essential for quantum error correction. Implementing them in an all-microwave manner simplifies signal routing and control apparatus of superconducting quantum processors. We propose and experimentally demonstrate an all-microwave controlled-Z…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033261] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: An all-microwave controlled-Z gate between superconducting transmon qubits mediated by a tunable coupler, achieving high fidelity with partial erasure-error detection.
motivation: Entangling gates are essential for quantum error correction, and implementing them in an all-microwave manner simplifies signal routing and control in superconducting processors while erasure detection improves error handling.
method: The authors propose and experimentally demonstrate an all-microwave CZ gate using a transmon coupler architecture, incorporating a scheme for partial erasure-error detection to flag certain failure events.
result: The gate achieves high fidelity in experiment, and the partial erasure-error detection enables identification of a subset of gate errors that could otherwise be treated as undetectable Pauli errors.
conclusion: All-microwave CZ gates with erasure-error detection offer a practical route to simplified control and improved error mitigation in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Determines The Pure-State I.i.d. Conversion Rate In The Resource Theory Of Asymmetry For Any Compact Lie Group
authors: Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, And Hiroyasu Tajima
abstract:
Author(s): Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, and Hiroyasu Tajima

Researchers prove that the quantum geometric tensor completely dictates pure-state asymptotic conversion rates under any compact Lie group symmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031028] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: The quantum geometric tensor completely determines the pure-state i.i.d. asymptotic conversion rate in the resource theory of asymmetry for any compact Lie group.
motivation: Asymptotic state conversion rates quantify the operational value of asymmetry as a resource, but a general solution for arbitrary compact Lie group symmetries was lacking.
method: The authors analyze pure-state i.i.d. conversion protocols under compact Lie group symmetry and derive the asymptotic rate in terms of the quantum geometric tensor (quantum Fisher information matrix).
result: They prove that the optimal conversion rate is exactly given by a ratio of quantum geometric tensors, establishing this quantity as the central resource measure for asymmetry.
conclusion: The quantum geometric tensor fully characterizes asymptotic asymmetry conversion, unifying and extending previous results with implications for quantum metrology and resource theories.

title: Logical Accreditation: A Framework For Efficient Certification Of Fault-Tolerant Computations
authors: James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, And Elham Kashefi
abstract:
Author(s): James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, and Elham Kashefi

Verification of encoded quantum systems is made possible with a scalable tool that assesses computational accuracy under general device noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033053] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Logical Accreditation, a scalable framework for certifying the accuracy of fault-tolerant quantum computations under general device noise.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computations require reliable certification of encoded logical operations, but existing verification methods are often inefficient or assume restricted noise models.
method: The authors develop a certification framework for encoded quantum systems that efficiently assesses computational accuracy under general device noise, likely leveraging fault-tolerant encoding and accreditation techniques.
result: The framework provides a scalable tool for verifying fault-tolerant computations, demonstrating its effectiveness under general device noise as published in PRX Quantum.
conclusion: Logical Accreditation enables efficient verification of fault-tolerant quantum computations, advancing practical certification of encoded quantum systems.

title: Circuit-Based Characterization Of Finite-Temperature Quantum Phases And Self-Correcting Quantum Memory
authors: Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, And Shengqi Sang
abstract:
Author(s): Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, and Shengqi Sang

A circuit-based framework characterizing thermal quantum phases via a correlation-decay condition is presented, establishing self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033052] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a circuit-based framework that characterizes finite-temperature quantum phases via correlation decay and shows that self-correction is a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.
motivation: Understanding finite-temperature quantum phases and the conditions for self-correcting quantum memories is crucial for robust quantum information storage and topological quantum error correction.
method: The authors use a circuit-based approach and a correlation-decay condition to analyze thermal quantum phases and memory stability.
result: They establish that self-correction is a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories, providing a general characterization of thermal phases.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum phase classification and quantum error correction, offering new insights into finite-temperature quantum memory.

title: Quantum State Designs From Minimally Random Quantum Circuits
authors: Jonathon Riddell, Katja Klobas, And Bruno Bertini
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathon Riddell, Katja Klobas, and Bruno Bertini

For quantum circuits that generate complex dynamics, a single, one-site operation is sufficient to produce randomness, showcasing a trade-off between dynamical chaos and randomness.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033047] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that quantum circuits generating complex dynamics require only a single one-site operation to produce randomness, revealing a trade-off between dynamical chaos and randomness.
motivation: Understanding the minimal resources needed to generate quantum randomness and state designs is important for quantum information processing, benchmarking, and the study of quantum chaos.
method: The authors analyze random quantum circuits with minimal one-site operations and assess their ability to generate quantum state designs and randomness.
result: A single one-site operation suffices to produce randomness in complex dynamics, demonstrating a trade-off between dynamical chaos and the amount of randomness required.
conclusion: Minimal randomness can yield complex dynamics, which has implications for the design of random quantum circuits and the characterization of quantum chaos.

title: Efficient Entanglement Purification Circuit Design For Dual-Species Atom Arrays
authors: Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, and Liang Jiang

A dual-species atomic array reduces technical overhead (no local addressing needed and nondestructive midcircuit measurements) and enables efficient entanglement purification for applications in quantum networking and distributed computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033044] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents efficient entanglement purification circuit designs for dual-species atom arrays, targeting quantum networking and distributed computation applications.
motivation: Entanglement purification is essential for quantum networks and distributed quantum computing, but practical implementations face technical overhead. Dual-species atom arrays can reduce this overhead by eliminating local addressing and enabling nondestructive midcircuit measurements.
method: The authors design purification circuits that exploit the unique capabilities of dual-species atomic arrays, such as global control and nondestructive midcircuit measurement, to implement efficient entanglement purification.
result: The proposed circuits enable efficient entanglement purification with reduced technical overhead, improving feasibility for networking and distributed computation.
conclusion: Dual-species atom arrays provide a promising platform for scalable entanglement purification in future quantum networks.

title: Analytical Blueprint For 99.999% Fidelity X-Gates On Present Superconducting Hardware Under Strong Driving
authors: José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, And Felix Motzoi
abstract:
Author(s): José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, and Felix Motzoi

A new analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG protocols to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99%.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033040] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: An analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit X-gates with fidelities above 99.99%.
motivation: High-fidelity ultrafast single-qubit gates on superconducting hardware are limited by leakage to higher transmon levels under strong driving, which standard DRAG protocols do not fully address.
method: The authors develop an analytical pulse-shaping framework that extends DRAG protocols to suppress multiphoton leakage and optimize control pulses for strongly driven superconducting transmons.
result: The method yields X-gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99% on present superconducting hardware, demonstrating robustness under strong driving.
conclusion: This provides a practical blueprint for achieving near-perfect single-qubit gates on existing superconducting platforms without requiring hardware improvements.

title: Defect-Free Arrays At The Thousand-Atom Scale In A 4-k Cryogenic Environment
authors: Desiree Lim, Hadriel Mamann, Grégoire Pichard, Lilian Bourachot, Arvid Lindberg, Clotilde Hamot, Hugo Le Bars, Florian Fasola, Siddhy Tan, Gwennolé Cournez, Sylvain Dutartre, Thierry Cartry, Sylvain Lemettre, Richard Hostein, Julien Paris, Franck Ferreyrol, Andréa Collardey, Adrien Signoles, Thierry Lahaye, Corentin Monmeyran, And Bruno Ximenez
abstract:
Author(s): Desiree Lim, Hadriel Mamann, Grégoire Pichard, Lilian Bourachot, Arvid Lindberg, Clotilde Hamot, Hugo Le Bars, Florian Fasola, Siddhy Tan, Gwennolé Cournez, Sylvain Dutartre, Thierry Cartry, Sylvain Lemettre, Richard Hostein, Julien Paris, Franck Ferreyrol, Andréa Collardey, Adrien Signoles, Thierry Lahaye, Corentin Monmeyran, and Bruno Ximenez

Cryogenic operation and high optical access combine to enable creation of perfect neutral-atom arrays with single-atom trapping for thousands of seconds, a key step toward large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033032] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates defect-free neutral-atom arrays with thousands of single atoms trapped for thousands of seconds in a 4 K cryogenic environment, advancing large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing.
motivation: Large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing requires scalable, defect-free arrays of individually trapped atoms with long coherence and trapping lifetimes, which is challenging at room temperature due to vacuum and optical access constraints.
method: Combines cryogenic operation at 4 K with high optical access to create optical tweezer arrays, achieving single-atom trapping and array assembly.
result: The authors realize perfect (defect-free) arrays at the thousand-atom scale, with single-atom trapping lifetimes reaching thousands of seconds.
conclusion: This platform is a key step toward large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing, offering improved scalability and stability for future quantum information processing.

title: No-Go Theorem On Fault Tolerant Gadgets For Multiple Logical Qubits
authors: Aranya Chakraborty And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Aranya Chakraborty and Daniel Gottesman

Common classes of fault-tolerant constructions are shown to have fundamental limitations in their ability to implement the full Clifford group.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033027] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: A no-go theorem showing that common classes of fault-tolerant gadget constructions cannot implement the full Clifford group on multiple logical qubits.
motivation: Fault-tolerant gadget constructions are central to scalable quantum computing, and understanding their fundamental limitations clarifies what logical operations are achievable on encoded qubits.
method: The authors analyze broad classes of fault-tolerant gadgets and prove structural constraints on their ability to realize the full Clifford group across multiple logical qubits.
result: They establish a fundamental limitation: common fault-tolerant construction classes cannot implement the complete Clifford group for multiple logical qubits.
conclusion: The result identifies inherent obstacles in standard fault-tolerant gadget designs, informing the design of future fault-tolerant architectures and transversal/logical gate schemes.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality
authors: Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, And Francesco Da Ros
abstract:
Author(s): Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, and Francesco Da Ros

An integrated silicon photonic architecture enables semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033022] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: An integrated silicon photonic chip implements semi-device-independent quantum random number generation by exploiting contextuality, enabling practical on-chip randomness certification.
motivation: Device-independent randomness certification is highly secure but experimentally demanding, so semi-device-independent protocols based on contextuality offer a practical compromise for integrated photonic platforms.
method: The authors design and fabricate an integrated silicon photonic architecture that generates random bits by measuring contextuality witnesses in a semi-device-independent framework.
result: The chip demonstrates semi-device-independent quantum random number generation, validating contextuality as a resource and showing feasibility for on-chip integration.
conclusion: This work advances practical randomness certification by combining contextuality-based semi-device-independent security with scalable silicon photonics.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum low-density parity-check codes with parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires low overhead in qubits and time, motivating the use of quantum LDPC codes and efficient logical operations.
method: The authors combine good quantum LDPC codes with parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation to enable constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
result: The proposed approach achieves fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes with parallelized code surgery offer a promising route to practical fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms are shown to offer advantages for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation due to the small atomic mass.
motivation: The unique properties of helium-3, particularly its small mass, could enable new capabilities in quantum technologies such as tunable hopping and continuous-variable operations.
method: The authors theoretically and/or experimentally investigate arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms held in optical tweezer potentials, analyzing their potential for quantum simulation and computing.
result: The small mass of helium-3 is found to provide advantages in continuous-variable quantum computing and in simulating materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 atom arrays represent a promising hybrid quantum platform for quantum simulation and continuous-variable quantum information processing.

title: Generating Honeycomb-Structured Entanglement With A Reconfigurable Spatially Structured Pump
authors: Yu Guo, Xiaozhou Pan, Shengshuai Liu, Guanjun Zeng, Kai Zhang, And Jietai Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Yu Guo, Xiaozhou Pan, Shengshuai Liu, Guanjun Zeng, Kai Zhang, and Jietai Jing

Multipartite entanglement is a fundamental resource for quantum information processing. Various degrees of freedom of light, such as time, frequency, and space, have been widely exploited to create large-scale entangled quantum sources, enhancing information transmission capacity. Here, we demonstra…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 110203] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally generates honeycomb-structured multipartite entanglement using a reconfigurable spatially structured pump.
motivation: Multipartite entanglement is a key resource for quantum information processing, and exploiting spatial degrees of freedom can enable large-scale entangled sources and higher information capacity.
method: A reconfigurable spatially structured pump beam is used to create a honeycomb lattice of entangled optical modes, likely through a nonlinear optical process.
result: Honeycomb-structured entanglement across multiple spatial modes is demonstrated, with the pump configuration allowing reconfigurable geometries.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile source of structured multipartite entanglement, potentially useful for quantum information and networking tasks.

title: Practical Roadmap To Measurement-Altered Criticality In Rydberg Arrays
authors: Stephen Naus, Yue Liu, Sara Murciano, Pablo Sala, Manuel Endres, And Jason Alicea
abstract:
Author(s): Stephen Naus, Yue Liu, Sara Murciano, Pablo Sala, Manuel Endres, and Jason Alicea

Weak measurements have been predicted to dramatically alter universal properties of quantum critical wave functions, though experimental validation remains an open problem. Here we devise a practical scheme for realizing measurement-altered criticality in a chain of Rydberg atoms tuned to Ising and …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 110403] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a practical experimental roadmap to realize measurement-altered criticality using a chain of Rydberg atoms tuned to Ising and related critical points.
motivation: Weak measurements are predicted to dramatically alter universal properties of quantum critical wave functions, but this effect has not yet been experimentally validated.
method: The authors devise a concrete scheme based on Rydberg atom arrays, exploiting tunable Ising interactions and local weak measurements to access measurement-altered criticality.
result: The proposed protocol identifies accessible parameter regimes and observables where measurement-altered critical behavior can be detected in current Rydberg experiments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical guide for experimentalists to observe measurement-induced modifications of quantum criticality in neutral-atom platforms.

title: Optimal Logical Bell Measurements On Stabilizer Codes With Linear Optics
authors: Simon D. Reiß And Peter van Loock
abstract:
Author(s): Simon D. Reiß and Peter van Loock

Bell measurements (BMs) are ubiquitous in quantum information and technology. They are basic elements for quantum commmunication, computation, and error correction. In particular, when performed on logical qubits encoded in physical photonic qubits, they allow for a read-out of stabilizer syndrome i…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032421] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes optimal schemes for performing logical Bell measurements on stabilizer codes using linear optics.
motivation: Bell measurements are essential for quantum communication, computation, and error correction, but implementing them on encoded logical qubits with linear optics is challenging due to photon loss and nondeterministic operations.
method: The authors develop linear-optical circuits that achieve optimal logical Bell measurements on stabilizer codes, leveraging stabilizer formalism and resource-efficient optical elements.
result: They identify optimal configurations and show how logical Bell measurements enable stabilizer syndrome readout and other logical operations on photonic qubits.
conclusion: These results provide practical tools for photonic quantum information processing and fault-tolerant quantum error correction.

title: Microscopic Quantum Electrodynamics Origin Of Spin Entanglement
authors: M. Zarei
abstract:
Author(s): M. Zarei

We study effective spin interactions arising from quantum electrodynamics scattering between localized fermionic spins. By integrating out photon and mediator fields, the dynamics reduce to an effective spin Hamiltonian. For two qubits in the nonrelativistic regime, the resulting interaction takes a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032204] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives an effective spin Hamiltonian from QED scattering to reveal the microscopic origin of spin entanglement between localized fermionic spins.
motivation: To understand the fundamental quantum electrodynamical origin of effective spin interactions and entanglement between localized spins, bridging QED and quantum information.
method: Integrating out photon and mediator fields to obtain an effective spin Hamiltonian, then analyzing the resulting two-qubit interaction in the nonrelativistic regime.
result: The effective interaction yields a specific spin Hamiltonian that generates entanglement between two qubits, with parameters determined by QED scattering amplitudes.
