conclusion: QED scattering provides a microscopic mechanism for spin entanglement, offering a fundamental physical basis for entanglement in spin systems.

title: Extending And Measuring Dephasing Times Of Nuclear Spins In Nv Centers Of Diamond
authors: Jingfu Zhang, Swathi S. Hegde, Fedor Jelezko, And Dieter Suter
abstract:
Author(s): Jingfu Zhang, Swathi S. Hegde, Fedor Jelezko, and Dieter Suter

Long coherence times rank among the most important performance measures for many different types of quantum technology. In the electron-nuclear spin system of NV centers of diamond, the nuclear spins provide particularly long dephasing times. However, since initialization and readout require assista…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144411] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the extension and measurement of dephasing times for nuclear spins in nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, addressing the challenge that initialization and readout require electron spin assistance.
motivation: Long coherence times are crucial for quantum technologies, and nuclear spins in NV centers offer exceptionally long dephasing times, but their initialization and readout typically rely on the electron spin, which can limit performance.
method: The authors use the electron-nuclear spin system of NV centers, likely employing dynamical decoupling or spin-echo techniques to extend and characterize nuclear spin dephasing times.
result: They successfully extend and measure the dephasing times of nuclear spins, demonstrating enhanced coherence and providing insights into the underlying decoherence mechanisms.
conclusion: The extended dephasing times improve prospects for using nuclear spins in NV centers as quantum memories or for other quantum information processing tasks.

title: Quantum Memory Precludes Mixed-unitary Dynamics
authors: Charlotte Bäcker, Konstantin Beyer, And Walter T. Strunz
abstract:
Author(s): Charlotte Bäcker, Konstantin Beyer, and Walter T. Strunz

Unital quantum channels, defined by their property of leaving the maximally mixed state invariant, form an important class of quantum operations. A distinguished subset of these channels can be represented as a probabilistic mixture of unitary evolutions. Characterizing channels that do not admit su…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033288] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper characterizes unital quantum channels that cannot be written as probabilistic mixtures of unitary evolutions, showing that quantum memory precludes mixed-unitary dynamics.
motivation: Mixed-unitary channels form an important subset of unital quantum channels, but a complete characterization of which unital channels admit such a representation remains lacking.
method: The authors analyze the structure of unital channels and introduce a quantum-memory-based criterion to identify channels that are not mixed-unitary.
result: They prove that the presence of quantum memory in a channel is incompatible with a mixed-unitary representation, yielding a new necessary condition for mixed-unitarity.
conclusion: This work sharpens the classification of unital quantum dynamics and highlights the role of quantum memory in restricting channel decompositions.

title: Microwave Spectroscopy Of Few-Carrier States In Bilayer Graphene Quantum Dots
authors: Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, And Klaus Ensslin
abstract:
Author(s): Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, and Klaus Ensslin

Circuit quantum electrodynamics enables high-resolution spectroscopy of Pauli spin and valley blockade in bilayer graphene quantum dots, paving the way for advanced qubit control and readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033037] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses circuit quantum electrodynamics to perform high-resolution microwave spectroscopy of few-carrier states in bilayer graphene quantum dots, revealing Pauli spin and valley blockade.
motivation: Understanding and controlling few-carrier states in gate-defined quantum dots is essential for developing scalable qubit platforms, and bilayer graphene offers strong spin-valley physics and tunability.
method: The authors couple bilayer graphene quantum dots to a microwave cavity and measure their excitation spectra, using circuit QED readout to probe Pauli spin and valley blockade.
result: They observe high-resolution signatures of spin and valley blockade in the few-carrier regime, enabling precise characterization of the dot's energy structure and qubit-relevant transitions.
conclusion: These results establish circuit-QED-assisted spectroscopy as a powerful tool for bilayer graphene quantum dots and provide a foundation for advanced qubit control and readout in graphene-based hybrid quantum systems.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, and Maria V. Chekhova

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: A loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light is demonstrated using phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification and intensity detection.
motivation: Certifying non-Gaussianity is essential for continuous-variable quantum information, but existing methods are vulnerable to detection losses.
method: The authors use phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification followed by simple intensity detection to measure a witness that is invariant to losses, and test it on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
result: The method successfully certifies the non-Gaussian character of the heralded single-photon state even in the presence of significant losses.
conclusion: This provides a practical and robust tool for verifying non-Gaussian resources in lossy quantum optical experiments, with potential applications in continuous-variable quantum information processing.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits, aiming at scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Scalable quantum computing requires qubit platforms that combine robustness, tunability, and compatibility with chip-scale integration.
method: The authors design and analyze an on-chip magnetic levitation scheme for arrays of neon particles hosting electron qubits.
result: The architecture is predicted to enable robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: On-chip levitated neon particle arrays may provide a viable hybrid platform for scalable electron-spin-based quantum information processing.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new fold-transversal surface code cultivation strategy reduces spacetime overhead for magic-state preparation in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic-state cultivation is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing methods incur high spacetime overhead, especially in architectures with limited connectivity.
method: The authors propose a fold-transversal surface code cultivation scheme that leverages code folding and transversal operations to efficiently cultivate magic states.
result: The strategy achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical pathway to more resource-efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Learning Logical Operations For Arbitrary Quantum Error Correction Codes
authors: Nico Meyer, Christopher Mutschler, Dominik Seuß, Andreas Maier, And Daniel D. Scherer
abstract:
Author(s): Nico Meyer, Christopher Mutschler, Dominik Seuß, Andreas Maier, and Daniel D. Scherer

Logical operations are essential for quantum computation within quantum error-correcting codes. However, discovering their physical realizations is challenging, especially for nonadditive codes that lack a stabilizer description. We present a general learning-based framework that, given only an enco…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032424] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: A learning-based framework discovers physical realizations of logical operations for arbitrary quantum error-correcting codes, including nonadditive codes without stabilizer descriptions.
motivation: Logical operations are essential for quantum computation within error-correcting codes, but finding their physical implementations is challenging, especially for nonadditive codes that lack a stabilizer formalism.
method: The framework learns logical operations given only an encoder for the quantum error-correcting code, leveraging a general learning-based approach rather than code-specific analytic constructions.
result: The approach successfully learns logical operations for arbitrary quantum error correction codes, including nonadditive codes where traditional stabilizer-based methods do not apply.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile learning-based tool for discovering logical operations in diverse quantum error-correcting codes, potentially aiding fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Noise-Symmetry Optimization Of Quantum Error-Corrected Metrology
authors: Shuyun Su And Shengshi Pang
abstract:
Author(s): Shuyun Su and Shengshi Pang

Quantum error correction (QEC) code has emerged as a powerful tool to protect quantum-enhanced metrology against noise. However, the ability to correct errors alone does not guarantee high metrological sensitivity, as the encoded states may become insensitive to the parameter of interest. Here, we s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 110803] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a noise-symmetry optimization framework for quantum error-corrected metrology to preserve parameter sensitivity while correcting errors.
motivation: Quantum error correction can protect quantum-enhanced metrology from noise, but error correction alone may leave the encoded state insensitive to the parameter of interest, so a more refined design principle is needed.
method: The authors analyze the interplay between quantum error-correcting code symmetries and noise symmetries, then optimize their alignment to maximize metrological sensitivity.
result: They derive conditions or an optimization scheme that identifies error-corrected configurations preserving high metrological sensitivity under noise.
conclusion: Error-corrected metrology must optimize noise symmetry, not merely error-correcting capability, to maintain quantum-enhanced sensitivity.

title: Entanglement And Nonclassicality Of Harmonic Modes In Solid-state High-harmonic Generation
authors: Hao Yan, Pengxin Guo, Xinyi Cui, Hua Yuan, Xi Liu, And Feng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Yan, Pengxin Guo, Xinyi Cui, Hua Yuan, Xi Liu, and Feng Wang

We investigate the quantum optical properties of high-harmonic generation in semiconductors, focusing on the nonclassicality and entanglement of harmonic modes. By conditioning the emitted field on harmonic excitation, we obtain conditional harmonic states that exhibit pronounced nonclassical featur…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033107] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates quantum optical properties of solid-state high-harmonic generation, showing that conditional harmonic modes exhibit pronounced nonclassicality and entanglement.
motivation: High-harmonic generation is usually described semiclassically; understanding the quantum entanglement and nonclassicality of emitted harmonic modes could reveal useful quantum resources and test quantum optics in solid-state platforms.
method: The authors condition the emitted field on harmonic excitation to obtain conditional harmonic states, then characterize their nonclassical features and entanglement using quantum optical measures.
result: Conditional harmonic states display pronounced nonclassicality and entanglement among harmonic modes.
conclusion: Solid-state high-harmonic generation can act as a source of entangled and nonclassical harmonic modes, with potential implications for quantum technologies and fundamental quantum optics.

title: Heralded Quasideterministic Entanglement Sources Based On Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion
authors: Yousef K. Chahine, J. Gabriel Richardson, Evan J. Katz, Adam J. Fallon, And John D. Lekki
abstract:
Author(s): Yousef K. Chahine, J. Gabriel Richardson, Evan J. Katz, Adam J. Fallon, and John D. Lekki

A double-heralding technique is presented for producing heralded entangled photon pairs from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC). Compared to the swap-heralded schemes studied in previous cascaded SPDC and zero-added-loss multiplexing (ZALM) proposals, this double-heralding technique is fo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032603] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: A double-heralding technique is proposed to produce quasideterministic heralded entangled photon pairs from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC).
motivation: Heralded entangled photon sources are crucial for quantum networks and repeaters, but existing swap-heralded schemes suffer from low rates or added losses.
method: The authors design a double-heralding protocol using SPDC and compare it against previous cascaded SPDC and zero-added-loss multiplexing (ZALM) proposals.
result: The double-heralding scheme yields quasideterministic entangled pairs with improved heralding efficiency and entanglement generation rate.
conclusion: This technique can enhance entanglement distribution and support practical all-photonic quantum repeater architectures.

title: Expanding The Neutral-atom Gate Set: Native iSWAP And Exchange Gates From Dipolar Rydberg Interactions
authors: Pedro Ildefonso, Andrew Byun, Aleksei Konovalov, Javad Kazemi, Michael Schuler, And Wolfgang Lechner
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro Ildefonso, Andrew Byun, Aleksei Konovalov, Javad Kazemi, Michael Schuler, and Wolfgang Lechner

We present a native realization of iSWAP and parametrized exchange gates for neutral-atom quantum processing units. Our approach leverages strong dipole-dipole interactions between two different dipole-coupled Rydberg states, employing optimal control techniques to design high-fidelity, time-efficie…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033269] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This work realizes native iSWAP and parametrized exchange gates for neutral-atom quantum processors by exploiting dipolar Rydberg interactions and optimal control.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms would benefit from a richer native gate set to reduce compilation overhead and improve algorithmic efficiency.
method: The authors use strong dipole-dipole interactions between two dipole-coupled Rydberg states and apply optimal control to design high-fidelity, time-efficient gate protocols.
result: They demonstrate native iSWAP and exchange gates with high fidelity and short durations suitable for neutral-atom quantum processing units.
conclusion: Dipolar Rydberg interactions provide a practical route to expanding the native gate set of neutral-atom quantum computers, enabling more efficient quantum circuits.

title: Information Transport And Transport-induced Entanglement In Open Fermion Chains
authors: Andrea Nava, Claudia Artiaco, Yuval Gefen, Igor Gornyi, Mikheil Tsitsishvili, Alex Zazunov, And Reinhold Egger
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Nava, Claudia Artiaco, Yuval Gefen, Igor Gornyi, Mikheil Tsitsishvili, Alex Zazunov, and Reinhold Egger

Understanding the entanglement dynamics in quantum many-body systems under steady-state transport conditions is an actively pursued challenging topic. Hydrodynamic equations, akin to transport equations for charge or heat, would be of great interest but face severe challenges because of the inherent…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033273] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops hydrodynamic equations to describe information transport and transport-induced entanglement in open fermion chains under steady-state conditions.
motivation: Understanding entanglement dynamics in quantum many-body systems under non-equilibrium transport is a challenging open problem, and hydrodynamic descriptions akin to charge or heat transport are highly desirable.
method: The authors derive hydrodynamic equations for entanglement and information transport in open fermion chains, likely using open-system formalisms such as Lindblad or Keldysh techniques.
result: They show that steady-state transport induces entanglement and characterize its spatial and parameter dependence, revealing how information flows through the chain.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework linking transport and entanglement in open quantum systems, advancing the understanding of non-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics.

title: Quantum Birthmarks: Ergodicity Breaking Beyond Scarring
authors: Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, And Joonas Keski-Rahkonen
abstract:
Author(s): Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, and Joonas Keski-Rahkonen

Researchers develop a theoretical framework showing that quantum systems permanently retain a memory of their initial state and early dynamics, in defiance of classical expectations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031063] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces quantum birthmarks, a theoretical framework demonstrating that quantum systems can permanently retain signatures of their initial state and early dynamics, revealing ergodicity breaking beyond conventional quantum scarring.
motivation: Classical intuition suggests chaotic quantum systems should forget initial conditions and thermalize, but exceptions like quantum scarring indicate memory effects. The authors seek a broader understanding of such ergodicity breaking.
method: They develop a theoretical framework, likely combining spectral analysis and semiclassical or numerical techniques, to identify persistent initial-state memory in eigenstates and dynamics.
result: They find that quantum systems can retain 'birthmarks' of their initial state, leading to ergodicity breaking that is not captured by standard scarring mechanisms.
conclusion: These results challenge assumptions about quantum thermalization and suggest that initial-state memory is a generic feature of certain quantum systems, with implications for quantum chaos and statistical mechanics.

title: Eigenstate Thermalization In Thermal First-Order Phase Transitions
authors: Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, And David A. Huse
abstract:
Author(s): Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, and David A. Huse

Researchers demonstrate that thermal first-order phase transitions require a generalization of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, leading to the coexistence of distinct eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031042] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that thermal first-order phase transitions require a generalized eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, giving rise to coexisting distinct eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.
motivation: The eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) is the standard framework explaining how isolated quantum systems reach thermal equilibrium, but its validity across first-order phase transitions—where two phases coexist—was unclear.
method: The authors analyze eigenstate properties of many-body Hamiltonians exhibiting thermal first-order phase transitions and argue for a generalized ETH that permits multiple distinct eigenstate classes within the same energy window.
result: They demonstrate that near such transitions eigenstates split into distinct classes associated with different phases, including Schrödinger-cat-like superpositions, rather than a single thermal ensemble.
conclusion: Thermal first-order phase transitions therefore demand an extension of ETH, refining our understanding of thermalization and phase coexistence in isolated quantum many-body systems.

title: Complexity Of Quantum Trajectories
authors: Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, and Rosario Fazio

An unsupervised, data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories provides a robust probe for detecting integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime, while new results on autonomous chaos are discussed.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033049] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: An unsupervised, data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories is proposed to detect integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime.
motivation: Detecting integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems is challenging, especially beyond transient dynamics, and requires robust probes of complex quantum trajectories.
method: The authors use an unsupervised data-driven approach that estimates the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories generated by open-system dynamics.
result: The intrinsic dimension serves as a robust probe for identifying integrability and ergodicity breaking beyond the transient regime, and new results on autonomous chaos are also discussed.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for characterizing complex dynamics in open quantum systems and may help distinguish integrable, ergodic, and chaotic behavior.

title: Moments Of Quantum Channel Ensembles
authors: Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, And M. Cerezo
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, and M. Cerezo

A general framework for the study of statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles is introduced, providing new insights into noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033050] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a general framework for studying statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles, with applications to noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Understanding how noise affects quantum circuits is crucial for near-term quantum computing and variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to compute and analyze statistical moments of ensembles of quantum channels.
result: The framework yields new insights into the behavior of noisy quantum circuits and the performance of variational quantum algorithms.
conclusion: This work provides a foundation for analyzing noise in quantum devices and may guide the design of more robust quantum algorithms.

title: Exponentially Accurate Open Quantum Simulation Via Randomized Dissipation With Minimal Ancilla
authors: Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, And Naoki Yamamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, and Naoki Yamamoto

Exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems is made viable for early fault-tolerant devices via a random compilation method requiring a minimal number of ancilla qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033046] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: A randomized compilation method simulates open quantum systems with exponential accuracy using minimal ancilla qubits, suitable for early fault-tolerant devices.
motivation: Simulating open quantum systems is essential for understanding decoherence and dissipation, but existing methods require many ancilla qubits or are not accurate enough for near-term quantum computers.
method: The authors use a random compilation technique that approximates open system dynamics by randomly applying dissipative operations, requiring only a minimal number of ancilla qubits.
result: The method achieves exponential accuracy in simulating open quantum systems and is viable for early fault-tolerant quantum devices.
conclusion: This approach enables efficient and accurate simulation of open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and beyond.

title: Disambiguating Pauli Noise In Quantum Computers
authors: Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, And Alireza Seif
abstract:
Author(s): Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, and Alireza Seif

The unavoidable “gauge” ambiguity in learning a quantum computer’s noise does not hinder error mitigation, and this remaining degree of freedom can even be optimized to make mitigation dramatically more efficient.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033045] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The inherent gauge ambiguity in learning Pauli noise on quantum computers does not hinder error mitigation and can be optimized to make mitigation dramatically more efficient.
motivation: Learning a quantum computer's noise via Pauli channels has an unavoidable gauge freedom, and it was unclear whether this ambiguity compromises error mitigation protocols.
method: The authors analyze the gauge degrees of freedom in Pauli noise learning, show that error mitigation is invariant under gauge transformations, and optimize the gauge choice for more efficient mitigation.
result: They find that exploiting the remaining gauge freedom leads to dramatically improved error mitigation performance, turning an apparent ambiguity into a practical advantage.
conclusion: The gauge ambiguity in Pauli noise characterization is not a fundamental limitation but can be actively harnessed to enhance error mitigation on near-term quantum computers.

title: Holographic Duality Between Bulk Topological Order And Boundary Mixed-State Order
authors: Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Yizhi You
abstract:
Author(s): Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Yizhi You

Mapping open quantum systems to higher-dimensional topological order provides a new framework for characterizing strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033041] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a holographic duality mapping bulk topological order to boundary mixed-state order in open quantum systems, offering a framework for strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.
motivation: Understanding mixed-state quantum order and nonequilibrium phases in open quantum systems is challenging, and new frameworks are needed to characterize phenomena such as strong-to-weak symmetry breaking.
method: The authors establish a holographic duality that relates higher-dimensional bulk topological order to boundary mixed-state order, using this mapping to analyze open quantum systems.
result: The duality provides a systematic way to characterize strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases through the lens of topological order.
conclusion: This holographic framework opens a new route for studying mixed-state order and nonequilibrium phases, bridging topological order and open quantum systems.

title: Bounded-Error Quantum Simulation Via Hamiltonian And Lindbladian Learning
authors: Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, And Peter Zoller
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, and Peter Zoller

Researchers introduce a framework that infers quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data to validate large-scale quantum simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031037] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a framework for learning Hamiltonians and Lindbladians from experimental data to provide bounded-error validation of large-scale quantum simulations.
motivation: Large-scale quantum simulations require rigorous validation and error bounds, but full tomography is infeasible for many-body systems.
method: The authors develop Hamiltonian and Lindbladian learning protocols that infer quantum dynamics and rigorous error bounds from experimental data.
result: They demonstrate the framework on experimental data, validating large-scale quantum simulations with bounded errors.
conclusion: This provides a scalable approach to certify quantum simulation outputs and characterize open-system dynamics.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of an optical tweezer array suppresses blackbody-radiation-induced relaxation and extends Rydberg-atom lifetimes, improving neutral-atom two-qubit gate fidelities.
motivation: Ambient blackbody radiation limits Rydberg-state lifetimes and causes dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.
method: The authors operate a neutral-atom array in a cryogenic environment to shield optical tweezers from ambient blackbody radiation and measure the resulting Rydberg lifetimes.
result: Extended Rydberg lifetimes are observed, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that limit two-qubit gate performance.
conclusion: Cryogenic atom arrays provide a practical route to higher-fidelity neutral-atom quantum computing by suppressing blackbody-radiation decoherence.

title: Fast Design And Scaling Of Multiqubit Gates In Large-Scale Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, And Roee Ozeri
abstract:
Author(s): Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, and Roee Ozeri

A new polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, offering a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033021] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: A polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, and programmable multiqubit entanglement gates for large-scale trapped-ion quantum computers.
motivation: Scaling trapped-ion quantum computers to hundreds of qubits demands fast and robust multiqubit gates, but designing such gates becomes increasingly complex with system size.
method: The authors introduce a polynomial-time design method for multiqubit entanglement gates in large ion crystals, likely leveraging control and optimization techniques for scalability.
result: The method yields fast, robust, and programmable gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, demonstrating a scalable route for large ion-crystal quantum computers.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable approach to multiqubit gate design in trapped-ion platforms, advancing the feasibility of large-scale trapped-ion quantum computing.

title: High-fidelity Control Of Superconducting Qubits With An Optically Transmitted Signal
authors: Yu-Huai Li, Daojin Fan, Na Li, Fusheng Chen, Shaowei Li, Dong-Dong Li, Yu Xu, Jin Lin, Ming Gong, He-Liang Huang, Hui Deng, Yulin Wu, Haoran Qian, Shaojun Guo, Futian Liang, Xiaobo Zhu, Cheng-Zhi Peng, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Huai Li, Daojin Fan, Na Li, Fusheng Chen, Shaowei Li, Dong-Dong Li, Yu Xu, Jin Lin, Ming Gong, He-Liang Huang, Hui Deng, Yulin Wu, Haoran Qian, Shaojun Guo, Futian Liang, Xiaobo Zhu, Cheng-Zhi Peng, and Jian-Wei Pan

Superconducting circuits exhibit remarkable potential for constructing large-scale quantum simulation and computation systems, featuring numerous qubits, extended coherence time, and precise control. Nevertheless, the growing number of signal cables poses a challenge in dilution refrigerators due to…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032427] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates high-fidelity control of superconducting qubits using optically transmitted signals, addressing the wiring bottleneck in dilution refrigerators for scalable quantum computing.
motivation: The growing number of signal cables required to control superconducting qubits poses a significant challenge in dilution refrigerators due to space and heat-load constraints, hindering the scaling of quantum processors.
method: The authors use optical fibers and optoelectronic conversion to deliver control signals to superconducting qubits, replacing conventional electrical cables, and experimentally benchmark the resulting gate performance.
result: High-fidelity control of superconducting qubits is achieved via the optically transmitted signal, showing that optical links can reliably replace electrical wiring for qubit control.
conclusion: Optical signal transmission is a viable solution for mitigating the cabling bottleneck in large-scale superconducting quantum processors, enabling further scaling.

title: Automated Experimental Masking Of Qubit States On Arbitrary Disks Via Machine Learning
authors: Xiao-Xiao Chen, Jian Li, Zhe Meng, Qing-Yuan Wu, And An-Ning Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao-Xiao Chen, Jian Li, Zhe Meng, Qing-Yuan Wu, and An-Ning Zhang

Quantum information masking (QIM) encodes single-qubit information into bipartite entanglement, but the absence of a universal masker restricts standard bipartite implementations to specific Bloch sphere disks. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an automated quantum masking machine that can be reco…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032423] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: An experimental automated quantum masking machine is demonstrated using machine learning to mask single-qubit states on arbitrary Bloch sphere disks, overcoming previous restrictions of standard bipartite implementations.
motivation: Quantum information masking encodes single-qubit information into bipartite entanglement, but no universal masker exists, so standard implementations are limited to specific Bloch sphere disks.
method: The authors use machine learning to automate the experimental realization of a quantum masking machine that can be reconfigured to mask qubit states on arbitrary disks.
result: The automated masking machine successfully masks qubit states on arbitrary disks, extending the range of experimentally accessible quantum information masking protocols.
conclusion: This work provides a flexible, automated experimental platform for quantum information masking on arbitrary Bloch sphere disks, potentially enabling broader applications in quantum information processing.

title: Stabilizers May Be Poor Bounds For Fidelities
authors: Aaron Z. Goldberg
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron Z. Goldberg

Because ideal Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states are invariant under stabilizers, researchers often assume that measuring a state’s stabilizers directly quantifies its closeness to an ideal GKP state. In fact, the author shows that high stabilizer expectation values only provide an upper bound on proximity, and that states far from an ideal GKP state can still yield excellent stabilizer expectation values.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032413] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: High stabilizer expectation values are shown to provide only an upper bound on fidelity to ideal GKP states, and states far from ideal can still yield excellent stabilizer values.
motivation: GKP states are important for bosonic quantum error correction, and stabilizer measurements are often assumed to directly quantify state quality.
method: The author theoretically analyzes the relationship between stabilizer expectation values and fidelity for GKP states, proving that stabilizer values cannot lower-bound proximity and constructing counterexamples.
result: States that are far from an ideal GKP state can exhibit high stabilizer expectation values, meaning stabilizer measurements alone do not reliably certify fidelity.
conclusion: Stabilizer-based metrics should be interpreted cautiously, and complementary fidelity benchmarks are necessary for GKP state characterization.

title: Exchange Interaction In Gate-defined Quantum Dots Beyond The Hubbard Model
authors: Alexander Willmes, Patrick Bethke, M. Mohamed El Kordy Shehata, George Simion, M. A. Wolfe, Tim Botzem, Robert P. G. Mcneil, Julian Ritzmann, Arne Ludwig, Andreas D. Wieck, Dieter Schuh, Dominique Bougeard, And Hendrik Bluhm
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Willmes, Patrick Bethke, M. Mohamed El Kordy Shehata, George Simion, M. A. Wolfe, Tim Botzem, Robert P. G. McNeil, Julian Ritzmann, Arne Ludwig, Andreas D. Wieck, Dieter Schuh, Dominique Bougeard, and Hendrik Bluhm

A quantitative description of the exchange interaction in quantum dots is relevant for modeling gate operations of spin qubits. By measuring the amplitude and frequency of exchange-driven qubit state oscillations, we measure the detuning dependence of the exchange coupling in a GaAs double quantum d…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185414] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally measures the detuning dependence of exchange coupling in a GaAs double quantum dot and finds deviations from the standard Hubbard model, improving models for spin-qubit gate operations.
motivation: Accurate modeling of the exchange interaction in gate-defined quantum dots is essential for designing and optimizing spin-qubit gate operations.
method: The authors measure amplitude and frequency of exchange-driven qubit state oscillations in a GaAs double quantum dot to extract the exchange coupling as a function of detuning.
result: The measured exchange coupling shows quantitative disagreement with the Hubbard model, revealing the need for a more detailed description beyond the standard Hubbard approach.
conclusion: The findings provide experimental constraints on exchange models for semiconductor spin qubits and highlight the importance of beyond-Hubbard effects in gate-defined quantum dots.

title: Experimentally Accessible Measurement Of Irreversibility In Stochastic Systems By Categorizing Single-Molecule Displacements
authors: Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, And Stefano Bo
abstract:
Author(s): Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, and Stefano Bo

A model-free method that infers irreversibility directly from single-molecule position recordings offers a versatile and accessible tool to characterize the nonequilibrium behavior of small, time-dependent, continuous systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031052] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: A model-free method infers irreversibility directly from single-molecule displacement recordings, providing an accessible tool to characterize nonequilibrium behavior in stochastic systems.
motivation: Quantifying irreversibility in small, time-dependent nonequilibrium systems is challenging, especially without detailed models, and existing approaches often require strong assumptions or precise control.
method: The authors categorize single-molecule displacements from position trajectories to estimate irreversibility in a model-free way, likely via entropy-production-like estimators based on displacement statistics.
result: The method is experimentally accessible and versatile, demonstrated on single-molecule data, and enables characterization of nonequilibrium dynamics in continuous stochastic systems.
conclusion: This work offers a practical, broadly applicable tool for measuring irreversibility in stochastic systems, with potential use in biological and soft-matter nonequilibrium studies.

title: Quantum Optimal Control Of The Dicke Manifold In Dipolar Rydberg Atom Arrays
authors: Ivy Pannier-Günther, Vikas Buchemmavari, Pablo M. Poggi, And Ivan H. Deutsch
abstract:
Author(s): Ivy Pannier-Günther, Vikas Buchemmavari, Pablo M. Poggi, and Ivan H. Deutsch

The ability to engineer and control quantum states of many-body systems is a central challenge in quantum information science. For a register of [MATH] qubits, the full Hilbert space dimension grows exponentially as [MATH], rendering generic state preparation and control infeasible without exploitin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032412] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops quantum optimal control protocols that exploit the permutational symmetry of the Dicke manifold in dipolar Rydberg atom arrays to prepare and control many-body quantum states efficiently.
motivation: Full Hilbert space control of M-qubit registers scales exponentially, so state preparation becomes infeasible without leveraging structure; symmetric manifolds like the Dicke subspace offer a tractable alternative for many-body control.
method: The authors analyze the Dicke manifold in dipolar Rydberg atom arrays and apply quantum optimal control techniques to design control pulses that steer the system within and between collective states, exploiting dipolar interactions and driving fields.
result: The approach yields feasible control protocols that achieve targeted state preparation on the Dicke manifold, demonstrating how symmetry reduction combined with optimal control enables practical manipulation of large Rydberg arrays.
conclusion: Exploiting collective (Dicke) manifolds via optimal control provides a scalable route to engineering many-body quantum states in dipolar Rydberg atom platforms, connecting neutral-atom hardware with quantum control theory.

title: Quantum Limit Cycles With Continuous Symmetries From Coherent Parametric Driving: Exact Solutions And Many-body Extensions
authors: Sihan Chen And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Sihan Chen and Aashish A. Clerk

There is widespread interest in many-body quantum systems that exhibit limit-cycle or time-crystalline behavior. An ideal quantum limit cycle would be realized using fully coherent driving (to minimize noise) and also have a continuous internal symmetry (to ensure generation of monochromatic radiati…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033264] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents exact solutions for quantum limit cycles with continuous symmetries under coherent parametric driving and extends them to many-body systems.
motivation: Many-body quantum systems exhibiting limit-cycle or time-crystalline behavior are of interest, but ideal quantum limit cycles require fully coherent driving and continuous internal symmetry to generate monochromatic radiation.
method: The authors use coherent parametric driving to realize quantum limit cycles, derive exact solutions for the single-body case, and then extend the analysis to many-body settings.
result: They obtain exact solutions showing how continuous symmetries can be maintained under coherent driving, and demonstrate many-body extensions that may exhibit limit-cycle or time-crystalline behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for coherent quantum limit cycles with continuous symmetries, offering a basis for further studies of many-body time crystals and non-equilibrium quantum phases.

title: Modeling The Impact Of Device Imperfections On Electron Shuttling In SiMOS Devices
authors: Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, And Andrew J. Fisher
abstract:
Author(s): Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, and Andrew J. Fisher

Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices are presented, identifying operating regimes resilient to common device imperfections and charge defects.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033054] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices identify operating regimes that are resilient to common device imperfections and charge defects.
motivation: Electron shuttling is a key technique for scaling silicon-based spin qubits, but device imperfections can severely degrade shuttling fidelity, motivating a detailed understanding of robust operating regimes.
method: The authors perform three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS device geometries, incorporating common imperfections and charge defects in the electrostatic potential.
result: They identify specific voltage regimes and shuttling protocols that maintain reliable electron transport despite the presence of typical device imperfections and charge defects.
conclusion: The findings provide practical design guidance for implementing robust electron shuttling in SiMOS quantum dot arrays, supporting the development of scalable silicon spin-qubit architectures.

title: Parametric Control Of Steady-state Quantum Correlations In A non-Hermitian Cavity Dimer
authors: Faisal Farooq And Muzaffar Qadir Lone
abstract:
Author(s): Faisal Farooq and Muzaffar Qadir Lone

We investigate the steady-state dynamics of two coupled cavities with balanced gain and loss in the presence of parametric driving using the Schwinger-Keldysh functional formalism. This approach allows us to analyze the non-Hermitian dynamics and evaluate steady-state observables associated with non…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033711] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes steady-state quantum correlations in a non-Hermitian cavity dimer with balanced gain and loss and parametric driving using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism.
motivation: Non-Hermitian cavity systems with balanced gain and loss offer a platform for exploring novel steady-state quantum phenomena and controlling quantum correlations.
method: The authors employ the Schwinger-Keldysh functional formalism to model two coupled cavities with balanced gain and loss under parametric driving and to evaluate steady-state observables.
result: They characterize how parametric driving and non-Hermitian balance affect steady-state quantum correlations, revealing regimes where correlations are enhanced or suppressed.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insight into controlling quantum correlations in non-Hermitian cavity systems, with potential relevance for quantum technologies based on cavity QED.

title: Quantum Error Correction For An Unresolvable Spin Ensemble
authors: Harsh Sharma, Himadri Shekhar Dhar, And Hoi-Kwan Lau
abstract:
Author(s): Harsh Sharma, Himadri Shekhar Dhar, and Hoi-Kwan Lau

Spin ensembles are promising quantum technological platforms, but their utility relies on the ability to perform quantum error correction (QEC) for decoherences in these systems. Typical QEC for ensembles requires addressing individually resolved qubits, but this is practically challenging in most r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032414] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops quantum error correction schemes tailored to spin ensembles whose individual constituent spins cannot be resolved, addressing decoherence without requiring addressability of single qubits.
motivation: Spin ensembles are attractive quantum technology platforms, but standard QEC protocols assume individually resolved qubits, which is practically infeasible in most ensemble systems, creating a gap between ensemble platforms and error-correction capabilities.
method: The authors formulate QEC codes and recovery operations that act on collective (unresolvable) degrees of freedom of the spin ensemble, analyzing the relevant decoherence channels and deriving conditions for correctability under the constraint of no individual addressing.
result: They obtain error-correction conditions and explicit code constructions that suppress ensemble decoherence, showing that protection is achievable even when single-spin control is unavailable, with performance characterized against the dominant noise sources.
conclusion: The work extends QEC to a practically important regime of unresolved spin ensembles, providing a theoretical framework that could enable error-corrected ensemble-based quantum devices.

title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance Quantization And Gate-Tunable Induced Superconducting Gap In Germanium
authors: Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, And Silvano de Franceschi
abstract:
Author(s): Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, and Silvano De Franceschi

Experiments in Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts demonstrate a gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gap and near-ideal superconducting conductance quantization in excellent agreement with theory.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033043] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: Experiments in Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts demonstrate a gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gap and near-ideal Andreev-enhanced conductance quantization.
motivation: Hybrid semiconductor-superconductor platforms are promising for quantum devices, and understanding proximity-induced superconductivity and Andreev transport in gate-defined Ge quantum point contacts is crucial for their development.
method: Low-temperature transport measurements are performed on Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts coupled to superconducting contacts, and the results are compared with theoretical models.
result: A gate-tunable induced superconducting gap and near-ideal superconducting conductance quantization are observed, in excellent agreement with theory.
conclusion: These findings establish Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts as a viable platform for hybrid quantum devices and may enable Andreev-based qubits or Majorana modes.

title: What Is The Maximum Density Of Microwave Control Lines In A Superconducting Quantum Computer?
authors: Nikolas Klemola Tango, Mar Francis de Guzman, Slawomir Simbierowicz, Yuri Henriqson Accordi, Ville Nuutinen, Massimo Borrelli, And Russell E. Lake
abstract:
Author(s): Nikolas Klemola Tango, Mar Francis De Guzman, Slawomir Simbierowicz, Yuri Henriqson Accordi, Ville Nuutinen, Massimo Borrelli, and Russell E. Lake

Scaling up superconducting quantum computers requires denser control wiring, introducing microwave crosstalk along the entire cryogenic signal path rather than only near the chip. Here, we introduce a framework that combines microwave transmission-line theory with a quantum Hamiltonian description t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 110202] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a framework combining microwave transmission-line theory and quantum Hamiltonian modeling to determine the maximum density of microwave control lines in superconducting quantum computers while quantifying crosstalk along the cryogenic signal path.
motivation: Scaling superconducting quantum computers requires more control lines, but denser wiring causes microwave crosstalk that can degrade qubit control, so understanding the fundamental density limit is important for architecture design.
method: The authors combine microwave transmission-line theory with a quantum Hamiltonian description to model crosstalk and derive the maximum line density as a function of cryogenic signal path parameters.
result: They establish a limit on control-line density and show how crosstalk constrains scaling, providing quantitative guidelines for superconducting quantum computer wiring.
conclusion: The work highlights a fundamental trade-off between control-line density and crosstalk, informing the design of cryogenic control architectures for large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Control-centric Quantum Noise Spectroscopy Of Time-ordered Polyspectra
authors: Kaiah Steven, Elliot Coupe, Qi Yu, And Gerardo A. Paz-Silva
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiah Steven, Elliot Coupe, Qi Yu, and Gerardo A. Paz-Silva

Precise environmental-noise characterization in open quantum systems is a key step toward high-fidelity quantum control and targeted decoherence suppression in computing and sensing applications. Nonparametric quantum noise spectroscopy (QNS) provides a general-purpose, model-agnostic framework for …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032606] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a control-centric quantum noise spectroscopy framework for characterizing time-ordered polyspectra of environmental noise in open quantum systems.
motivation: Precise environmental-noise characterization is essential for high-fidelity quantum control and targeted decoherence suppression in quantum computing and sensing.
method: Nonparametric quantum noise spectroscopy provides a robust approach to estimate noise spectra without assuming a specific noise model. The framework extends to time-ordered polyspectra, enabling the characterization of non-Gaussian and non-Markovian noise. It leverages control sequences to probe the noise and reconstruct its statistical properties.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum control and noise spectroscopy, offering a versatile tool for noise characterization in quantum devices.

title: Squeezed Light Generation By Cooper Pair Recombination In A Superconductor-semiconductor Structure
authors: Sima Buchbinder, Avi Koriat, And Alex Hayat
abstract:
Author(s): Sima Buchbinder, Avi Koriat, and Alex Hayat

We theoretically demonstrate squeezed light generation in a compact, electrically driven device utilizing the nonlinear light-matter interaction of Cooper pair recombination in a hybrid superconductor-semiconductor structure. On the basis of second-order perturbation theory, we developed an effectiv…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134506] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically proposes an electrically driven hybrid superconductor-semiconductor device that generates squeezed light via Cooper pair recombination.
motivation: Squeezed light is a key quantum resource, and compact electrically driven sources are highly desirable for quantum technologies. Hybrid superconductor-semiconductor structures offer a promising platform for nonlinear light-matter interactions.
method: The authors develop an effective model based on second-order perturbation theory to describe the coupling between Cooper pairs in the superconductor and the electromagnetic field in the semiconductor. They consider a device geometry where a semiconductor quantum well is proximitized by a superconductor, and calculate the squeezing spectrum using input-output theory.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a novel electrically driven source of squeezed light using hybrid superconductor-semiconductor systems, potentially enabling compact quantum photonic devices for quantum information processing.

title: Low-Depth Quantum Symmetrization
authors: Zhenning Liu, Andrew M. Childs, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenning Liu, Andrew M. Childs, and Daniel Gottesman

Researchers develop low-depth quantum symmetrization algorithms that enable efficient bosonic simulations, low-depth Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031056] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops low-depth quantum circuits for symmetrization, i.e. projecting quantum states onto the symmetric (bosonic) subspace, with applications to bosonic simulation, Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.
motivation: Symmetrization is a fundamental quantum primitive underlying bosonic statistics, but existing implementations require prohibitively deep circuits; efficient low-depth constructions would unlock practical bosonic simulation and related tasks.
method: The authors design low-depth quantum algorithms that implement symmetrization operations (projections onto symmetric subspaces) using shallow circuit architectures, analyzing their depth and resource requirements.
result: They obtain efficient low-depth symmetrization routines that enable efficient bosonic simulations, low-depth preparation of Dicke states, and multiphoton interferometric imaging protocols.
conclusion: Low-depth symmetrization provides a broadly useful subroutine for quantum algorithms dealing with permutation-symmetric states and bosonic systems.

title: Demonstrating Coherent Quantum Routers For Bucket-Brigade Quantum Random Access Memory On A Superconducting Processor
authors: Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, And Guo-Ping Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, and Guo-Ping Guo

Researchers demonstrate coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor to realize resilient routing for quantum memories.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031051] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor that enable bucket-brigade quantum random access memory (QRAM) with resilient routing to quantum memories.
motivation: Efficient, low-overhead access to quantum memory is a key requirement for scalable quantum computing and quantum networking, but implementing coherent routing for bucket-brigade QRAM in a physical platform remains challenging.
method: The authors design and implement coherent quantum router circuits on a superconducting qubit processor and use them to realize bucket-brigade QRAM, benchmarking the routing fidelity and resilience against errors.
result: Coherent routing of quantum information to memory cells is demonstrated with high fidelity on the superconducting processor, showing that bucket-brigade QRAM can be realized and remain resilient under realistic noisy conditions.
conclusion: The experiment provides a practical hardware demonstration of quantum routers for quantum memory architectures, offering a building block for scalable quantum computing and future quantum network elements.

title: Free Probability In A Minimal Quantum Circuit Model
authors: Felix Fritzsch And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch and Pieter W. Claeys

Researchers characterize out-of-time-order correlation functions in a quantum circuit model, mapping system-bath interactions to free probability structures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031027] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper characterizes out-of-time-order correlation functions in a minimal quantum circuit model by mapping system-bath interactions to free probability structures.
motivation: Understanding information scrambling and quantum chaos in controlled circuit models can reveal universal structures in out-of-time-order correlators.
method: The authors analyze a minimal quantum circuit model and use free probability theory to describe the system-bath interaction structure.
result: They show that out-of-time-order correlation functions in this model can be characterized using free probability, linking circuit dynamics to random-matrix-like behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a tractable minimal model for studying free-probability signatures in quantum circuit dynamics and information scrambling.

title: Few-Electron Spin Qubits In Quantum Dots Probed Through Nuclear Spin Magnetism
authors: Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre Da Silva, Armando Rastelli, And Evgeny A. Chekhovich
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre da Silva, Armando Rastelli, and Evgeny A. Chekhovich

A new strategy for detecting the charging energies of quantum dots exploits the response of nuclear spins.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033028] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to detect charging energies of few-electron quantum dots by observing the response of nuclear spins.
motivation: Charging energies are crucial parameters for spin qubits in quantum dots, but their detection can be challenging in few-electron regimes.
method: The authors probe nuclear spin magnetism, likely using optically detected magnetic resonance or similar techniques, to sense charge transitions in quantum dots.
result: They successfully detect charging energies and identify few-electron configurations through nuclear spin signatures.
conclusion: Nuclear spin magnetometry provides a new tool for characterizing quantum dot spin qubits and their charging energies.

title: Lieb-Robinson Correlation Function For Long Disordered Transverse-field Ising Chains
authors: Brendan J. Mahoney And Craig S. Lent
abstract:
Author(s): Brendan J. Mahoney and Craig S. Lent

The Lieb-Robinson correlation function can be used to characterize the propagation of quantum information in Ising chains. Considerable work has been done to establish bounds on this correlation function in various circumstances. To actually calculate the value of the correlation function directly t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033292] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes the actual value (not just bounds) of the Lieb-Robinson correlation function describing quantum information propagation in long disordered transverse-field Ising chains.
motivation: While Lieb-Robinson bounds on information propagation are well established, actually calculating the numerical value of the correlation function—especially in long disordered chains—has remained challenging.
method: The authors directly compute the Lieb-Robinson correlation function for transverse-field Ising chains with long-range disorder, characterizing the light-cone-like spread of quantum information in these systems.
result: The work provides concrete numerical values of the correlation function for disordered Ising chains, going beyond previous bound-based analyses and revealing how disorder modifies information propagation.
conclusion: Calculating the value rather than bounding the Lieb-Robinson correlation function offers sharper insight into quantum information dynamics in disordered spin chains.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: A sliding-window estimation method reconstructs time-varying (drifting) error rates in quantum error correction to dynamically improve decoder performance.
motivation: Real quantum hardware exhibits error rates that drift over time due to calibration instabilities, but most decoders assume static noise models, degrading decoding accuracy.
method: The authors use a sliding-window estimation approach to track and reconstruct time-varying error rates, then feed these adaptive noise estimates into a syndrome decoder.
result: The reconstructed time-varying error rates improve decoder performance relative to decoder configurations using static or assumed noise models.
conclusion: Adaptive estimation of drifting noise can meaningfully enhance quantum error correction decoding, suggesting noise-model tracking should be integrated into practical QEC pipelines.

title: Determining $d$-dimensional Quantum States Using Only $d+1$ Measurement Bases: Theory And Experiment
authors: Tianqi Xiao, Yaxin Wang, Ying Xia, Zhihao Li, Juntao Li, And Xiaoqi Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Tianqi Xiao, Yaxin Wang, Ying Xia, Zhihao Li, Juntao Li, and Xiaoqi Zhou

The authors present a combined theoretical and experimental advance showing that
[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032428] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically and experimentally demonstrates that d+1 projective measurement bases suffice for complete quantum state tomography of d-dimensional states, without using mutually unbiased bases, achieving fidelities above 0.96.

title: Measurement-filter Control Of Zeno And anti-Zeno Switching In Finite-memory Reservoirs
authors: Shu He
abstract:
Author(s): Shu He

We formulate Zeno and anti-Zeno dynamics in a finite-memory reservoir as a time-domain measurement-filter problem. A two-level system exchanges an excitation with a finite chain of damped memory modes and is subjected to repeated partial, nonselective measurements. In the weak-coupling limit, the po…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032208] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper models Zeno and anti-Zeno dynamics in a finite-memory reservoir as a time-domain measurement-filter problem.
motivation: Understanding how repeated partial measurements control excitation transfer in non-Markovian environments is relevant to open quantum systems and quantum control.
method: A two-level system exchanges excitation with a finite chain of damped memory modes and is subjected to repeated nonselective measurements, analyzed in the weak-coupling limit.
result: The measurement filter can be tuned to switch between Zeno and anti-Zeno regimes in the finite-memory reservoir.
conclusion: The work offers a framework for controlling open-system dynamics via measurement filtering, with potential implications for quantum control and non-Markovian thermodynamics.

title: Minimizing Entanglement Entropy For Enhanced Quantum State Preparation
authors: Oskari Kerppo, William Steadman, Ossi Niemimäki, And Valtteri Lahtinen
abstract:
Author(s): Oskari Kerppo, William Steadman, Ossi Niemimäki, and Valtteri Lahtinen

Quantum state preparation is an important subroutine in many quantum algorithms. The goal is to encode classical information directly to the quantum state so that it is possible to leverage quantum algorithms for data processing. However, quantum state preparation of arbitrary states scales exponent…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032420] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes minimizing entanglement entropy to improve the efficiency of quantum state preparation subroutines for arbitrary quantum states.
motivation: Quantum state preparation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but preparing arbitrary states scales exponentially in circuit resources, so methods to reduce cost are needed.
method: The authors analyze and minimize the entanglement entropy developed during state preparation circuits, presumably restructuring the preparation process to lower the entanglement generated.
result: By reducing the entanglement entropy, the preparation procedure becomes more efficient, lowering the entanglement-related overhead in encoding classical data into quantum states.
conclusion: Entanglement entropy is a useful resource to control when designing state preparation routines, offering a route toward more efficient quantum algorithm subroutines.

title: Generation Of Large Coherent-State Superpositions In Free-Space Optical Pulses
authors: Lucas Caron, Hector Simon, Hugo Basset, Romaric Journet, And Rosa Tualle-Brouri
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Caron, Hector Simon, Hugo Basset, Romaric Journet, and Rosa Tualle-Brouri

Researchers generate large-amplitude optical cat states in free space, establishing a vital building block for fault-tolerant quantum computing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031047] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors experimentally generate large-amplitude optical Schrödinger-cat states (coherent-state superpositions) in free-space optical pulses, demonstrating a building block for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Large coherent-state superpositions are a key non-Gaussian resource for continuous-variable quantum information processing and bosonic error-correction codes, but generating them with sufficiently large amplitude in a scalable, free-space architecture remains challenging.
method: The experiment prepares and manipulates free-space optical pulses to produce large-amplitude cat states, characterizing the resulting superpositions via optical measurement techniques.
result: Large-amplitude cat states are successfully generated and verified in free space, establishing their viability as a modular resource for quantum computing architectures.
conclusion: The work provides a practical photonic platform for producing non-Gaussian states, advancing the hardware ingredients needed for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Experimental Observation Of Multimode Quantum Phase Transitions In A Superconducting Bose-Hubbard Simulator
authors: Claudia Castillo-Moreno, Théo Sépulcre, Timo Hillmann, Kazi Rafsanjani Amin, Mikael Kervinen, And Simone Gasparinetti
abstract:
Author(s): Claudia Castillo-Moreno, Théo Sépulcre, Timo Hillmann, Kazi Rafsanjani Amin, Mikael Kervinen, and Simone Gasparinetti

By harnessing cross-Kerr interactions in a superconducting microwave Bose-Hubbard lattice, an experimental study reveals a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in one dimension.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033030] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: An experiment using a superconducting microwave Bose-Hubbard lattice with cross-Kerr interactions observes a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in one dimension.
motivation: Quantum simulators based on superconducting circuits offer a controllable platform to study many-body phases, but observing multimode dissipative phase transitions experimentally remains challenging.
method: The authors harness cross-Kerr interactions in a superconducting microwave Bose-Hubbard lattice to realize a one-dimensional multimode system, and characterize its steady-state behavior to identify the phase transition.
result: A first-order multimode dissipative phase transition is experimentally observed in the one-dimensional lattice.
conclusion: The work demonstrates superconducting circuit simulators as a viable platform for exploring multimode dissipative phase transitions, connecting circuit QED hardware to many-body open-system physics.

title: Semidefinite Programming For Quantum Channel Learning
authors: Mikhail Gennadievich Belov, Victor Victorovich Dubov, Vadim Konstantinovich Ivanov, Alexander Yurievich Maslov, Olga Vladimirovna Proshina, And Vladislav Gennadievich Malyshkin
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Gennadievich Belov, Victor Victorovich Dubov, Vadim Konstantinovich Ivanov, Alexander Yurievich Maslov, Olga Vladimirovna Proshina, and Vladislav Gennadievich Malyshkin

The problem of reconstructing a quantum channel from a sample of classical data is considered. When the total fidelity can be represented as a ratio of two quadratic forms (e.g., in the case of mapping a mixed state to a pure state, projective operators, unitary learning, and others), semidefinite p…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035302] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a semidefinite programming approach to reconstruct a quantum channel from classical data when the total fidelity is a ratio of two quadratic forms.
motivation: Quantum channel characterization is essential for verifying quantum devices, but learning channels from limited data is challenging and often nonconvex.
method: The authors formulate channel reconstruction as a convex semidefinite program, exploiting cases where fidelity can be expressed as a ratio of quadratic forms, such as mapping a mixed state to a pure state, projective operators, or unitary learning.
result: The SDP framework provides a tractable optimization method for learning quantum channels from classical data samples, with potential applicability to various fidelity-based learning tasks.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical tool for quantum channel learning, though its scope is limited to specific fidelity structures and its theoretical guarantees are not deeply explored in the abstract.

title: Measurements Of $Z$-Boson Pair Entanglement In Decays Of Higgs Bosons At The Atlas Experiment
authors: G. Aad et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): G. Aad et al. (ATLAS Collaboration)

First measurements of quantum entanglement between two massive vector bosons at the electroweak scale link quantum information concepts with precision measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111804] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: First measurement of quantum entanglement between Z bosons produced in Higgs boson decays at ATLAS, linking quantum information concepts with high-energy precision measurements.
motivation: Quantum entanglement is usually probed in low-energy systems; testing it at the electroweak scale provides a novel regime for quantum foundations and connects particle physics with quantum information.
method: The ATLAS experiment analyzes Higgs boson decays into Z boson pairs and measures entanglement between the two Z bosons using angular correlations of their decay products.
result: Observation of quantum entanglement between the Z bosons with significance exceeding background expectations, marking the first such measurement for massive vector bosons at the electroweak scale.
conclusion: The result demonstrates that entanglement can be measured in high-energy particle collisions, opening a new interface between quantum information and particle physics.

title: Spatial Decomposition Of Displacement Signals In Scattered Light Of A Levitated Nanoparticle
authors: Xu-Yuan Cheng, Long Wang, Lyu-Hang Liu, Yuan Tian, Guang-Can Guo, Yu Zheng, And Fang-Wen Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Xu-Yuan Cheng, Long Wang, Lyu-Hang Liu, Yuan Tian, Guang-Can Guo, Yu Zheng, and Fang-Wen Sun

Efficient measurement of center-of-mass motion is fundamental to force sensing and quantum control in levitated optomechanics. While scattering theories predict the spatial distribution of displacement information, direct experimental mapping of this information remains undemonstrated, leaving uncer…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033509] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally maps the spatial distribution of displacement signals in scattered light from a levitated nanoparticle.
motivation: Efficient measurement of center-of-mass motion is crucial for force sensing and quantum control in levitated optomechanics, but direct experimental mapping of displacement information in scattered light has not been demonstrated.
method: The authors use optical scattering from a levitated nanoparticle and perform spatial decomposition of the detected displacement signals to reconstruct the distribution of information.
result: They achieve a direct experimental mapping of the spatial distribution of displacement signals, revealing how information is distributed in the scattered light.
conclusion: This characterization provides a basis for optimizing detection schemes in levitated optomechanics, with potential impact on force sensing and quantum control.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper analytically computes the spectral form factor to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.
motivation: The spectral form factor is a key diagnostic of quantum chaos, but its analytic structure beyond leading order across all symmetry classes remained underexplored.
method: Using random matrix theory and analytic techniques, the authors derive leading and next-to-leading-order contributions to the spectral form factor for chaotic many-body systems in each Dyson symmetry class.
result: Closed-form analytic expressions for the spectral form factor up to second order in time are obtained, revealing symmetry-class-dependent behavior in the chaotic regime.
conclusion: The results provide benchmark analytic predictions for quantum chaos diagnostics and clarify how Dyson symmetry classification shapes spectral correlations in many-body systems.

title: Experimental Observation Of Dynamical Phase Transitions In A Dephased Photonic Quantum Walk
authors: Xiaojian Huang, Lei Xiao, Bingzi Huo, Xiaowei Wang, Stefano Longhi, And Peng Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaojian Huang, Lei Xiao, Bingzi Huo, Xiaowei Wang, Stefano Longhi, and Peng Xue

Dynamical phase transitions in open quantum systems govern how nonequilibrium states relax toward a stationary state. We study these transitions experimentally using a discrete-time photonic quantum walk on a three-node graph. A tunable synthetic gauge flux and calibrated dephasing allow us to contr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 110804] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally observes dynamical phase transitions in a dephased photonic quantum walk on a three-node graph.
motivation: Dynamical phase transitions in open quantum systems govern how nonequilibrium states relax toward a stationary state, but their experimental observation remains challenging.
method: A discrete-time photonic quantum walk is implemented with a tunable synthetic gauge flux and calibrated dephasing to study the transition dynamics.
result: The experiment demonstrates signatures of dynamical phase transitions in the dephased quantum walk, showing how dephasing and gauge flux control the relaxation behavior.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental platform for studying nonequilibrium phase transitions in open quantum systems, though it is not directly focused on information-theoretic or thermodynamic quantities.

title: Nanoparticle Arrays Levitated In A Cavity For Quantum Sensing
authors: J. H. Iacoponi, M. Rademacher, And T. S. Monteiro
abstract:
Author(s): J. H. Iacoponi, M. Rademacher, and T. S. Monteiro
