Levitated nanoparticles are being investigated as ultrasensitive quantum sensors of forces and accelerations, with applications ranging from fundamental physics phenomena such as dark matter or quantum gravity to real-world applications. Attention is now turning to multiparticle regimes, and an impo…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033286] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies arrays of levitated nanoparticles inside an optical cavity for ultrasensitive quantum sensing of forces and accelerations.
motivation: Levitated nanoparticles are promising quantum sensors, and moving to multiparticle regimes could improve sensitivity for fundamental physics and real-world applications.
method: The authors likely analyze cavity optomechanics with multiple levitated nanoparticles, examining collective effects and sensing performance.
result: The work characterizes how nanoparticle arrays in a cavity can enhance or enable quantum sensing, though specific results are not fully detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: Cavity-levitated nanoparticle arrays may provide a viable platform for quantum sensing, but the focus is applied metrology rather than core quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Long-Lived Mechanically Detected Molecular Spins For Quantum Sensing
authors: Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, And Raffi Budakian
abstract:
Author(s): Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, and Raffi Budakian

Researchers integrate molecular spins with mechanical readout to detect nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031018] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: Researchers integrate molecular spins with mechanical readout to detect nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra.
motivation: Molecular spins offer long coherence times and nanoscale sensing potential, but sensitive detection of their magnetic signals remains challenging.
method: The work couples molecular spins to a mechanical resonator and uses mechanical readout to transduce magnetic-field-driven spin dynamics.
result: The platform achieves nanotesla magnetic-field sensitivity and resolves local nuclear magnetic resonance spectra while maintaining long spin coherence.
conclusion: Mechanically detected molecular spins provide a promising hybrid platform for quantum sensing and nanoscale magnetometry, though not directly for quantum information processing.

title: Efficient Quantum Optimization Via Dynamical Simulation
authors: Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, And Nathan Wiebe
abstract:
Author(s): Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, and Nathan Wiebe

A gradient-free approach to quantum optimization based on coherent simulation of time evolution can outperform gradient-descent-based methods in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033026] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: A gradient-free quantum optimization method based on coherent simulation of time evolution is shown to beat gradient-descent approaches in query complexity and resilience to barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational and gradient-based quantum optimization schemes suffer from poor scaling and barren plateaus, motivating alternative strategies that avoid gradients entirely.
method: The authors replace gradient-descent-based optimization with a coherent simulation of time evolution, treating optimization as a dynamical process realized directly on the quantum device.
result: The dynamical simulation approach achieves better query complexity than gradient-based methods and shows improved robustness against barren plateaus.
conclusion: Simulating dynamics coherently offers an efficient, gradient-free route to quantum optimization, though its relevance is to quantum algorithms rather than the researcher's information-theoretic or thermodynamic focus areas.

title: Observation Of Individual Vortex Penetration In A Coplanar Superconducting Resonator
authors: Kirill Shulga, Shunsuke Nishimura, Pavel A. Volkov, Miu Hirano, Toshiaki Inada, Ryota Hasegawa, Takeyuki Tsuji, Takayuki Iwasaki, Mutsuko Hatano, Kento Sasaki, And Kensuke Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Kirill Shulga, Shunsuke Nishimura, Pavel A. Volkov, Miu Hirano, Toshiaki Inada, Ryota Hasegawa, Takeyuki Tsuji, Takayuki Iwasaki, Mutsuko Hatano, Kento Sasaki, and Kensuke Kobayashi

A coplanar superconducting resonator makes possible the direct observation of the real-time entry of individual Abrikosov vortices.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116001] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A coplanar superconducting resonator is used to directly observe the real-time entry of individual Abrikosov vortices.
motivation: Understanding vortex dynamics in superconducting films is important because trapped vortices degrade the performance of superconducting devices, yet individual vortex penetration events are hard to observe in real time.
method: The authors exploit a coplanar superconducting resonator whose resonance response is sensitive to the presence of single vortices, allowing time-resolved detection of vortex entry events.
result: Individual vortex penetration events are observed in real time, revealing discrete, stochastic entry of Abrikosov vortices into the resonator.
conclusion: The work establishes a sensitive resonator-based platform for studying single-vortex dynamics, with implications for vortex-induced loss in superconducting devices.

title: Qualitative And Quantitative Analysis For The Route To Chaos Via Intermittent Chaos In An Optomechanical Resonator
authors: Yue Huo, Zhe Wang, Zhenning Yang, Xiaohe Tang, Deng-Wei Zhang, Qianchuan Zhao, Wenjie Wan, Yu-Xi Liu, Xin-You Lü, Guangming Zhao, Liang Lu, And Jing Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Huo, Zhe Wang, Zhenning Yang, Xiaohe Tang, Deng-Wei Zhang, Qianchuan Zhao, Wenjie Wan, Yu-xi Liu, Xin-You Lü, Guangming Zhao, Liang Lu, and Jing Zhang

Intermittent chaos is a particular nonlinear phenomenon representing a transitional state in the route to chaos. It alternates between periodic and chaotic motions over time, different from the conventional period-doubling bifurcation. Here we qualitatively and quantitatively analyze this specific b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033510] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper qualitatively and quantitatively analyzes intermittent chaos as a route to chaos in an optomechanical resonator.
motivation: Intermittent chaos is a transitional nonlinear phenomenon that alternates between periodic and chaotic motions, and its route to chaos in optomechanical resonators is not well understood.
method: The authors use nonlinear dynamics analysis, likely involving numerical simulations, bifurcation diagrams, and quantitative measures such as Lyapunov exponents or time-series analysis.
result: They characterize the intermittent chaotic behavior and provide qualitative and quantitative descriptions of the transition to chaos in the optomechanical system.
conclusion: The study offers insights into nonlinear dynamics of optomechanical resonators, but it does not directly address quantum information processing or hybrid quantum system applications.

title: A Heuristic For Matrix Product State Simulation Of Out-of-Equilibrium Dynamics Of Two-Dimensional Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, And Kostyantyn Kechedzhi
abstract:
Author(s): Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, and Kostyantyn Kechedzhi

A new heuristic approach accelerates the convergence of classical simulation of two-dimensional quantum dynamics, enabling the verification of quantum simulation experiments in previously inaccessible regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033048] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: A heuristic is introduced to accelerate matrix product state classical simulation of out-of-equilibrium dynamics in two-dimensional quantum spin systems.
motivation: Classical simulation of 2D quantum dynamics is challenging, but verification of quantum simulation experiments requires access to previously inaccessible regimes.
method: The authors develop a heuristic that improves convergence of matrix product state simulations for out-of-equilibrium dynamics in 2D quantum spin systems.
result: The heuristic enables classical simulation in regimes that were previously inaccessible, aiding verification of quantum simulation experiments.
conclusion: This provides a specialized numerical tool for benchmarking 2D quantum dynamics, though it falls outside the core information-theoretic and thermodynamic interests.

title: Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies Against Quantum Vulnerabilities: Resource Estimates And Mitigations
authors: Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, And Dan Boneh
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, and Dan Boneh

The quantum computer that breaks cryptocurrencies is smaller and closer than the community assumed—this Perspective quantifies the threat and charts the urgent migration to postquantum security.


[PRX Quantum 7, 031001] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This Perspective estimates the quantum resources needed to break elliptic curve cryptocurrencies and advocates for urgent migration to post-quantum cryptography.
motivation: Quantum computers threaten ECC-based cryptocurrencies, and the required resources may be smaller and closer than previously assumed.
method: The authors provide resource estimates for Shor's algorithm applied to elliptic curve discrete logarithms, considering various qubit technologies and error correction.
result: They find that breaking ECC may require significantly fewer physical qubits and gates than earlier estimates, making the threat more imminent.
conclusion: Urgent migration to post-quantum cryptographic standards is necessary to secure cryptocurrencies.

title: Intermittent Time-crystalline Dynamics Under Stochastic Measurements
authors: Carlos Caro And Francisco Gámez
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Caro and Francisco Gámez

Discrete time crystals are nonequilibrium states of periodically driven quantum matter characterized by robust subharmonic responses. We investigate how such temporal order behaves in the presence of stochastic measurements. Using trajectory-resolved simulations of a monitored Floquet-Ising model, w…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032422] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: Trajectory-resolved simulations of a monitored Floquet-Ising model show that discrete time-crystalline order becomes intermittent under stochastic measurements.
motivation: Discrete time crystals are nonequilibrium periodically driven phases with robust subharmonic response, and it is unclear how measurement backaction—ubiquitous in monitored quantum systems—competes with or destroys this temporal order.
method: The authors numerically simulate a monitored Floquet-Ising model with stochastic measurements, resolving individual quantum trajectories to track the emergence and stability of time-crystalline order.
result: Time-crystalline dynamics become intermittent: the subharmonic response survives but fluctuates erratically, with measurement-induced competition between ordered and disordered trajectories.
conclusion: Stochastic measurements qualitatively reshape time-crystalline behavior, highlighting the interplay between measurement, decoherence, and nonequilibrium temporal order in driven quantum matter.

title: Interference-induced State Engineering And Hamiltonian Control For Noisy Collective-spin Metrology
authors: Le Bin Ho, Vu Xuan Tung Duong, Nozomu Takahashi, And Hiroaki Matsueda
abstract:
Author(s): Le Bin Ho, Vu Xuan Tung Duong, Nozomu Takahashi, and Hiroaki Matsueda

Interference provides a fundamental mechanism for generating and manipulating entanglement in many-body quantum systems. Here, we develop an interference framework in which the nonlinear dynamics of collective spin-[MATH] ensembles are mapped onto phase accumulation and self-interference in p…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032206] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an interference-based framework to engineer states and control Hamiltonians in noisy collective-spin ensembles for improved quantum metrology.
motivation: Collective spin ensembles are promising for quantum-enhanced metrology, but nonlinear dynamics and noise limit achievable precision.
method: The authors map the nonlinear dynamics of collective spin ensembles onto phase accumulation and self-interference in phase space, enabling state engineering and Hamiltonian control.
result: They show that interference-induced states and tailored Hamiltonians can mitigate noise and enhance metrological sensitivity beyond conventional schemes.
conclusion: The framework offers a practical route to robust quantum metrology with noisy collective-spin systems, though it remains platform-specific and applied.

title: Halving The Arbitrary Rotation Cost Of Controlled, Trotterized Time Evolution
authors: William A. Simon And Peter J. Love
abstract:
Author(s): William A. Simon and Peter J. Love

Quantum simulation is a promising application for quantum computing. Quantum simulation algorithms may require the ability to control the time evolution unitary. Naive techniques to control a unitary can substantially increase the required computational resources. A standard approach to controlling …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032425] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to halve the cost of arbitrary rotations in controlled Trotterized time evolution for quantum simulation.
motivation: Quantum simulation algorithms often require controlled time evolution, but naive control techniques can substantially increase the required computational resources, motivating the need for more efficient implementations.
method: The authors analyze and optimize the implementation of controlled Trotterized time evolution, likely using gate decompositions or symmetry arguments to reduce the number of arbitrary rotations.
result: They achieve a factor of two reduction in the arbitrary rotation cost compared to standard approaches for controlled time evolution.
conclusion: This reduction in rotation cost lowers the resource overhead for quantum simulation, potentially enabling more efficient implementations on quantum hardware.

title: Spatially Resolved Temperature Measurement Using Rydberg Doppler Broadening Thermometry
authors: K. N. Trivedi, M. Carminati, Èlia Solé Cardona, T. Bonaccorsi, R. Donofrio, B. Bégoc, And O. Morsch
abstract:
Author(s): K. N. Trivedi, M. Carminati, Èlia Solé Cardona, T. Bonaccorsi, R. Donofrio, B. Bégoc, and O. Morsch

We demonstrate a technique for spatially resolved temperature measurement utilizing Rydberg Doppler broadening thermometry. This method employs two focused laser beams arranged perpendicularly to excite laser-cooled atoms from the ground state to a Rydberg state via a two-photon absorption process. …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 113401] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: A technique for spatially resolved temperature measurement using Rydberg Doppler broadening thermometry with two focused laser beams.
motivation: To enable spatially resolved temperature measurements in cold atom systems, which is important for understanding and controlling ultracold gases.
method: Two perpendicular focused laser beams excite laser-cooled atoms from the ground state to a Rydberg state via a two-photon absorption process, and the Doppler broadening of the Rydberg transition is analyzed to infer temperature with spatial resolution.
result: The method provides spatially resolved temperature measurements, demonstrating its capability in a cold atom experiment.
conclusion: This technique offers a new tool for thermometry in cold atom systems, with potential applications in quantum simulation and computing.

title: Lowering The Temperature Of Two-dimensional Fermionic Tensor Networks With Cluster Expansions
authors: Sander de Meyer, Atsushi Ueda, Yuchi He, Nick Bultinck, And Jutho Haegeman
abstract:
Author(s): Sander De Meyer, Atsushi Ueda, Yuchi He, Nick Bultinck, and Jutho Haegeman

Representing the time-evolution operator as a tensor network constitutes a key ingredient in several algorithms for studying quantum lattice systems at finite temperature or in a nonequilibrium setting. For a Hamiltonian composed of strictly short-range interactions, the Suzuki-Trotter decomposition…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175113] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a cluster-expansion-based tensor network method for simulating two-dimensional fermionic lattice systems at lower temperatures by representing the time-evolution operator.
motivation: Simulating finite-temperature and nonequilibrium quantum lattice systems is challenging, especially in two dimensions where tensor network methods face severe entanglement growth at low temperatures.
method: The authors use the Suzuki-Trotter decomposition and cluster expansions to construct an efficient tensor network representation of the time-evolution operator for short-range Hamiltonians.
result: This approach lowers the achievable temperature in 2D fermionic tensor network simulations, likely by reducing the required bond dimension or computational cost.
conclusion: The method extends tensor network techniques to access lower temperatures in finite-temperature and nonequilibrium studies of two-dimensional fermionic systems.

title: Non-Hermitian Symmetry Breaking And Lee-Yang Theory For Quantum $xyz$ And Clock Models
authors: Tian-Yi Gu And Gaoyong Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Tian-Yi Gu and Gaoyong Sun

Lee-Yang theory offers a unifying framework for understanding classical phase transitions and dynamical quantum phase transitions through the analysis of partition functions and Loschmidt echoes. Recently, this framework was extended to characterize quantum phase transitions of quantum Ising models …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034119] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends Lee-Yang theory and non-Hermitian symmetry breaking to characterize quantum phase transitions in quantum XYZ and clock models.
motivation: Lee-Yang theory provides a unifying framework for classical and dynamical quantum phase transitions via partition functions and Loschmidt echoes, and its recent extension to quantum Ising models motivates application to more complex spin systems.
method: The authors analyze partition functions and Loschmidt echoes, likely using non-Hermitian Hamiltonians and Lee-Yang zeros, to probe symmetry breaking and criticality in quantum XYZ and clock models.
result: They identify Lee-Yang zeros and non-Hermitian symmetry-breaking signatures that diagnose quantum phase transitions in these models.
conclusion: The framework generalizes Lee-Yang theory to broader quantum models and establishes a connection between non-Hermitian symmetry breaking and quantum critical phenomena.

title: Taming Nonlinear Energy Diffusion: The Case Of Time-crystal Energy Condensates
authors: P. I. Hurtado And G. Cortés-Guillén
abstract:
Author(s): P. I. Hurtado and G. Cortés-Guillén

The authors study a model of heat conduction with a bulk driving mechanism resembling the effect of an external field. They find that they can induce the spontaneous formation of traveling energy condensates that exhibit robust long-range temporal order reminiscent of continuous time crystals.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034110] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: A classical model of heat conduction with bulk driving exhibits spontaneous traveling energy condensates and long-range temporal order reminiscent of continuous time crystals.
motivation: To understand nonlinear energy diffusion and whether a bulk driving mechanism can induce robust temporal order in nonequilibrium heat transport.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional heat conduction model with a bulk driving term and study the formation, propagation, and stability of energy condensates.
result: They find that the driven system spontaneously forms traveling energy condensates with robust long-range temporal order, resembling continuous time crystals.
conclusion: The work shows that nonlinear energy diffusion can be tamed to produce time-crystal-like condensates, offering a classical mechanism for long-lived temporal order.

title: Extracting Conformal Data From Finite-size Tensor-network Flow In Critical Two-dimensional Classical Models
authors: Sing-Hong Chan And Pochung Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Sing-Hong Chan and Pochung Chen

We present a general framework for extracting conformal data from critical two-dimensional classical lattice models using finite-size tensor-network flow. The central idea is to identify, from transfer-matrix spectra, a self-consistent finite-size window together with a crossover scale that separate…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033297] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A tensor-network framework extracts conformal data from finite-size transfer-matrix spectra of critical two-dimensional classical lattice models by identifying a self-consistent finite-size window and crossover scale.
motivation: Conformal field theory provides a powerful description of critical two-dimensional systems, but reliably extracting conformal data from finite lattice models is complicated by finite-size effects.
method: The authors use finite-size tensor-network flow and transfer-matrix spectra to find a self-consistent window and a crossover scale that separate universal scaling from lattice-specific corrections.
result: The framework enables extraction of conformal data such as central charge and scaling dimensions from classical lattice models in a controlled way.
conclusion: This provides a general numerical tool for connecting lattice models to conformal field theory, but it lies outside the core quantum information and quantum thermodynamics interests of the researcher.

title: Block Encoding Of Sparse Matrices Via Coherent Permutation
authors: Abhishek Setty
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Setty

Block encoding of sparse matrices underpins quantum algorithms such as quantum singular value transformation, Hamiltonian simulation, and quantum linear system solvers, yet its efficient gate-level realization remains challenging, with index-mapping oracles constituting one important source of overh…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033282] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: A gate-level construction for block-encoding sparse matrices using coherent permutations to reduce index-mapping oracle overhead.
motivation: Block encoding is essential for quantum algorithms like quantum singular value transformation and Hamiltonian simulation, but its efficient gate-level realization is hindered by index-mapping overhead.
method: The paper proposes a coherent permutation-based approach to implement the index-mapping oracle, reducing the need for explicit index computation.
result: The method achieves lower gate complexity and resource requirements compared to existing techniques for block encoding sparse matrices.
conclusion: This coherent permutation technique makes block encoding more practical for near-term quantum algorithms.

title: Real-Time Dynamics In Two Dimensions With Tensor Network States Via Time-Dependent Variational Monte Carlo Method
authors: Yantao Wu And Jannes Nys
abstract:
Author(s): Yantao Wu and Jannes Nys

A new computational method, combining tensor network and Monte Carlo techniques, extends the reach of classical simulation for quantum dynamics in two dimensions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033035] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: A new time-dependent variational Monte Carlo method combining tensor network states and Monte Carlo sampling is proposed to simulate real-time quantum dynamics in two dimensions.
motivation: Simulating real-time dynamics of two-dimensional quantum many-body systems is challenging due to entanglement growth and sign problems, motivating efficient classical simulation methods.
method: The method combines tensor network states with time-dependent variational Monte Carlo, using stochastic sampling to optimize tensor network parameters for real-time evolution.
result: The approach extends the reach of classical simulation for two-dimensional quantum dynamics, potentially enabling study of larger systems and longer times.
conclusion: This technique provides a promising computational tool for investigating non-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics in two dimensions.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Electronic Structure Via Quantum Fast Multipole Method
authors: Dominic W. Berry, Kianna Wan, Andrew D. Baczewski, Elliot C. Eklund, Arkin Tikku, And Ryan Babbush
abstract:
Author(s): Dominic W. Berry, Kianna Wan, Andrew D. Baczewski, Elliot C. Eklund, Arkin Tikku, and Ryan Babbush

An algorithm for fast summation of the Coulomb potential enables quantum simulation of electronic structure with the lowest known asymptotic complexity in particle number.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033025] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: An algorithm for fast summation of the Coulomb potential enables quantum simulation of electronic structure with the lowest known asymptotic complexity in particle number.
motivation: Quantum simulation of electronic structure is a promising application of quantum computers, but efficient algorithms for computing Coulomb interactions are needed to achieve practical speedups.
method: The authors develop a quantum fast multipole method for fast summation of the Coulomb potential, leveraging classical fast multipole techniques adapted to quantum computation.
result: The algorithm achieves the lowest known asymptotic complexity in particle number for quantum simulation of electronic structure.
conclusion: This work provides an efficient quantum algorithm for electronic structure simulation, though its relevance to quantum information theory and thermodynamics is limited.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for polynomial-time tensor network contraction with rigorous approximation error bounds and exponential convergence.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is crucial for simulating quantum many-body systems, but existing belief propagation methods lack systematic corrections and error guarantees.
method: The authors develop a cluster-based correction to belief propagation that enables polynomial-time contraction of tensor networks while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential convergence in cluster size and provides certified approximations, improving upon standard belief propagation.
conclusion: This work advances tensor network contraction methods, offering a practical and rigorous tool for efficient simulation of quantum systems.

title: Topological Flowscape Reveals State Transitions In Nonreciprocal Living Matter
authors: Hyunseok Lee, Eliseanne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, And Nikta Fakhri
abstract:
Author(s): Hyunseok Lee, EliseAnne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, and Nikta Fakhri

Characterizing living systems far from the thermodynamic limit can yield insight into the physics of nonreciprocity and biological self-organization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031061] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a 'topological flowscape' framework to characterize nonreciprocal dynamics and state transitions in living (active) matter far from equilibrium.
motivation: Living systems operate far from thermodynamic equilibrium, and understanding nonreciprocity and self-organization in such systems could yield insight into the physics of biological organization.
method: The authors develop a topological flowscape formalism to analyze nonreciprocal dynamics, likely applied to experimental data from living matter to identify state transitions.
result: The topological flowscape reveals state transitions in nonreciprocal living matter, providing a new characterization of far-from-equilibrium biological dynamics.
conclusion: The framework offers a tool for understanding nonreciprocity and self-organization in living systems, though it remains within classical biological/active matter physics rather than information thermodynamics.

title: Gauge Anomaly And Visible Dissipation Bounds In Active Matter
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

We formulate a nonequilibrium gauge theory for active many-body steady states and derive rigorous, data-accessible lower bounds on dissipation. The setting is an overdamped translational sector on an extended one-particle state space, where internal variables may encode orientations, species, or oth…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034123] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a nonequilibrium gauge theory for active many-body steady states and derives rigorous, experimentally accessible lower bounds on dissipation.
motivation: Active matter systems continuously dissipate energy to sustain self-organized steady states, motivating a general framework that relates observable currents and internal variables to fundamental dissipation costs.
method: The authors construct an overdamped gauge theory on an extended one-particle state space where internal variables encode orientations or species, and use it to derive data-accessible dissipation bounds.
result: Rigorous lower bounds on dissipation are obtained for active many-body steady states, expressed in terms of experimentally measurable quantities.
conclusion: The gauge-theoretic formulation provides a principled, data-accessible route to bounding dissipation in active matter, extending thermodynamic constraints to classical nonequilibrium many-body systems.

title: Flux-Floquet Instability In Fluctuating Superconductors
authors: Marios H. Michael, Duilio de Santis, Eugene A. Demler, And Patrick A. Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Marios H. Michael, Duilio De Santis, Eugene A. Demler, and Patrick A. Lee

Intense terahertz light triggers a flux-Floquet instability in high-temperature superconductors, generating a giant magnetic response that reveals bound electron pairs survive well above the superconducting transition temperature.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031055] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: Intense terahertz light induces a flux-Floquet instability in fluctuating high-temperature superconductors, producing a giant magnetic response that indicates bound electron pairs persist well above Tc.
motivation: Understanding whether superconducting pairing correlations survive above the transition temperature is a central question in high-Tc physics, and driven (Floquet) light-matter protocols offer a route to probe these fluctuations.
method: Theoretical analysis of a Floquet-driven superconducting system where a terahertz field couples to fluctuating order, leading to a flux-Floquet instability and an enhanced magnetic (diamagnetic/paramagnetic) response.
result: The instability generates a giant magnetic response, which is interpreted as evidence that preformed electron pairs remain intact well above the equilibrium superconducting transition temperature.
conclusion: Driven Floquet dynamics can reveal hidden superconducting pairing correlations in the fluctuating regime above Tc, suggesting new optical probes of preformed pairs in high-temperature superconductors.

title: Revealing Electron-Ytterbium Interactions Through Rydberg Molecular Spectroscopy
authors: Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, And Matthew T. Eiles
abstract:
Author(s): Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, and Matthew T. Eiles

Precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules provides a powerful new window into fundamental atomic properties, laying essential groundwork for future experiments with divalent atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031045] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: Precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules reveals electron-ytterbium interactions and provides benchmark data for future experiments with divalent atoms.
motivation: Rydberg molecules offer a sensitive probe of low-energy electron-atom scattering and atomic structure, but such precision measurements had not been extended to divalent (two-valence-electron) species like ytterbium.
method: The authors performed high-resolution Rydberg molecular spectroscopy on ultracold ytterbium, measuring spectral lines of giant Rydberg molecules and fitting them to extract electron-ytterbium interaction parameters.
result: The measured spectra yield precise values for the electron-ytterbium scattering properties and molecular binding energies, quantifying the interaction strength in these giant Rydberg molecules.
conclusion: The work establishes a spectroscopic window into fundamental atomic properties of divalent atoms and lays groundwork for future experiments with ytterbium-based Rydberg systems.

title: Pauli Propagation: A Computational Framework For Simulating Quantum Systems
authors: Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, and Zoë Holmes

A comprehensive account of the Pauli propagation method for simulating quantum systems, from theory framework to software implementation and applications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 032001] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper has low relevance to quantum information and is not recommended.

title: Quantized Transport In Floquet Topological Insulators
authors: Rekha Kumari, Manas Kulkarni, And Abhishek Dhar
abstract:
Author(s): Rekha Kumari, Manas Kulkarni, and Abhishek Dhar

We study quantum transport in a periodically driven (Floquet) topological system coupled to static fermionic reservoirs. Using the Floquet nonequilibrium Green's-function (NEGF) formalism, we show, from exact numerics for a strip geometry, that the two-terminal (longitudinal) conductance is quantize…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165116] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Exact numerics for a periodically driven topological system coupled to static fermionic reservoirs show a quantized two-terminal longitudinal conductance.
motivation: Floquet topological insulators are predicted to host novel transport phenomena, but quantized transport in the presence of reservoirs is not fully understood.
method: The authors use the Floquet nonequilibrium Green's-function (NEGF) formalism and exact numerics for a strip geometry.
result: The two-terminal (longitudinal) conductance is found to be quantized in the driven topological phase.
conclusion: The results demonstrate robust quantized transport in Floquet topological insulators, with potential implications for driven topological devices.

title: Edge States Of A ${\mathrm{Bi}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{3}$ Nanosheet In A Perpendicular Magnetic Field
authors: S. P. J. Koenis, L. Maisel Licerán, And H. T. C. Stoof
abstract:
Author(s): S. P. J. Koenis, L. Maisel Licerán, and H. T. C. Stoof

Conventional wisdom dictates that the conducting edge states of two-dimensional topological insulators of the [MATH] family are protected by time-reversal symmetry. However, theoretical bulk calculations and a recent experiment show that the edge states persist in the p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175405] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies edge states in a Bi2Se3 nanosheet under a perpendicular magnetic field, showing they persist despite broken time-reversal symmetry.
motivation: Conventional wisdom holds that the conducting edge states of Bi2Se3-family topological insulators are protected by time-reversal symmetry, but recent bulk calculations and experiments suggest they can survive in a perpendicular magnetic field.
method: The authors perform theoretical bulk and edge-state calculations, likely using a tight-binding or k·p model, to analyze the robustness of edge states in the presence of a perpendicular magnetic field.
result: They find that the edge states persist even when time-reversal symmetry is broken by the magnetic field, challenging the standard protection mechanism.
conclusion: The persistence of edge states in a perpendicular magnetic field indicates that additional protection mechanisms beyond time-reversal symmetry may be at play in Bi2Se3 nanosheets.

title: Probing Atom-surface Interactions From Tunneling-time Measurements Via Rotation Transport On An Atom Chip
authors: J-B. Gerent, R. Veyron, V. Mancois, R. Huang, E. Beraud, And S. Bernon
abstract:
Author(s): J-B. Gerent, R. Veyron, V. Mancois, R. Huang, E. Beraud, and S. Bernon

We propose a method to measure the interaction between an ultracold gas of neutral atoms and a surface. This solution combines an optical dipole trap reflected by the surface, a magnetic trap formed by current carrying wires embedded below the surface, and a rotation of the surface itself. It allows…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033289] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose an atom-chip scheme that measures atom-surface interactions by monitoring rotation-induced tunneling transport of an ultracold neutral gas in a combined optical dipole and magnetic trap.
motivation: Precise characterization of the forces between cold neutral atoms and nearby surfaces is important for understanding Casimir-Polder-like potentials and for mitigating surface-induced decoherence in chip-based atomtronic devices.
method: An optical dipole trap reflected by a surface is combined with a magnetic trap formed by current-carrying wires buried beneath the surface; rotating the surface drives a controllable transport that is read out through tunneling-time measurements sensitive to the atom-surface potential.
result: The proposed protocol yields a measurable signature of the atom-surface interaction through the tunneling dynamics, offering a route to extract the interaction strength and range from rotation-transport data.
conclusion: The scheme provides a practical atom-chip platform for probing surface forces on ultracold gases, though it remains a metrology-oriented proposal rather than a quantum-information or thermodynamic result.

title: Robustness Of Real-Space Topology In Moiré Systems
authors: Kryštof Kolář, Kang Yang, Felix von Oppen, And Christophe Mora
abstract:
Author(s): Kryštof Kolář, Kang Yang, Felix von Oppen, and Christophe Mora

Topological analysis of real-space electronic textures in nonidealized moiré systems establishes a robust band index and maps wave functions onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031043] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a topological analysis of real-space electronic textures in nonidealized moiré systems, defining a robust band index and mapping wave functions onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.
motivation: Moiré systems host rich topological band structures, but idealizations break down in realistic devices where strain, disorder, and lattice relaxation distort the real-space texture, motivating a characterization of topology that remains robust under such nonidealities.
method: The authors analyze the real-space electronic textures of moiré superlattices, constructing a band index from the texture and mapping the wave functions onto an emergent fictitious magnetic field derived from the texture itself.
result: They show that the real-space topological band index is robust against nonideal features of the moiré pattern and that the fictitious magnetic field picture faithfully captures the wave-function behavior.
conclusion: Real-space topological descriptors provide a robust framework for classifying moiré bands, extending topological analysis beyond idealized continuum models.

title: Superballistic Transport Of Thermal Photons In Confined Many-Body Systems
authors: Jian Dong, Junming Zhao, Philippe Ben-Abdallah, And Linhua Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jian Dong, Junming Zhao, Philippe Ben-Abdallah, and Linhua Liu

Ballistic transport is traditionally regarded as a limiting regime for scattering-free energy transfer. Here, we predict a superballistic radiative heat transport regime that surpasses this limit in dilute chains of plasmonic nanoparticles confined within cavities. This anomalous regime exhibits sup…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116303] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts a superballistic regime of radiative heat transport in dilute chains of plasmonic nanoparticles confined in cavities, exceeding the conventional ballistic limit.
motivation: Ballistic transport is normally viewed as the upper bound for scattering-free energy transfer, and the authors ask whether radiative heat transport in confined many-body systems can surpass it.
method: They analyze radiative heat transfer between plasmonic nanoparticles in cavity-confined chains, using many-body electromagnetic/thermal transport modeling to characterize the transport exponent.
result: A superballistic transport regime is found in which heat flux grows faster than linearly with system length, exceeding the ballistic limit in dilute nanoparticle chains.
conclusion: Confined many-body geometries can enable anomalous radiative heat transport regimes, offering new design principles for nanoscale thermal management.

title: Restoration Of Topological Protection By Adiabatic-geometry-induced Suppression Of Intervalley Mixing
authors: Keita Funayama, Jotaro J. Nakane, And Ai Yamakage
abstract:
Author(s): Keita Funayama, Jotaro J. Nakane, and Ai Yamakage

Topological protection is weakened at armchair interfaces in quantum valley Hall systems because the two valleys mix and open a gap in the interface states. Here, the authors demonstrate that an adiabatic mass domain wall suppresses intervalley mixing, restoring robust propagation of topological interface modes throughout the bulk band gap. Experiments on silicon MEMS waveguides confirm efficient transmission through 90°, 120°, and 150° bends, establishing adiabatic geometry as a general strategy for designing versatile topological waveguides.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144103] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: An adiabatic mass domain wall suppresses intervalley mixing in quantum valley Hall systems, restoring robust topological interface modes and enabling efficient transmission through sharp bends in silicon MEMS waveguides.
motivation: Topological protection is weakened at armchair interfaces in quantum valley Hall systems because intervalley mixing opens a gap in the interface states, degrading topological transport.
method: The authors design an adiabatic mass domain wall to suppress intervalley mixing and experimentally test it using silicon MEMS waveguides with 90°, 120°, and 150° bends.
result: The adiabatic geometry restores robust propagation of topological interface modes throughout the bulk band gap, achieving efficient transmission through sharp bends.
conclusion: Adiabatic geometry is established as a general strategy for designing versatile topological waveguides with restored topological protection.

title: Effect Of Competing Orders On The Half-magnetization Plateaus In Spin-1 And Spin-3/2 Pyrochlore Magnets
authors: Imre Hagymási
abstract:
Author(s): Imre Hagymási

We use large-scale density-matrix renormalization group simulations with bond dimensions up to [MATH] to determine the magnetization curves of spin-1 and spin-[MATH] pyrochlore Heisenberg antiferromagnets. Both models exhibit a robust half-magnetization plateau. O…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154408] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: DMRG simulations show that spin-1 and spin-3/2 pyrochlore Heisenberg antiferromagnets host robust half-magnetization plateaus shaped by competing orders.
motivation: Half-magnetization plateaus in frustrated quantum magnets are important for understanding competing orders in pyrochlore systems.
method: Large-scale density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations with large bond dimensions are used to compute magnetization curves for spin-1 and spin-3/2 pyrochlore Heisenberg antiferromagnets.
result: Both models exhibit a robust half-magnetization plateau, with competing orders affecting its stability and magnetic response.
conclusion: The study clarifies how competing interactions and orders stabilize magnetization plateaus in frustrated pyrochlore magnets, providing benchmarks for future theoretical and experimental work.

title: Erratum: Trapping Potentials And Quantum Gates For Microwave-dressed Rydberg Atoms On An Atom Chip [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 013088 (2026)]
authors: Iason Tsiamis, Georgios Doultsinos, Andreas F. Tzortzakakis, Manuel Kaiser, Dominik Jakab, Andreas Günther, József Fortágh, And David Petrosyan
abstract:
Author(s): Iason Tsiamis, Georgios Doultsinos, Andreas F. Tzortzakakis, Manuel Kaiser, Dominik Jakab, Andreas Günther, József Fortágh, and David Petrosyan
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 039003] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the original paper on trapping potentials and quantum gates for microwave-dressed Rydberg atoms on an atom chip.
motivation: To correct errors in the original publication and ensure the accuracy of the scientific record.
method: Publication of a formal erratum notice referencing the original article (Phys. Rev. Research 8, 013088 (2026)).
result: The erratum provides a correction to the original article but contains no new scientific findings.
conclusion: It serves only to correct the record and is not a standalone research contribution.

title: Observation Of Correlated Plasmons In Low-Valence Nickelates
authors: Y. Shen, W. He, J. Sears, Xuefei Guo, Xiangpeng Luo, A. Roll, J. Li, J. Pelliciari, Xi He, I. Božovič, Junjie Zhang, J. F. Mitchell, V. Bisogni, M. Mitrano, S. Johnston, And M. P. M. Dean
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Shen, W. He, J. Sears, Xuefei Guo, Xiangpeng Luo, A. Roll, J. Li, J. Pelliciari, Xi He, I. Božovič, Junjie Zhang, J. F. Mitchell, V. Bisogni, M. Mitrano, S. Johnston, and M. P. M. Dean

Resonant inelastic x-ray scattering measurements reveal propagating plasmons in the low-valence nickelate Pr
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031031] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: Resonant inelastic x-ray scattering reveals propagating plasmons in the low-valence nickelate Pr-based compound, with dynamics distinct from cuprate superconductors.
motivation: To understand the nature of correlated plasmons in nickelates and compare their behavior with that of cuprate superconductors, which may shed light on the role of plasmons in high-temperature superconductivity.
method: The authors performed resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) measurements on single crystals of a low-valence nickelate to probe charge excitations and plasmon dispersion.
result: They observed correlated propagating plasmons whose energy-momentum dispersion and damping differ markedly from those in cuprates, suggesting different electronic correlation effects.
conclusion: The findings highlight distinct plasmon dynamics in nickelates, offering new insights into the physics of correlated electron systems and their contrast with cuprates.

title: Quantum-informed Reduction Algorithm For The Maximum Independent Set Problem
authors: Martin J. A. Schuetz, Romina Yalovetzky, Ruben S. Andrist, Grant Salton, Yue Sun, Rudy Raymond, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Atithi Acharya, Ruslan Shaydulin, Marco Pistoia, And Helmut G. Katzgraber
abstract:
Author(s): Martin J. A. Schuetz, Romina Yalovetzky, Ruben S. Andrist, Grant Salton, Yue Sun, Rudy Raymond, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Atithi Acharya, Ruslan Shaydulin, Marco Pistoia, and Helmut G. Katzgraber

We propose and implement a quantum-informed reduction algorithm for the maximum independent set problem that integrates classical kernelization techniques with information extracted from quantum devices. Our larger framework consists of dedicated application, algorithm, and hardware layers, and easi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033296] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum-informed reduction algorithm that combines classical kernelization for the maximum independent set problem with information extracted from quantum devices.
motivation: Solving maximum independent set is classically hard, and near-term quantum devices may provide useful heuristic information to guide classical preprocessing and reduction.
method: A layered framework (application, algorithm, hardware) integrates classical kernelization techniques with quantum-derived information to iteratively reduce graph instances.
result: The hybrid reduction scheme demonstrates how quantum device outputs can inform and shrink problem instances, potentially improving solvability of large graphs.
conclusion: Quantum-informed reductions offer a practical hybrid route for combinatorial optimization, though gains depend on quantum hardware quality and problem structure.

title: Hamiltonian Learning Quantum Magnets With Dynamical Impurity Tomography
authors: Netta Karjalainen, Greta Lupi, Rouven Koch, Adolfo O. Fumega, And Jose L. Lado
abstract:
Author(s): Netta Karjalainen, Greta Lupi, Rouven Koch, Adolfo O. Fumega, and Jose L. Lado

Nanoscale engineered spin systems, ranging from spins on surfaces to nanographenes, provide flexible platforms to realize entangled quantum magnets from a bottom-up approach. However, assessing the quantum many-body Hamiltonian realized in a specific experiment remains an exceptional open challenge,…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033281] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a dynamical impurity tomography protocol to learn the many-body Hamiltonian of nanoscale engineered quantum magnets, such as spins on surfaces and nanographenes.
motivation: Engineered spin systems provide flexible bottom-up platforms for entangled quantum magnets, but determining the actual many-body Hamiltonian realized in a given experiment remains a major open challenge.
method: The authors use dynamical impurity tomography, exploiting the time-resolved dynamics of an impurity probe coupled to the magnet to reconstruct Hamiltonian parameters from measurable response signals.
result: The protocol is shown to recover the microscopic Hamiltonian of quantum magnets, bridging experimentally accessible dynamical signatures with the underlying spin-model parameters.
conclusion: Dynamical impurity tomography offers a practical route to Hamiltonian learning in nanoscale quantum magnets, connecting surface-science platforms to quantum many-body model characterization.

title: Quantum Computing Demonstration Of The Polaron-molecule Transition On A Noisy Intermediate-scale Quantum Device
authors: Hugo Catalá, Ezequiel Valero, And Germán Rodrigo
abstract:
Author(s): Hugo Catalá, Ezequiel Valero, and Germán Rodrigo

The simulation of strongly correlated fermionic systems remains a significant challenge in computational physics due to the exponential growth of the Hilbert space and the fermionic sign problem. In this work, we report a quantum computing demonstration exploring the unified physics of the Fermi pol…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032609] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A NISQ-era quantum computing demonstration simulating the polaron-to-molecule transition in strongly correlated Fermi gases.
motivation: Simulating strongly correlated fermionic systems classically is intractable due to exponential Hilbert-space growth and the fermionic sign problem, motivating quantum simulation approaches.
method: The authors use a noisy intermediate-scale quantum device to simulate the unified physics of the Fermi polaron system and its transition to a molecular state.
result: The quantum device reproduces signatures of the polaron-molecule transition, demonstrating feasibility of NISQ hardware for strongly correlated fermionic problems.
conclusion: The work shows current noisy quantum hardware can address nontrivial correlated fermion physics, though it remains a domain-specific quantum simulation demonstration rather than a contribution to quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum hardware.

title: Coexisting Spin, Vibrational, And Orbital Excitations In Conductance Spectra
authors: Arnab Banerjee, Roberto Robles, Nicolás Lorente, Richard Berndt, And Alexander Weismann
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Banerjee, Roberto Robles, Nicolás Lorente, Richard Berndt, and Alexander Weismann

A simple conductance asymmetry metric helps disentangle coexisting spin, vibrational, and orbital excitations within a single cobaltocene molecule, unlocking new pathways for single-molecule quantum computing.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116403] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A conductance asymmetry metric is used to disentangle coexisting spin, vibrational, and orbital excitations in a single cobaltocene molecule.
motivation: Understanding and controlling multiple coexisting excitations in single molecules is relevant for single-molecule quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze conductance spectra of a cobaltocene molecule using a simple asymmetry metric to separate contributions from spin, vibrational, and orbital excitations.
result: The metric successfully distinguishes and characterizes the coexisting spin, vibrational, and orbital excitations within a single molecule.
conclusion: This approach unlocks new pathways for single-molecule quantum computing by enabling clearer identification of molecular excitations.

title: Influence Of Different Radio-frequency Discharge Conditions And Impurities On The Process Of $^{3}\mathrm{He}$ Nuclear Polarization In Magnetized Plasma
authors: A. S. Makarchenko And V. V. Kuzmin
abstract:
Author(s): A. S. Makarchenko and V. V. Kuzmin

In this article we report on an experimental study of the polarization of atoms in magnetized plasma (PAMP) in [MATH] gas under various conditions of radio-frequency (rf) excitation of plasma. Among parameters influencing the plasma dynamics are frequency, average and peak rf powers. Our …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032813] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study of 3He nuclear polarization in magnetized plasma (PAMP) under varying radio-frequency discharge conditions and impurity levels.
motivation: Optimizing 3He polarization is important for applications such as polarized targets, neutron spin filters, and spin-based metrology, where plasma parameters strongly affect achievable polarization.
method: Experimental measurements of 3He nuclear polarization in magnetized rf-excited plasma, systematically varying excitation frequency, average and peak rf power, and gas impurities.
result: The dependence of polarization on rf frequency, average/peak power, and impurity concentration is characterized, revealing the plasma conditions that favor or suppress efficient 3He polarization.
conclusion: Control over rf discharge parameters and impurity levels is essential for maximizing 3He nuclear polarization in magnetized plasma, informing practical optimization of such polarized-gas sources.

title: Lie-algebra-assisted Quantum Simulation And Quantum Optimal Control Via High-order Magnus Expansions
authors: R. F. Dos Santos And S. J. J. M. F. Kokkelmans
abstract:
Author(s): R. F. dos Santos and S. J. J. M. F. Kokkelmans

The evolution of a quantum system under time-dependent driving exhibits phenomena that are absent in its stationary counterpart. However, the high dimensionality and noncommutative nature of quantum dynamics make this a challenging problem. The Magnus expansion provides an analytic framework to appr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032415] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops high-order Magnus expansion techniques assisted by Lie algebra for quantum simulation and quantum optimal control of time-dependent driven quantum systems.
motivation: Time-dependent quantum dynamics are high-dimensional and noncommutative, making accurate simulation and control challenging with standard methods.
method: The authors use Lie-algebraic structures to construct high-order Magnus expansions that approximate the time-evolution operator and enable optimal control protocols.
result: The approach yields improved analytic approximations and control strategies for quantum systems under time-dependent driving.
conclusion: The work advances quantum simulation and control theory but does not directly address the researcher's core interests in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dynamical Decoupling For Quantum Metrology With Periodically Driven Hamiltonians
authors: Qifei Wei, Haorui Chen, And Shengshi Pang
abstract:
Author(s): Qifei Wei, Haorui Chen, and Shengshi Pang

Quantum metrology exploits quantum resources to achieve measurement precision beyond classical scaling, but this advantage is often compromised by environmental decoherence. While dynamical decoupling is a powerful tool for eliminating non-Markovian noise, it has a fundamental conflict: The decoupli…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032418] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes dynamical decoupling strategies for quantum metrology when the sensing Hamiltonian is periodically driven, addressing the conflict between noise suppression and signal preservation.
motivation: Quantum metrology can surpass classical precision but is limited by decoherence, and dynamical decoupling, while effective against non-Markovian noise, may interfere with the periodic driving used for parameter encoding.
method: The authors study periodically driven Hamiltonians combined with dynamical decoupling pulse sequences, likely using analytical or numerical models to assess measurement precision under non-Markovian noise.
result: They show how the interplay between decoupling and periodic driving affects metrological precision, potentially identifying conditions where decoupling improves or degrades sensitivity.
conclusion: The work provides guidance for designing dynamical decoupling protocols in quantum metrology with periodically driven systems, although it does not align with the defined core research directions.

title: Spinon-induced Phonon Dynamics In Chiral And $π$-flux Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Zachary Hizon And Kristian Hauser Villegas
abstract:
Author(s): Zachary Hizon and Kristian Hauser Villegas

Quantum spin liquids (QSLs) are magnetic phases that evade long-range order down to the lowest temperatures due to strong quantum fluctuations. Their lack of conventional order parameters, however, makes experimental identification challenging. In this work, we investigate how distinct QSL phases af…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175117] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how spinon excitations in chiral and π-flux quantum spin liquids influence phonon dynamics, suggesting phonon signatures as a probe of these phases.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are difficult to identify experimentally due to the absence of conventional order parameters, motivating the search for characteristic signatures in other observables such as phonon dynamics.
method: The authors theoretically compute the spinon-induced phonon self-energy and related dynamical response for two distinct quantum spin liquid phases (chiral and π-flux) using slave-particle mean-field theory and linear response.
result: They find that the two QSL phases produce qualitatively different phonon dynamics, including distinct temperature and momentum dependencies in the phonon lifetime or thermal conductivity.
conclusion: Phonon dynamics can serve as a discriminating experimental probe for distinguishing chiral and π-flux quantum spin liquids.

title: Physical Signatures Of Supercritical Fluid Boundaries
authors: Sha Jin, Xinyang Li, Xue Fan, Matteo Baggioli, And Yuliang Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Sha Jin, Xinyang Li, Xue Fan, Matteo Baggioli, and Yuliang Jin

In the supercritical fluid (SCF) region, at temperatures and pressures above the critical point, the thermodynamic singularity separating liquids and gases no longer exists. Recent arguments based on thermodynamics and critical scalings have revived the proposal that the SCF constitutes an intermedi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035410] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates physical signatures of boundaries in supercritical fluids using thermodynamic arguments and critical scaling, reviving the proposal that supercritical fluids form an intermediate state between liquids and gases.
motivation: Above the critical point, the liquid-gas distinction vanishes because the thermodynamic singularity disappears, yet recent thermodynamic and scaling arguments suggest that residual boundaries or crossover regimes may still exist.
method: The authors likely combine thermodynamic analysis, critical scaling arguments, and possibly molecular dynamics or equation-of-state modeling to identify signatures of supercritical fluid boundaries.
result: They find physical signatures—likely in response functions or structural quantities—that support the existence of distinct regimes or boundaries within the supercritical fluid region.
conclusion: The work contributes to the ongoing debate on whether supercritical fluids possess hidden boundaries, but it remains a classical thermodynamics/statistical mechanics study with no quantum information or quantum thermodynamics content.

title: Nonlinear Density Scaling Of Spin Noise Reveals Atomic Correlations In Warm Vapors
authors: J. Delpy, E. Cardoz, K. V. Adwaith, N. Fayard, N. Belabas, F. Bretenaker, And F. Goldfarb
abstract:
Author(s): J. Delpy, E. Cardoz, K. V. Adwaith, N. Fayard, N. Belabas, F. Bretenaker, and F. Goldfarb

We experimentally demonstrate a nonlinear dependence of the spin-noise variance on atomic density in a warm alkali vapor. Implementing high-bandwidth spin-noise spectroscopy (SNS) near the [MATH] transition of rubidium, a quadratic spin-noise contribution is shown to arise at high densit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033283] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: Experimental spin-noise spectroscopy in warm rubidium vapor reveals a quadratic density scaling of spin-noise variance that signals atomic correlations.
motivation: Understanding spin correlations in warm alkali vapors is important for precision spectroscopy and for assessing whether such systems can support collective quantum effects.
method: High-bandwidth spin-noise spectroscopy is performed near an optical transition of rubidium, and the spin-noise variance is measured as a function of atomic density.
result: The spin-noise variance exhibits a nonlinear, quadratic dependence on density, indicating the emergence of atomic correlations at high densities.
conclusion: Spin-noise spectroscopy provides a sensitive probe of density-dependent atomic correlations in warm vapors, with possible implications for collective spin dynamics.

title: Quantum-ready Formulation For Uncompromised Data Assimilation With High-rank Covariances
authors: Takemasa Miyoshi
abstract:
Author(s): Takemasa Miyoshi

Data assimilation (DA) optimally fuses observational data with mathematical models, serving as a core computational framework for forecasting complex dynamical systems like the weather. Because manipulating large-scale high-rank error covariances is classically intractable, conventional DA is forced…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033287] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum-ready data assimilation formulation that handles high-rank error covariances without approximation, aiming to overcome classical intractability.
motivation: Data assimilation is central to forecasting complex systems like weather, but classically manipulating large-scale high-rank error covariances is intractable, forcing approximations.
method: Develops a quantum-compatible formulation for data assimilation, likely mapping high-rank covariance operations into quantum linear algebra or quantum circuit primitives.
result: The formulation offers an uncompromised treatment of high-rank covariances, though practical quantum implementation and resource estimates are not the focus of the abstract.
conclusion: Provides a conceptual pathway toward quantum-accelerated data assimilation for weather forecasting and other high-dimensional dynamical systems.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, and Alán Aspuru-Guzik

Injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas is shown to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with little cost increase, enabling a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033018] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces corrected product formulas with auxiliary terms to dramatically improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy at lower circuit depth for both quantum and classical simulations.
motivation: Product formulas are the dominant approach for Hamiltonian simulation, but their accuracy–cost tradeoff limits practical applications; there is a need for methods achieving higher accuracy without proportionally increasing circuit depth.
method: The authors inject carefully designed auxiliary terms into standard Trotter-like product formulas, deriving error-corrected decompositions and analyzing the resulting error scaling and resource costs.
result: The corrected product formulas reach target simulation accuracy with substantially reduced circuit depth and gate count compared to conventional product formulas of the same order.
conclusion: Corrected product formulas provide a practical route to faster algorithmic quantum and classical simulation of quantum systems, improving the accuracy-versus-cost frontier.

title: Generalized Hydrodynamics Of Bloch Oscillations In The Absence Of A Lattice
authors: Stefano Scopa, Philip Zechmann, Michael Knap, Jacopo de Nardis, And Alvise Bastianello
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Scopa, Philip Zechmann, Michael Knap, Jacopo De Nardis, and Alvise Bastianello

Objects subjected to a constant force generally increase their velocity over time. This expectation fails whenever their energy is a smooth and periodic function of momentum, resulting in periodic Bloch oscillations instead. Periodic dispersions, typical of lattice systems, can also emerge in contin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 113404] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a generalized hydrodynamics framework to describe Bloch oscillations in continuous systems without an underlying lattice.
motivation: Bloch oscillations are typically tied to lattice periodic potentials, but periodic dispersions can arise in continuum systems, and their many-body dynamics are not well understood.
method: Using generalized hydrodynamics, the authors analyze integrable many-body systems subject to a constant force and with a periodic single-particle dispersion, without an underlying lattice.
result: They show that Bloch oscillations persist and are captured by GHD, revealing how interactions modify the oscillation dynamics in the absence of a lattice.
conclusion: This extends the phenomenon of Bloch oscillations to continuum integrable systems, with implications for non-equilibrium quantum transport and hydrodynamics.

title: Merging And Oscillations Of Dipolar Bose-Einstein-condensate Droplets
authors: Wojciech Orłowski And Bartłomiej Szafran
abstract:
Author(s): Wojciech Orłowski and Bartłomiej Szafran

We investigate the dynamics of Bose-Einstein-condensate droplets composed of [MATH] atoms formed in a double-well potential following removal of the interwell barrier. By solving the dipolar Gross-Pitaevskii equation, we determine phase diagrams of ground-state configurations as functio…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033316] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the merging and oscillations of dipolar Bose-Einstein-condensate droplets in a double-well potential after barrier removal using the dipolar Gross-Pitaevskii equation.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of dipolar quantum droplets in double-well potentials is important for exploring many-body phenomena in ultracold atomic systems.
method: The authors solve the dipolar Gross-Pitaevskii equation numerically to obtain phase diagrams of ground-state configurations and simulate the real-time dynamics after removing the interwell barrier.
result: They identify distinct ground-state phases and observe merging dynamics and oscillations of the droplets, characterized by the interplay of dipolar interactions and quantum fluctuations.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the nonequilibrium behavior of dipolar BEC droplets, but it does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Coherent Densification Of Cold Atoms In A Wannier-Stark Ladder By Spatially Structured Resonant Coupling
authors: Quentin Thommen
abstract:
Author(s): Quentin Thommen

We propose a mechanism for coherent densification in a tilted optical lattice. The starting point is a well-known property of Wannier-Stark ladders: a homogeneous resonant coupling between neighboring Wannier-Stark states restores coherent translation. When the coupling amplitude is position depende…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033318] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes coherent densification of cold atoms in a tilted optical lattice via spatially structured resonant coupling in a Wannier-Stark ladder.
motivation: Wannier-Stark ladders enable coherent control of atoms in tilted lattices, and position-dependent coupling may allow densification.
method: Analyze a Wannier-Stark ladder with spatially structured resonant coupling to induce coherent translation and localization.
result: Demonstrates a mechanism for coherent densification, potentially enabling control of atomic density in optical lattices.
conclusion: The scheme offers a route to manipulate cold atoms in tilted lattices, though relevance to quantum information/thermodynamics/networks is limited.

title: Mapping The Parameter Space Of Double Microwave Shielding
authors: Hubert J. Jóźwiak, Ian Stevenson, Sebastian Will, And Tijs Karman
abstract:
Author(s): Hubert J. Jóźwiak, Ian Stevenson, Sebastian Will, and Tijs Karman

The authors systematically map the four-dimensional parameter space of double microwave shielding using universal dimensionless calculations to identify operating regimes free of field-linked bound states. By incorporating realistic experimental field constraints, they demonstrate that heavy, strongly dipolar molecules achieve strong two-body loss suppression alongside broad tunability of effective dipolar interactions.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033315] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper maps the four-dimensional parameter space of double microwave shielding to identify regimes free of field-linked bound states and shows that heavy, strongly dipolar molecules can achieve strong two-body loss suppression with broad tunability of dipolar interactions.
motivation: Microwave shielding is a key technique for stabilizing ultracold polar molecules by suppressing collisional loss, but optimal operating parameters and the role of field-linked bound states need systematic exploration.
method: The authors perform universal dimensionless calculations over a four-dimensional parameter space, incorporating realistic experimental field constraints to map operating regimes.
result: They identify parameter regimes free of field-linked bound states and demonstrate that heavy, strongly dipolar molecules can achieve strong two-body loss suppression alongside broad tunability of effective dipolar interactions.
conclusion: The findings provide practical guidance for implementing double microwave shielding in ultracold molecular experiments, enabling better control over dipolar interactions and loss.

title: High-optical-depth, sub-Doppler-width Absorption Lines At Telecom Wavelengths In Hot, Optically Driven Rubidium Vapor
authors: Inna Kviatkovsky, Lucas Pache, Viola-Antonella Zeilberger, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, Arno Rauschenbeutel, And Leonid Yatsenko
abstract:
Author(s): Inna Kviatkovsky, Lucas Pache, Viola-Antonella Zeilberger, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, Arno Rauschenbeutel, and Leonid Yatsenko

Doppler broadening presents a major limitation for high-resolution spectroscopy and nonlinear optics in room-temperature atomic vapors. Here, we demonstrate the suppression of Doppler broadening accompanied by pronounced absorption on the upper transition of a three-level ladder system, achieved by …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033714] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates sub-Doppler absorption lines at telecom wavelengths in hot, optically driven rubidium vapor using a three-level ladder system.
motivation: Doppler broadening limits high-resolution spectroscopy and nonlinear optics in room-temperature atomic vapors.
method: An optically driven three-level ladder system in hot Rb vapor is used to suppress Doppler broadening and achieve pronounced absorption on the upper transition.
result: High-optical-depth, sub-Doppler-width absorption lines are observed on the upper transition at telecom wavelengths.
conclusion: The technique enables high-resolution spectroscopy and nonlinear optics in hot vapors, but it does not directly advance quantum information theory or the specified research directions.

title: Anomalous Supercurrents In The Presence Of Particle Losses
authors: Risa Ogino And Shun Uchino
abstract:
Author(s): Risa Ogino and Shun Uchino

We show that the supercurrent properties of a superfluid or superconducting junction are significantly modified by single-particle losses in a conduction channel. In the presence of a spin-independent particle loss, we find regimes where the Josephson current [MATH] can develop additional zero…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033313] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically shows that single-particle losses in a conduction channel significantly modify supercurrent properties, leading to anomalous Josephson currents in superfluid or superconducting junctions.
motivation: Particle losses are ubiquitous in open quantum systems, but their impact on supercurrent and Josephson physics in junctions remains poorly understood.
method: The authors analyze a superfluid or superconducting junction subject to spin-independent single-particle losses, using theoretical modeling of the conduction channel.
result: They find regimes where the Josephson current develops additional zero crossings or otherwise anomalous behavior due to the particle losses.
conclusion: The results highlight the strong effect of dissipation on supercurrent and may be relevant for designing dissipative quantum devices based on Josephson junctions.

title: Improving Fermionic Variational Quantum Eigensolvers With Majorana swap Networks
authors: D. E. Fisher, S. A. Fldzhyan, D. V. Minaev, S. S. Straupe, And M. Yu. Saygin
abstract:
Author(s): D. E. Fisher, S. A. Fldzhyan, D. V. Minaev, S. S. Straupe, and M. Yu. Saygin

Simulating computationally hard fermionic systems is a promising application of quantum computing. However, mapping nonlocal fermionic operators to qubits often produces deep circuits, rendering such simulations impractical on near-term hardware. We introduce two Majorana swap network compilation st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032419] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces two Majorana swap network compilation schemes to reduce circuit depth for fermionic variational quantum eigensolvers on near-term quantum hardware.
motivation: Simulating computationally hard fermionic systems is a promising quantum computing application, but mapping nonlocal fermionic operators to qubits often produces deep circuits, making such simulations impractical on near-term devices.
method: The authors propose two compilation schemes based on Majorana swap networks to improve fermionic variational quantum eigensolvers.
result: The schemes are introduced with the aim of reducing circuit depth and enhancing the feasibility of fermionic simulations on near-term quantum hardware.
conclusion: This work may enable more practical fermionic quantum simulations by mitigating circuit-depth challenges through Majorana swap network compilation.

title: Parameter Estimation With One- And Two-time Measurements On The Emission Field Of The Boundary Time Crystal
authors: Albert Cabot, Federico Carollo, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Albert Cabot, Federico Carollo, and Igor Lesanovsky

Many-body quantum systems can exhibit collective effects that enhance the sensitivity of parameter estimation protocols. An example is provided by resonantly driven two-level atoms subject to collective dissipation, which can display a transition between a stationary phase and a time-crystal one. Pr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032604] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates parameter estimation using one- and two-time measurements on the emission field of a boundary time crystal, showing how collective dissipative dynamics can enhance metrological sensitivity.
motivation: Many-body quantum systems can exhibit collective effects that boost parameter estimation, and boundary time crystals—arising in driven dissipative atom ensembles—offer a promising platform for such enhanced sensing.
method: The authors consider resonantly driven two-level atoms with collective dissipation, compute the emission field, and analyze one- and two-time correlation measurements to estimate parameters across the stationary and time-crystal phases.
result: They find that two-time measurements can provide improved parameter estimation compared to single-time measurements, with sensitivity depending on the proximity to the phase transition and the specific measurement scheme.
conclusion: The results highlight the potential of boundary time crystals for quantum metrology and suggest that temporal correlations in the emission field are a valuable resource for parameter estimation.

title: Josephson Phase Shift And Diode Effect Due To The Inverse Spin Hall Effect
authors: Gen Tatara, Yositake Takane, And Aurelien Manchon
abstract:
Author(s): Gen Tatara, Yositake Takane, and Aurelien Manchon

We theoretically study the direct and inverse spin Hall effects in a superconductor-normal metal-superconductor junction induced by a spin-orbit interaction that is invariant under spatial inversion. We show that a supercurrent induces a spin Hall effect, leading to a static spin accumulation with o…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134415] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
