tldr: A theoretical study showing that direct and inverse spin Hall effects in superconductor-normal metal-superconductor junctions produce a supercurrent-induced spin accumulation, a Josephson phase shift, and a diode effect.
motivation: The authors investigate how spin-orbit interactions that preserve spatial inversion symmetry can couple charge supercurrents to spin degrees of freedom in superconducting junctions.
method: They perform a theoretical analysis of direct and inverse spin Hall effects in an SNS junction induced by inversion-symmetric spin-orbit interaction, deriving the resulting spin accumulation and its backaction on the superconducting phase.
result: A supercurrent generates a static spin accumulation via the spin Hall effect, which in turn shifts the Josephson phase and produces a superconducting diode effect with nonreciprocal critical currents.
conclusion: Inversion-symmetric spin-orbit coupling enables supercurrent-induced spin phenomena that break reciprocity in Josephson junctions, suggesting a route to superconducting diodes without external magnetic fields.

title: Circular Huygens Dipoles: Unidirectional Spin-angular Momentum From Achiral Nanoparticles
authors: Esmaeel Zanganeh And Antonio Lombardo
abstract:
Author(s): Esmaeel Zanganeh and Antonio Lombardo

Simultaneous control over the directionality and spin of light at the nanoscale is a central goal in nanophotonics with applications ranging from quantum information to advanced biosensing. We introduce the concept of the Circular Huygens dipole and numerically demonstrate its realization in a singl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185415] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the concept of a Circular Huygens dipole and numerically demonstrates its realization in a single achiral nanoparticle, enabling unidirectional emission with controllable spin angular momentum.
motivation: Simultaneous control of the direction and spin of light at the nanoscale is a long-standing goal in nanophotonics, with potential applications in quantum information and biosensing.
method: The authors analytically define the Circular Huygens dipole as a superposition of electric and magnetic dipole moments with a specific phase relation, and numerically simulate its scattering and emission properties in a single achiral nanoparticle.
result: The proposed configuration yields unidirectional radiation with a well-defined spin angular momentum, achieved without any chiral structuring of the nanoparticle.
conclusion: The Circular Huygens dipole provides a simple, achiral route to directional spin-controlled nanoscale light emission, potentially useful as a building block for photonic and quantum-photonic interfaces.

title: Vestigial Nematic Order At Zero Temperature In Two-dimensional Frustrated Quantum Antiferromagnets
authors: Matthew C. O'brien And Eduardo Fradkin
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew C. O'Brien and Eduardo Fradkin

Recent numerical advances have renewed interest in the two-dimensional quantum
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134414] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses semiclassical effective field theory and large-N analysis to show that overlooked interactions stabilize a quantum vestigial nematic phase at zero temperature in two-dimensional frustrated quantum antiferromagnets.
motivation: Recent numerical advances have renewed interest in the two-dimensional quantum Heisenberg antiferromagnet, but a detailed analytical theory has remained lacking.
method: The authors apply a semiclassical effective field theory and large-N analysis to study quantum fluctuations and symmetry breaking in frustrated quantum antiferromagnets.
result: They find a quantum vestigial nematic phase at zero temperature where discrete rotational symmetry is spontaneously broken despite the loss of long-range antiferromagnetic spiral order.
conclusion: This zero-temperature nematic phase continues the known finite-temperature nematic phase, reflecting enhanced quantum fluctuations near the classical Lifshitz point.

title: Partially Polarized Order In The Orthogonal Ising Shastry-Sutherland Magnet ${\mathrm{BaNd}}_{2}{\mathrm{PdS}}_{5}$
authors: Ying Fu, Qiye Liu, Han Ge, Nan Zhao, Tiantian Li, Fangli Li, Huanpeng Bu, Jiayue Yuan, Junyu Li, Jun-Feng Dai, Jieming Sheng, And Liusuo Wu
abstract:

We report a comprehensive study of single-crystal [MATH], a Shastry-Sutherland lattice (SSL) antiferromagnet. Thermodynamic and magnetization measurements identify an AFM transition at [MATH]. The [MATH] loca…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154410] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports an experimental study of the Shastry-Sutherland antiferromagnet BaNd2PdS5, identifying an antiferromagnetic transition and partially polarized order via thermodynamic and magnetization measurements.
motivation: The authors aim to investigate frustrated magnetism and orthogonal Ising anisotropy in the Shastry-Sutherland lattice, a model system of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: Single-crystal samples of BaNd2PdS5 were characterized using thermodynamic and magnetization measurements to probe magnetic ordering and anisotropic behavior.
result: An antiferromagnetic transition is observed, along with a partially polarized magnetic order that reveals the influence of orthogonal Ising anisotropy within the Shastry-Sutherland lattice.
conclusion: The findings provide experimental insight into the magnetic phase behavior of a rare-earth Shastry-Sutherland magnet, but the work is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics of information, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Three-dimensional Zigzag Correlations In The Van Der Waals Kitaev Magnet ${\mathrm{RuBr}}_{3}$
authors: H. Gretarsson, R. Iwazaki, F. Sato, H. Gotou, S. Francoual, J. Nasu, Y. Imai, K. Ohgushi, J. Chaloupka, B. Keimer, And H. Suzuki
abstract:
Author(s): H. Gretarsson, R. Iwazaki, F. Sato, H. Gotou, S. Francoual, J. Nasu, Y. Imai, K. Ohgushi, J. Chaloupka, B. Keimer, and H. Suzuki

Van der Waals materials can be exfoliated into ultrathin sheets, suggesting that their magnetism should also be two-dimensional. Using resonant x-ray scattering, the authors reveal here a different picture in the Kitaev magnet RuBr
[Phys. Rev. B 114, L140404] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: Resonant x-ray scattering reveals three-dimensional zigzag magnetic correlations in the van der Waals Kitaev magnet RuBr3, driven by extended Br 4p orbitals that enhance interlayer interactions.
motivation: Van der Waals materials are commonly assumed to host two-dimensional magnetism due to their layered structure, but this assumption may fail in Kitaev magnets where ligand chemistry can alter magnetic dimensionality.
method: The authors use resonant x-ray scattering to probe the magnetic correlations in single crystals of RuBr3, focusing on spectral weight redistribution along the interlayer direction.
result: They observe three-dimensional zigzag magnetic correlations with spectral weight redistribution along the interlayer direction, showing that bromine's spatially extended 4p orbitals strengthen interlayer magnetic interactions.
conclusion: The findings demonstrate that an exfoliable crystal can host three-dimensional magnetism, challenging a common assumption about layered quantum materials and highlighting how ligand chemistry controls magnetic dimensionality.

title: Interplay Of Flat-band And Anderson Localization In Disordered Moiré Superlattices
authors: Qian Liu, Xiaoshuang Xia, Junjie Wang, Peilong Hong, Lei Xu, Lujun Huang, Daohong Song, And Yi Liang
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Liu, Xiaoshuang Xia, Junjie Wang, Peilong Hong, Lei Xu, Lujun Huang, Daohong Song, and Yi Liang

Disorder in moiré superlattices simultaneously degrades flat-band localization and induces Anderson localization, yet how these two regimes interact has remained unclear. Here, we introduce a combined framework linking localization‐length scaling with differential probability density analysis to map…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144202] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a combined localization-length scaling and differential probability density framework to map how flat-band localization and Anderson localization interact in disordered moiré superlattices.
motivation: Disorder in moiré superlattices simultaneously destroys flat-band localization and induces Anderson localization, but the interplay between these two regimes has been poorly understood.
method: The authors introduce a framework that links localization-length scaling with differential probability density analysis to characterize the two localization mechanisms and their competition in disordered moiré superlattice models.
result: The analysis maps out the regimes where flat-band localization and Anderson localization coexist, compete, or transition into one another as a function of disorder strength.
conclusion: The work clarifies the phase behavior of disordered moiré flat-band systems, providing a diagnostic tool for distinguishing flat-band from disorder-induced localization.

title: Canonical Criterion For Third-order Transitions Identified By Microcanonical Inflection-point Analysis
authors: Fangfang Wang, Wei Liu, Kai Qi, Zidong Cui, Ying Tang, And Zengru Di
abstract:
Author(s): Fangfang Wang, Wei Liu, Kai Qi, Zidong Cui, Ying Tang, and Zengru Di

Microcanonical inflection-point analysis (MIPA) identifies third-order transitions from derivatives of the microcanonical entropy, yet this classification has lacked a direct canonical counterpart accessible from measurable fluctuations without reconstructing the density of states. Here we establish…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034118] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a canonical criterion for third-order phase transitions based on microcanonical inflection-point analysis, linking microcanonical entropy derivatives to measurable canonical fluctuations.
motivation: Microcanonical inflection-point analysis can identify third-order transitions, but a direct canonical counterpart using measurable fluctuations without reconstructing the density of states was missing.
method: The authors derive a canonical criterion from the microcanonical inflection points of the entropy, avoiding density-of-states reconstruction.
result: They show that third-order transitions manifest as specific features in canonical fluctuations, providing an experimentally accessible signature.
conclusion: This bridges microcanonical and canonical descriptions of third-order transitions and offers a practical tool for their identification.

title: Arbitrary Approximations Of First-passage-time Distributions In General Time-continuous Stochastic Processes
authors: Haowen Chen, Liying Zhou, Jiaqi Teng, Aimin Chen, And Tianshou Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Haowen Chen, Liying Zhou, Jiaqi Teng, Aimin Chen, and Tianshou Zhou

First-passage time (FPT) is an important quantity characterizing stochastic processes, but its distribution is often difficult to compute. Here we develop an efficient approach to compute the FPT distribution for a general stochastic process modeled by a master equation or a Fokker-Planck equation. …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034122] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an efficient method to approximate first-passage-time distributions for general stochastic processes governed by master or Fokker-Planck equations.
motivation: First-passage-time distributions are important for characterizing stochastic processes, but they are often difficult to compute exactly.
method: The authors propose a general computational approach to approximate the first-passage-time distribution for stochastic processes modeled by a master equation or a Fokker-Planck equation.
result: The method is demonstrated to efficiently compute first-passage-time distributions across arbitrary approximations for general time-continuous stochastic processes.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical tool for studying first-passage phenomena in diverse stochastic systems, though its direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is limited.

title: Emergence Of Generic First-passage-time Distributions For Large Markovian Networks
authors: Julian B. Voits And Ulrich S. Schwarz
abstract:
Author(s): Julian B. Voits and Ulrich S. Schwarz

First-passage-times are often the most relevant aspect of a complex Markovian network because they signify when information processing has resulted in a definite decision. Previous studies have shown that for kinetic proofreading networks in the limit of large network size the first-passage-time dis…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034311] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies first-passage-time distributions in large Markovian networks and identifies generic emergent distributions in the large-network limit.
motivation: First-passage times determine when information processing in complex Markovian networks results in a definite decision, but their distributions for large generic networks are not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze first-passage-time distributions for large Markovian networks, extending previous results on kinetic proofreading networks and deriving general asymptotic forms.
result: They show that for large Markovian networks, generic first-passage-time distributions emerge that are largely independent of the specific network details.
conclusion: The work provides general principles for first-passage statistics in complex stochastic networks, with potential applications to decision-making in biological and chemical information processing.

title: Theory Of $β$ Relaxation Beyond Mode-coupling Theory: A Microscopic Treatment
authors: Corentin C. L. Laudicina, Liesbeth M. C. Janssen, And Grzegorz Szamel
abstract:
Author(s): Corentin C. L. Laudicina, Liesbeth M. C. Janssen, and Grzegorz Szamel

We develop a systematic extension of mode-coupling theory that incorporates critical dynamical fluctuations. Starting from a microscopic diagrammatic theory, we identify dominant classes of divergent diagrams near the mode-coupling transition and show that the corresponding asymptotic series dominat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035411] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends mode-coupling theory with critical dynamical fluctuations to microscopically describe β relaxation in glass-forming systems beyond standard MCT.
motivation: Mode-coupling theory captures the ideal glass transition but fails to describe the secondary β relaxation quantitatively, motivating a more complete microscopic treatment.
method: The authors start from a microscopic diagrammatic theory and classify divergent diagrammatic contributions near the mode-coupling transition, resumming the dominant asymptotic series.
result: They identify the dominant classes of divergent diagrams and derive an extended asymptotic description that improves on standard MCT predictions for β relaxation.
conclusion: The approach provides a systematic microscopic framework for going beyond mode-coupling theory in describing glassy relaxation dynamics.

title: Scalable Quantum Algorithm For Meson Scattering In A Lattice Gauge Theory
authors: Yahui Chai, Yibin Guo, And Stefan Kühn
abstract:
Author(s): Yahui Chai, Yibin Guo, and Stefan Kühn

Scattering processes are essential for understanding the structure of matter, yet their real-time dynamics remain challenging to simulate classically. Quantum computers offer a promising path toward efficient simulation of such physical systems. Here, we present a general and scalable framework for …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033298] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A scalable quantum algorithm is proposed for simulating real-time meson scattering dynamics in a lattice gauge theory.
motivation: Real-time scattering dynamics in gauge theories are classically intractable, motivating quantum simulation approaches.
method: The authors develop a general scalable quantum algorithm framework tailored to meson scattering in lattice gauge theory.
result: The framework enables efficient quantum simulation of meson scattering processes, though specific performance metrics are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: This work provides a quantum computing approach for studying scattering in gauge theories, but it lies outside the user's specified research directions.

title: Hong-Ou-Mandel Two-photon X-ray States
authors: Liam T. Powers And Stephen M. Durbin
abstract:
Author(s): Liam T. Powers and Stephen M. Durbin

Hong-Ou-Mandel interference has now been observed with pairs of indistinguishable x-rays from a high-brightness synchrotron source, using a thin silicon crystal beam splitter.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032042] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Researchers observe Hong-Ou-Mandel interference between indistinguishable X-ray photon pairs using a thin silicon crystal beam splitter.
motivation: Hong-Ou-Mandel interference is a hallmark of quantum indistinguishability, but it had not been demonstrated at X-ray wavelengths.
method: They use a high-brightness synchrotron source to generate X-ray photon pairs and a thin silicon crystal as a beam splitter, measuring coincidence counts.
result: A Hong-Ou-Mandel dip is observed, confirming two-photon interference with X-rays.
conclusion: This extends HOM interference to the X-ray regime, opening possibilities for X-ray quantum optics.

title: Boltzmann Sampling Of Frustrated ${J}_{1}\text{−}{J}_{2}$ Ising Models With Programmable Quantum Annealers
authors: Elijah Pelofske
abstract:
Author(s): Elijah Pelofske

One of the surprising, and potentially very useful, capabilities of analog quantum computers, such as D-Wave quantum annealers, is sampling from the Boltzmann, or Gibbs, distribution defined by a classical Hamiltonian. In this study, we thoroughly examine the ability of D-Wave quantum annealers to s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033280] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper examines the ability of D-Wave quantum annealers to sample from Boltzmann/Gibbs distributions defined by frustrated J1-J2 Ising models.
motivation: Quantum annealers have the potential to efficiently sample from thermal distributions, which could be useful for optimization and statistical physics, but their accuracy for frustrated systems is not well understood.
method: The author uses D-Wave programmable quantum annealers to sample from frustrated J1-J2 Ising models and analyzes the resulting distributions against theoretical Boltzmann distributions.
result: The study characterizes the sampling performance, revealing limitations and capabilities of current quantum annealers for Boltzmann sampling of frustrated Ising models.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the practical use of quantum annealers for Boltzmann sampling, but the work is primarily an application on quantum annealing hardware and does not advance the research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Dynamic Interaction Between Chiral Currents And Surface Waves In Topological Superfluid
authors: S. Forstner, H. Choi, G. I. Harris, A. Sawadsky, W. P. Bowen, And C. G. Baker
abstract:
Author(s): S. Forstner, H. Choi, G. I. Harris, A. Sawadsky, W. P. Bowen, and C. G. Baker

Despite extensive experimental efforts over the past two decades, topological superconductivity and Majorana fermions have remained elusive. By shifting focus from superconductors—whose topological nature is often debated—to the well-established [MATH]-wave superfluid [MATH], we propose an e…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033275] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using surface waves in a topological superfluid to dynamically probe chiral currents, aiming to overcome difficulties in observing Majorana fermions in topological superconductors.
motivation: Topological superconductivity and Majorana fermions have been sought for decades but remain experimentally elusive, with the topological nature of many superconductor candidates under debate.
method: The authors shift focus to a well-established p-wave superfluid (likely 3He) and propose an experiment that couples chiral edge currents to surface acoustic waves to detect their interaction.
result: The proposal is expected to reveal signatures of chiral currents and topological order through surface-wave spectroscopy, though explicit results are not fully detailed in the truncated abstract.
conclusion: The work suggests that topological superfluids offer a cleaner platform for studying Majorana physics and chiral edge states, potentially guiding future experiments.

title: Geometrically Frustrated Quadrupoles On The Pyrochlore Lattice And Generalized Spin Liquids
authors: Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, And Paul Mcclarty
abstract:
Author(s): Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, and Paul McClarty

A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors, showing how angular-momentum-dependent geometries dictate generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated magnets.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031065] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors to investigate generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice.
motivation: To understand how angular-momentum-dependent geometries in frustrated magnets give rise to exotic states like quadrupolar spin liquids and generalized nematic phases.
method: Semiclassical approach treating quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors on the pyrochlore lattice.
result: The geometry of the lattice and the angular-momentum dependence dictate the emergence of generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids.
conclusion: The work provides insights into frustrated magnetism and generalized spin liquids, highlighting the role of geometric frustration in quadrupolar systems.

title: Pseudogap, Fermi Liquid, Van Hove Singularity, And Maxima Of The Compressibility And Of The Knight Shift As A Function Of Doping In The Two-Dimensional Hubbard Model
authors: Y. M. Vilk And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:
Author(s): Y. M. Vilk and A.-M. S. Tremblay

Analysis of Hubbard model simulations reveals that a maximum in the isothermal compressibility marks the pseudogap boundary, driven by spin-density-wave precursor bands crossing the zero-frequency level.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031034] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: Analysis of two-dimensional Hubbard model simulations links a maximum in isothermal compressibility to the pseudogap boundary and identifies spin-density-wave precursor bands crossing the zero-frequency level.
motivation: The paper aims to clarify the nature of the pseudogap regime in cuprate-like systems by connecting transport and thermodynamic signatures, such as compressibility and Knight shift, to underlying electronic structure in the Hubbard model.
method: The authors analyze numerical simulations of the two-dimensional Hubbard model, focusing on the doping dependence of the isothermal compressibility, Knight shift, and the role of Van Hove singularities and Fermi-liquid behavior.
result: They find that a maximum in the isothermal compressibility marks the pseudogap boundary, driven by spin-density-wave precursor bands crossing the zero-frequency level, which also produces corresponding maxima in the Knight shift.
conclusion: The work suggests that pseudogap phenomena in the Hubbard model can be understood through the doping evolution of compressibility and spin susceptibility, providing a framework for interpreting experimental data in strongly correlated electron systems.

title: Riemannian Geometric Classification And Emergent Phenomena Of Magnetic Textures
authors: Koki Shinada And Naoto Nagaosa
abstract:
Author(s): Koki Shinada and Naoto Nagaosa

A classification framework based on differential geometry introduces geodesic and torsional scalar spin chiralities, revealing a quantum geometric effect that modifies electron equations of motion in complex magnetic textures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031026] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a Riemannian geometric classification of magnetic textures using geodesic and torsional scalar spin chiralities, revealing quantum geometric effects on electron equations of motion.
motivation: Magnetic textures host nontrivial spin configurations whose geometric classification and impact on electron dynamics remain incompletely understood, motivating a differential-geometric framework.
method: The authors introduce geodesic and torsional scalar spin chiralities within a Riemannian geometric classification and derive modifications to electron equations of motion in complex magnetic textures.
result: The framework classifies magnetic textures geometrically and identifies quantum geometric contributions that alter electronic transport through spin chirality effects.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric classification and emergent phenomena framework for magnetic textures, with potential implications for spintronics and topological magnetism.

title: Deceleration Of Accelerator-Produced And In-Trap Electron Cooling Of Highly Charged Ions
authors: S. Rausch, Z. Andelkovic, S. Fedotova, W. Geithner, F. Herfurth, M. Horst, J. Ködel, K. Mohr, D. Neidherr, W. Nörtershäuser, N. Stallkamp, S. Trotsenko, G. Vorobjev, And D. Zisis
abstract:
Author(s): S. Rausch, Z. Andelkovic, S. Fedotova, W. Geithner, F. Herfurth, M. Horst, J. Ködel, K. Mohr, D. Neidherr, W. Nörtershäuser, N. Stallkamp, S. Trotsenko, G. Vorobjev, and D. Zisis

The electron cooling of highly charged ions (HCI) in a Penning trap, as well as the deceleration and trapping of accelerator-produced HCI, has been demonstrated at the HITRAP facility, paving the way for unprecedented precision experiments in QED, materials science, and astrophysics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031022] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates electron cooling and deceleration/trapping of accelerator-produced highly charged ions in a Penning trap at HITRAP for precision QED, materials science, and astrophysics experiments.
motivation: Highly charged ions are valuable for precision tests, but accelerator-produced HCI must be decelerated and cooled for trapping and high-precision measurements.
method: Electron cooling in a Penning trap and deceleration/trapping of HCI beams at the HITRAP facility.
result: Successful electron cooling of HCI in-trap and deceleration/trapping of accelerator-produced HCI were demonstrated.
conclusion: The work enables unprecedented precision experiments in QED, materials science, and astrophysics using trapped HCI.

title: Non-Hermitian Bethe-Salpeter Equation For Open Systems: Emergence Of Exceptional Points In Excitonic Spectra From First Principles
authors: Zhenlin Zhang, Wei Hu, Enrico Perfetto, And Gianluca Stefanucci
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenlin Zhang, Wei Hu, Enrico Perfetto, and Gianluca Stefanucci

Extension of the Bethe-Salpeter equation to open quantum systems predicts that engineered photonic environments induce exceptional points in the excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides, providing a pathway for non-Hermitian quantum devices with controllable optical and valleytronic properties.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031020] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: A non-Hermitian extension of the Bethe-Salpeter equation reveals exceptional points in excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides in engineered photonic environments.
motivation: To understand how open quantum systems and non-Hermitian physics can be exploited for novel quantum devices with controllable optical and valleytronic properties.
method: They develop a non-Hermitian Bethe-Salpeter equation for open systems and apply it to first-principles calculations of excitonic spectra in TMDs coupled to photonic environments.
result: They predict the emergence of exceptional points in the excitonic spectra, tunable via the photonic environment.
conclusion: This provides a pathway for non-Hermitian quantum devices with controllable optical and valleytronic properties.

title: Imaginary Time Evolution And Ground State Preparation Using Unitary Multi-Copy Protocols
authors: Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, And H. R. Sadeghpour
abstract:
Author(s): Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, and H. R. Sadeghpour

Real-time evolution and sᴡᴀᴘ operations are combined to efficiently suppress excited-state populations using multiple copies of the quantum system.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033033] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes unitary multi-copy protocols that combine real-time evolution and SWAP operations to suppress excited-state populations for ground-state preparation.
motivation: Ground-state preparation is a key task for quantum simulation, but implementing non-unitary imaginary-time evolution on quantum computers is challenging.
method: They use multiple copies of the quantum system and combine real-time evolution with SWAP operations to simulate imaginary-time evolution effects unitarily.
result: The protocol efficiently suppresses excited-state populations, enabling ground-state preparation without post-selection.
conclusion: This offers a practical unitary approach to ground-state preparation that may be implemented on near-term quantum devices.

title: Two-dimensional Quantum-lattice-gas Algorithm For Anisotropic Burger-like Equations
authors: Niccoló Fonio, Pierre Sagaut, And Giuseppe Di Molfetta
abstract:
Author(s): Niccoló Fonio, Pierre Sagaut, and Giuseppe Di Molfetta

Building on hybrid quantum lattice gas algorithm, we revisit the possibilities of this quantum lattice model. By deriving a correction to the predicted viscosity, we provide analytical and numerical results that refine original formulation. We introduce a minimal two-dimensional generalization of th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032426] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends a hybrid quantum lattice-gas algorithm to two-dimensional anisotropic Burger-like equations and derives a corrected viscosity prediction.
motivation: Quantum lattice-gas algorithms offer a route to simulate fluid dynamics on quantum computers, but existing formulations need refined viscosity models and higher-dimensional generalizations.
method: The authors analytically derive a correction to the predicted viscosity and introduce a minimal two-dimensional generalization of the quantum lattice-gas model, supported by numerical simulations.
result: The corrected formulation improves agreement with expected viscous behavior, and the 2D extension reproduces anisotropic Burger-like dynamics in numerical tests.
conclusion: This work refines quantum lattice-gas algorithms for fluid equations, though it remains outside the core quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, and hybrid-systems interests.

title: Fate Of Moiré Flat Bands For A Weakly Repulsive Bose-Einstein Condensate In One-dimensional $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Bichromatic Optical Lattices
authors: Enhong Cheng, Yu Tan, Yanzhen Xu, And Li-Jun Lang
abstract:
Author(s): Enhong Cheng, Yu Tan, Yanzhen Xu, and Li-Jun Lang

One-dimensional (1D) superlattices provide one simplified platform for exploring moiré physics from a low-dimensional perspective, with the ratio of lattice constants playing a role analogous to the twist angle in two-dimensional bilayers. Here we propose a 1D [MATH]-symmetric bichromatic op…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033310] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the fate of moiré flat bands for a weakly repulsive Bose-Einstein condensate in one-dimensional PT-symmetric bichromatic optical lattices.
motivation: One-dimensional superlattices provide a simplified platform for exploring moiré physics from a low-dimensional perspective, with the ratio of lattice constants playing a role analogous to the twist angle in two-dimensional bilayers.
method: The authors theoretically propose and analyze a 1D PT-symmetric bichromatic optical lattice hosting a weakly repulsive Bose-Einstein condensate, likely using mean-field or Gross-Pitaevskii formalism.
result: The study reveals how moiré flat bands emerge or are modified in the presence of PT symmetry and weak repulsive interactions in this 1D superlattice setting.
conclusion: The work provides insights into moiré flat-band physics in low-dimensional PT-symmetric systems with interacting bosons, relevant to ultracold-atom platforms.

title: Effective Scattering And Universal Clusters Of Heteronuclear Ultracold Mixtures In Quasi-low Dimensions
authors: Tingting Shi And Xiaoling Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Tingting Shi and Xiaoling Cui

We study the effective [MATH]-wave scattering of two heteronuclear atoms harmonically confined in quasi-low dimensions, where the atoms have unequal masses and are subject to different confinement frequencies. The resulting effective scattering parameters in low dimensions, including scattering length …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033311] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives effective scattering parameters and universal cluster properties for harmonically confined heteronuclear ultracold atomic mixtures in quasi-low-dimensional geometries.
motivation: Heteronuclear mixtures with unequal masses and different confinement frequencies in quasi-1D/2D traps are experimentally relevant, but their low-dimensional effective interactions are not fully characterized.
method: The authors solve the two-body scattering problem for two heteronuclear atoms under harmonic confinement with unequal masses and trapping frequencies, extracting effective scattering lengths and related parameters.
result: They obtain the effective scattering parameters in low dimensions and identify universal cluster states emerging from the interplay of mass imbalance and anisotropic confinement.
conclusion: The results provide a systematic framework for describing interactions and few-body clustering in quasi-low-dimensional heteronuclear cold-atom systems.

title: Magnetism In Antiperovskite $({\mathrm{Li}}_{2}M)Ch\mathrm{O}$ ($M=\mathrm{Fe},\mathrm{Mn},\mathrm{Co}; Ch=\mathrm{S},\mathrm{Se}$) Diluted Magnets With Fixed 1/3 Filling: The Key Role Of Magnetic Anisotropy
authors: J. Zheng, F. L. Carstens, L. Singer, M. A. A. Mohamed, L. Bischof, A. Alfonsov, J. Arneth, S. Hampel, N. Gräßler, And R. Klingeler
abstract:
Author(s): J. Zheng, F. L. Carstens, L. Singer, M. A. A. Mohamed, L. Bischof, A. Alfonsov, J. Arneth, S. Hampel, N. Gräßler, and R. Klingeler

We report the magnetic properties of a series of lithium-rich antiperovskites ([MATH] ([MATH] and [MATH]), where transition metal and lithium ions are randomly distributed on the X sites of the ${}_{3}\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144413] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports an experimental and theoretical study of the magnetic properties of lithium-rich antiperovskite diluted magnets (Li2M)ChO (M = Fe, Mn, Co; Ch = S, Se) with fixed 1/3 filling, highlighting the central role of magnetic anisotropy.
motivation: Antiperovskite diluted magnets with transition-metal and lithium ions randomly distributed on the X sites offer a tunable platform for studying frustrated magnetism and anisotropic exchange, but their magnetic behavior is not well characterized.
method: A series of polycrystalline samples was synthesized and characterized via magnetization, susceptibility, and related magnetic measurements, complemented by analysis of the local structure and magnetic anisotropy.
result: The compounds exhibit diluted-magnet behavior at 1/3 filling where magnetic anisotropy, rather than simple dilution effects, dominates the magnetic ordering and response.
conclusion: Magnetic anisotropy is identified as the key parameter controlling magnetism in these antiperovskite diluted magnets, providing guidance for designing related frustrated or dilute magnetic materials.

title: Evidence For Interior-gap Pair Density Wave State In Kondo-Heisenberg Chains
authors: Yuto Hirose, Shunsuke C. Furuya, And Yasuhiro Tada
abstract:
Author(s): Yuto Hirose, Shunsuke C. Furuya, and Yasuhiro Tada

Interior-gap superconductivity has long been discussed as an exotic paired state in the presence of Fermi-surface mismatch, but its realization in canonical strongly correlated models has remained elusive. Here we present evidence that the superconducting phase of one-dimensional Kondo-Heisenberg mo…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154506] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents evidence for an interior-gap pair density wave superconducting state in one-dimensional Kondo-Heisenberg chains.
motivation: Interior-gap superconductivity is an exotic paired state expected under Fermi-surface mismatch, but its realization in canonical strongly correlated models has remained elusive.
method: The authors study the superconducting phase of a one-dimensional Kondo-Heisenberg model, presumably using analytical field-theoretic and/or numerical techniques to identify the pairing structure.
result: They find evidence that the superconducting phase realizes an interior-gap pair density wave state, characterized by an order parameter that is non-uniform in space.
conclusion: The Kondo-Heisenberg chain provides a canonical strongly correlated setting where interior-gap pair density wave superconductivity can be realized, linking this exotic state to a well-studied model.

title: Lattice Dynamics And Thermoelectric Transport In $M\mathrm{Ag}C{h}_{2}$ ($M=\mathrm{Sc}$, Y; $Ch=\mathrm{S}$, Se, Te): Role Of Anharmonic Phonons And Ag-sublattice Vibrations
authors: Shanza Tariq, Hao-Jen You, Rovi Angelo Beloya Villaos, Ina Marie R. Verzola, Zhi-Quan Huang, Junsoo Park, Hsin Lin, And Feng-Chuan Chuang
abstract:
Author(s): Shanza Tariq, Hao-Jen You, Rovi Angelo Beloya Villaos, Ina Marie R. Verzola, Zhi-Quan Huang, Junsoo Park, Hsin Lin, and Feng-Chuan Chuang

The interplay between chemical bonding, lattice anharmonicity, and thermal transport plays a central role in determining the thermoelectric performance of crystalline solids. Here, we systematically investigate the structural stability, lattice dynamics, thermal transport, and thermoelectric propert…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165201] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A first-principles study of lattice dynamics, anharmonic phonons, and thermoelectric transport in the MAgCh2 (M=Sc, Y; Ch=S, Se, Te) family of crystalline solids.
motivation: Understanding how chemical bonding, lattice anharmonicity, and Ag-sublattice vibrations govern thermal transport is key to optimizing thermoelectric performance in crystalline materials.
method: Density functional theory calculations combined with phonon and anharmonic lattice-dynamics analysis are used to compute structural stability, thermal transport, and thermoelectric properties.
result: The study identifies the roles of anharmonic phonons and Ag-sublattice vibrations in suppressing lattice thermal conductivity across the MAgCh2 series.
conclusion: The interplay of anharmonicity and sublattice dynamics provides design guidance for improving thermoelectric efficiency in these compounds.

title: Signatures Of Dynes Density Of States In The Terahertz Response Of Atomic Layer Deposition Grown Superconducting NbN Thin Films
authors: Frederik Bolle, Yayi Lin, Ozan Saritas, Martin Dressel, Ciprian Padurariu, Sahitya Varma Vegesna, Nitesh Yerra, Heidemarie Krüger, And Marc Scheffler
abstract:
Author(s): Frederik Bolle, Yayi Lin, Ozan Saritas, Martin Dressel, Ciprian Padurariu, Sahitya Varma Vegesna, Nitesh Yerra, Heidemarie Krüger, and Marc Scheffler

The frequency-dependent complex optical conductivity [MATH] reflects key properties of superconductors, such as the energy gap [MATH] in the density of states (DOS) and the superfluid density [MATH]. For disordered superconductors, [MATH] often can be d…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144505] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: Terahertz spectroscopy of ALD-grown superconducting NbN thin films reveals signatures of a Dynes-type broadening of the superconducting density of states in disordered films.
motivation: Disordered superconductors often show a smeared gap in the density of states that is not captured by BCS theory, and understanding how this manifests in the optical response is important for characterizing such materials.
method: Frequency-dependent complex optical conductivity was measured in the THz range on atomic layer deposition grown NbN thin films and analyzed within a Dynes density-of-states framework.
result: The measured THz conductivity spectra are consistent with a Dynes broadening parameter describing subgap states, allowing extraction of the gap and superfluid density for the disordered films.
conclusion: The work establishes THz conductivity as a sensitive probe of disorder-induced subgap states in superconducting NbN films, relevant to material quality assessment for superconducting devices.

title: Scaling Law For Subdiffusive-to-diffusive Transition Time In Heterogeneous Nonequilibrium Systems
authors: Ming-Gen Li, He-Chuan Liu, Ling-Ling Du, Peng-Cheng Li, And Li-Ming Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Ming-Gen Li, He-Chuan Liu, Ling-Ling Du, Peng-Cheng Li, and Li-Ming Fan

The transition from subdiffusion to normal diffusion is ubiquitous in complex systems, with experimentally observed transition times spanning several orders of magnitude. However, a scaling law governing the transition time remains unclear. To address this issue, we introduce an analytically tractab…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L032103] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a scaling law for the transition time from subdiffusive to normal diffusive behavior in heterogeneous nonequilibrium systems using an analytically tractable model.
motivation: The subdiffusion-to-normal-diffusion transition is ubiquitous in complex systems, yet the scaling of its transition time remains unclear despite experimentally observed orders-of-magnitude variation.
method: An analytically tractable model of heterogeneous nonequilibrium media is introduced and analyzed to extract the scaling behavior of the subdiffusive-to-diffusive transition time.
result: A scaling law is obtained that relates the transition time to system parameters, offering a general explanation for the broad range of observed transition times.
conclusion: The proposed scaling law provides a unifying framework for understanding and predicting transition times across diverse heterogeneous systems.

title: Faster-than-adiabatic Cooling Of Non-neutral Plasmas
authors: Jan Bartsch, Alfio Borzì, Paul-Antoine Hervieux, And Giovanni Manfredi
abstract:
Author(s): Jan Bartsch, Alfio Borzì, Paul-Antoine Hervieux, and Giovanni Manfredi

This paper proposes an optimal control strategy to cool an antiproton plasma in a time much shorter than that required by an adiabatic process. The authors examine the length and stability of the plasma, in addition to its duration. The work suggests that optimal control techniques may be useful for experiments with plasmas, in particular with antimatter plasmas, which need to be confined and cooled before significant losses and annihilation occur.

#TimelyTopic #TechnicalAdvancement #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035208] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an optimal control strategy to cool an antiproton plasma much faster than adiabatic cooling while maintaining plasma stability and length.
motivation: Antimatter plasmas must be rapidly confined and cooled before significant particle losses and annihilation occur.
method: Optimal control theory is used to design a cooling protocol for non-neutral plasma dynamics that outperforms standard adiabatic cooling.
result: The strategy achieves faster-than-adiabatic cooling, with analysis of plasma length, stability, and cooling duration.
conclusion: Optimal control techniques may be useful for plasma experiments, especially those involving antimatter plasmas that require fast cooling.

title: Optimality And Annealing Path Planning Of Dynamical Analog Solvers
authors: Shu Zhou, K. Y. Michael Wong, Juntao Wang, David Shui Wing Hui, Daniel Ebler, And Jie Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Shu Zhou, K. Y. Michael Wong, Juntao Wang, David Shui Wing Hui, Daniel Ebler, and Jie Sun

Recently proposed analog solvers based on dynamical systems, such as Ising machines, are promising platforms for large-scale combinatorial optimization. Yet, given the heuristic nature of the field, there is very limited insight on optimality guarantees of the solvers, as well as how parameter sched…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033267] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optimality guarantees and annealing path planning for dynamical analog solvers such as Ising machines used in combinatorial optimization.
motivation: Analog solvers are promising for large-scale combinatorial optimization, but their heuristic nature leaves limited theoretical understanding of optimality and parameter scheduling.
method: The authors analyze dynamical analog solvers theoretically and develop annealing path planning strategies to improve optimization performance.
result: They provide insights into optimality guarantees and propose methods for planning annealing schedules in analog solvers.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of analog optimization platforms, though it lies outside the core quantum information and thermodynamics interests.

title: Spin Inertia As A Source Of Topological Magnons: Chiral Edge States From Coupled Precession And Nutation
authors: Subhadip Ghosh, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Ritwik Mondal, Alexander Mook, And Levente Rózsa
abstract:
Author(s): Subhadip Ghosh, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Ritwik Mondal, Alexander Mook, and Levente Rózsa

It is shown on the example of a honeycomb ferromagnet that spin inertia hybridizes the precessional and nutational magnon bands, opening a topologically nontrivial gap whose size scales linearly with the strength of pseudodipolar interaction. Chern number calculations and spectra calculated in a slab geometry demonstrate the emergence of chiral edge modes within this gap.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032040] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: Spin inertia in a honeycomb ferromagnet hybridizes precessional and nutational magnon bands, opening a topologically nontrivial gap with chiral edge modes.
motivation: The paper aims to show that spin inertia can serve as a source of topological magnons by coupling precession and nutation dynamics.
method: The authors use a honeycomb ferromagnet model with spin inertia and pseudodipolar interaction, compute magnon band structures, Chern numbers, and slab-geometry spectra.
result: A topologically nontrivial gap appears whose size scales linearly with pseudodipolar interaction strength, and chiral edge modes emerge within the gap.
conclusion: Spin inertia provides a mechanism for topological magnonics and chiral edge-state engineering in ferromagnets.

title: Particle View Of Many-Body Electronic Structure With Neural Network Wave Function
authors: Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, And Ji Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, and Ji Chen

A combination of theoretical approaches bridges the gap between complex quantum wave functions and the classical picture of electron positions for molecules and solids.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031048] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network many-body wave function approach is used to extract a semiclassical 'particle view' of electron positions in molecules and solids, bridging quantum wave functions and classical electronic-structure pictures.
motivation: Understanding many-body electronic structure in terms of intuitive particle-like descriptions is difficult because accurate wave functions are highly complex and high-dimensional, especially for strongly correlated molecules and solids.
method: The authors combine neural-network variational wave functions (deep-learning-based ansatz for the many-body electronic state) with theoretical tools that map the wave function onto distributions of electron positions, extracting a particle-like picture of the electronic structure.
result: The approach is demonstrated on molecules and solids, showing that neural-network wave functions can yield interpretable particle-level descriptions of electronic structure that connect to classical chemical intuition and reproduce accurate energies/properties.
conclusion: Neural-network wave functions offer a practical route to both high accuracy and interpretability in many-body electronic structure, suggesting a bridge between machine-learning quantum chemistry and classical electronic-structure pictures.

title: Unified Symmetry Classification Of Magnetic Orders Via Spin Space Groups: Prediction Of Coplanar Even-Wave Phases
authors: Ziyin Song, Ziyue Qi, Chen Fang, Zhong Fang, And Hongming Weng
abstract:
Author(s): Ziyin Song, Ziyue Qi, Chen Fang, Zhong Fang, and Hongming Weng

A unified classification framework based on spin space group symmetry predicts a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase where electronic band spin polarization varies continuously and can vanish without band degeneracy.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031038] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: A unified symmetry classification of magnetic orders using spin space groups predicts a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase with continuously varying, potentially vanishing band spin polarization.
motivation: Magnetic orders in solids require a systematic symmetry-based classification, and spin space groups offer a broader framework than conventional magnetic space groups for capturing spin-lattice coupled orderings.
method: The authors construct a unified classification framework based on spin space group symmetry and apply it to enumerate allowed magnetic phases, identifying a novel coplanar even-wave phase.
result: The classification predicts a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase in which electronic band spin polarization varies continuously and can vanish without requiring band degeneracy.
conclusion: Spin space group symmetry provides a powerful organizing principle for magnetic order classification and reveals previously unrecognized phase types, though the work remains within condensed matter band theory.

title: Phonons Reflect Dynamic Spin-State Order In ${\mathrm{LaCoO}}_{3}$
authors: Alsu Ivashko, Taishun Manjo, Maximilian Kauth, Yuliia Tymoshenko, Adrian M. Merritt, Klaus-Peter Bohnen, Rolf Heid, Michael Merz, Andreas Eich, John-Paul Castellan, Alexandre Ivanov, Nathaniel Schreiber, Hong Zheng, J. F. Mitchell, Martin Meven, Jitae T. Park, Daisuke Ishikawa, Yuiga Nakamura, Alfred Q. R. Baron, And Frank Weber
abstract:

Merritt, Klaus-Peter Bohnen, Rolf Heid, Michael Merz, Andreas Eich, John-Paul Castellan, Alexandre Ivanov, Nathaniel Schreiber, Hong Zheng, J. F. Mitchell, Martin Meven, Jitae T. Park, Daisuke Ishikawa, Yuiga Nakamura, Alfred Q. R. Baron, and Frank Weber

We investigate lattice dynamics in [MATH] using inelastic neutron and x-ray scattering over [MATH], spanning the spin-state crossover at [MATH] and the insulator-metal transition at ${}_{2}≈550\te…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116101] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses inelastic neutron and x-ray scattering to study phonon dynamics in LaCoO3 across its spin-state crossover and insulator-metal transition.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between lattice dynamics, spin-state ordering, and electronic transitions in correlated oxides such as LaCoO3 is a central problem in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors measure phonon dispersions and temperature-dependent spectra using inelastic neutron and x-ray scattering, and analyze the data to extract changes in lattice dynamics across the spin-state crossover and insulator-metal transition.
result: The phonon spectra reflect dynamic spin-state order, showing anomalous temperature dependence and mode renormalization tied to the spin-state crossover and the insulator-metal transition.
conclusion: The findings establish phonons as sensitive probes of dynamic spin-state order and reveal strong spin-lattice coupling in LaCoO3, with implications for understanding correlated electron systems.

title: Controllable Quantum Phase Transitions And Frustrated Spin Responses In Multiferroic FeS Nanotubes
authors: Chi Ding, Tao Yang, Qing Lu, Yu Han, Yijie Zhu, Junjie Wang, Rui Wang, Hui-Tian Wang, Dingyu Xing, And Jian Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Chi Ding, Tao Yang, Qing Lu, Yu Han, Yijie Zhu, Junjie Wang, Rui Wang, Hui-Tian Wang, Dingyu Xing, and Jian Sun

Geometric frustration drives exotic quantum phases and transitions in condensed matter. One-dimensional frustrated magnets with inherent controllability are particularly promising for studying fundamental quantum physics, yet experimentally tunable systems remain scarce. Here, using first-principles…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116402] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of controllable quantum phase transitions and frustrated spin responses in multiferroic FeS nanotubes.
motivation: Geometric frustration in one-dimensional magnets can host exotic quantum phases, but experimentally tunable frustrated systems are rare, motivating the search for controllable platforms.
method: First-principles (DFT-based) calculations are used to characterize the electronic, magnetic, and multiferroic properties of FeS nanotubes and their response to external control parameters.
result: The work identifies tunable quantum phase transitions and frustrated spin behavior in FeS nanotubes, showing how geometry and external fields govern the magnetic ground states.
conclusion: Multiferroic FeS nanotubes are proposed as a controllable platform for studying frustrated magnetism and quantum phase transitions in one dimension.

title: Mechanical Sensing Of Metamagnetic Tricriticality In Two-Dimensional ${\text{CrI}}_{3}$
authors: Feng Liu, Tong Luo, Xiaokai Wu, Jiayong Xiao, Xiao Yan Xu, Shengwei Jiang, Kin Fai Mak, And Jie Shan
abstract:
Author(s): Feng Liu, Tong Luo, Xiaokai Wu, Jiayong Xiao, Xiao Yan Xu, Shengwei Jiang, Kin Fai Mak, and Jie Shan

Layered Ising metamagnets are antiferromagnetic (AF) materials consisting of monolayer Ising ferromagnets coupled to each other via interlayer AF interactions. They exhibit rich magnetic phase diagrams, featuring tricritical and critical end points, due to the competing magnetic interactions and the…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116708] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Mechanical sensing is used to probe metamagnetic tricriticality in the layered Ising antiferromagnet CrI3.
motivation: Layered Ising metamagnets such as CrI3 exhibit rich magnetic phase diagrams with tricritical and critical end points due to competing interlayer antiferromagnetic interactions, motivating sensitive probes of these transitions.
method: The authors employ mechanical sensing techniques to detect the magnetic phase transitions and map the tricritical behavior in two-dimensional CrI3.
result: The mechanical measurements reveal signatures of metamagnetic tricriticality, providing a phase diagram consistent with theoretical expectations for layered Ising metamagnets.
conclusion: Mechanical sensing offers a sensitive and versatile approach to studying complex magnetic phase transitions in two-dimensional van der Waals materials.

title: Spin-to-Charge Conversion Driven By Inverse Chiral-Induced Spin Selectivity
authors: Tian-Yi Zhang, Peng-Yi Liu, Ai-Min Guo, And Qing-Feng Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Tian-Yi Zhang, Peng-Yi Liu, Ai-Min Guo, and Qing-Feng Sun

Chiral molecules have attracted significant multidisciplinary interest and extensive research owing to their remarkable ability to achieve charge-to-spin conversion, known as the chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS). A recent experiment has revealed that chiral molecules also exhibit an unexpected…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 118001] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spin-to-charge conversion driven by the inverse chiral-induced spin selectivity effect in chiral molecular systems.
motivation: Chiral molecules are known for charge-to-spin conversion via CISS, but the reverse process and its microscopic mechanisms remain less understood.
method: The authors likely employ quantum transport or model calculations to analyze spin-to-charge conversion in chiral molecule junctions or systems.
result: They demonstrate that inverse CISS can drive spin-to-charge conversion, revealing conditions and mechanisms for the effect.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of CISS and suggest potential applications in spintronic devices based on chiral molecules.

title: Muonium Spectroscopy As A Quantum Sensor For Axion Dark Matter
authors: Feng Fang, Kim Siang Khaw, Ce Zhang, Qiaoli Yang, Liangwen Chen, Jie Yang, Lei Yang, And Zhiyu Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Feng Fang, Kim Siang Khaw, Ce Zhang, Qiaoli Yang, Liangwen Chen, Jie Yang, Lei Yang, and Zhiyu Sun

High-intensity muon beams could enable a muonium-based axion search through resonant quantum transitions between hyperfine states. Combining theoretical calculations with simulation results, we demonstrate that such a muonium-based experimental approach could complement and tighten constraints on th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111803] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: Muonium hyperfine spectroscopy with high-intensity muon beams is proposed as a quantum sensor for axion dark matter, complementing existing constraints.
motivation: Axion dark matter remains experimentally unconfirmed, motivating new precision quantum-sensing approaches that can probe weakly coupled axion parameter space.
method: The authors combine theoretical calculations of muonium hyperfine transitions with simulation studies of a resonant spectroscopy experiment using high-intensity muon beams.
result: The simulated muonium-based experimental approach can complement and tighten existing constraints on axion dark matter couplings.
conclusion: Muonium spectroscopy offers a promising quantum-sensor route for axion dark matter searches, though it falls outside the researcher's core quantum information and thermodynamics interests.

title: Superconductivity In Noncentrosymmetric Rhombohedral ${\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}$
authors: Zhengxian Li, Xiaoyu Shen, Shaozheng Wang, Kai Liu, Yating Sha, Tianyang Wang, Feng Liu, Qingchen Duan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Peng Chen, Shiyong Wang, Ruidan Zhong, Dong Qian, Yufan Li, Shengwei Jiang, Noah F. Q. Yuan, And Guorui Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhengxian Li, Xiaoyu Shen, Shaozheng Wang, Kai Liu, Yating Sha, Tianyang Wang, Feng Liu, Qingchen Duan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Peng Chen, Shiyong Wang, Ruidan Zhong, Dong Qian, Yufan Li, Shengwei Jiang, Noah F. Q. Yuan, and Guorui Chen

Crystal stacking offers a powerful yet underexplored route to engineer symmetry in layered superconductors. Here we report superconductivity in rhombohedral-stacked [MATH] ([MATH]), a noncentrosymmetric polytype in which global inversion symmetry is removed by…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116002] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the discovery of superconductivity in rhombohedral-stacked noncentrosymmetric NbSe2, showing that crystal stacking can engineer symmetry and superconducting properties in layered materials.
motivation: Crystal stacking is an underexplored route to engineer symmetry in layered superconductors, and noncentrosymmetric polytypes provide a platform to study how broken inversion symmetry affects superconductivity.
method: The authors synthesize/fabricate rhombohedral-stacked NbSe2 (likely via exfoliation and stacking or crystal growth), characterize its crystal structure and symmetry, and perform transport measurements to detect superconductivity.
result: Superconductivity is observed in rhombohedral NbSe2, a noncentrosymmetric polytype in which global inversion symmetry is removed by the stacking arrangement, distinguishing it from the conventional centrosymmetric bulk phase.
conclusion: The findings establish rhombohedral stacking as a controllable knob for engineering symmetry and superconductivity in layered transition-metal dichalcogenides, opening avenues for exploring unconventional superconducting states.

title: Nearly Topological Flat Bands In $d\text{−}\mathrm{wave}$ Altermagnets
authors: Xu-Hui Yan, Dong-Hao Guan, Ying Han, Lu Qi, And Ai-Lei He
abstract:
Author(s): Xu-Hui Yan, Dong-Hao Guan, Ying Han, Lu Qi, and Ai-Lei He

Altermagnets, collinear antiferromagnets with vanishing net magnetization yet momentum-dependent spin splitting, open a new route to topology and strong correlations. In this work, we propose a general framework to construct nearly topological flat-band (TFB) models in [MATH]-wave altermagnets via stac…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185112] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a general framework for constructing nearly topological flat-band models in d-wave altermagnets.
motivation: Altermagnets combine vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent spin splitting, offering a platform for topology and strong correlations, but flat-band engineering in this context remains less explored.
method: The authors build nearly topological flat-band models in d-wave altermagnets using a stacked or lattice-based construction and analyze the resulting band structures and topological properties.
result: They obtain nearly flat bands with nontrivial topology in d-wave altermagnet systems, potentially enabling correlated topological phases.
conclusion: The work expands the design space for topological flat bands in altermagnetic materials, though it remains a condensed-matter band-structure study without direct quantum-information or thermodynamic focus.

title: Dual-pathway Symmetry Breaking Modulates Bright-dark Singlet Exciton Energy Ordering In CSi(Ge)N Monolayers
authors: Jiansheng Tang, Huiwen Luo, Siwei Luo, Chao Tang, Zongyu Huang, Jianxin Zhong, And Gencai Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Jiansheng Tang, Huiwen Luo, Siwei Luo, Chao Tang, Zongyu Huang, Jianxin Zhong, and Gencai Guo

The lowest-energy exciton in some two-dimensional (2D) materials can be optically dark owing to spin, momentum, or spatial-symmetry selection rules, which suppresses its direct radiative recombination. Controlling the relative energy ordering of bright and dark states in the exciton spectrum is ther…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185417] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how dual-pathway symmetry breaking controls the energy ordering of bright and dark singlet excitons in CSi(Ge)N monolayers.
motivation: The lowest-energy exciton in some 2D materials can be optically dark due to spin, momentum, or spatial-symmetry selection rules, and controlling bright-dark energy ordering is important for optoelectronic applications.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations to study excitonic states and symmetry-breaking effects in CSi(Ge)N monolayers.
result: They find that dual-pathway symmetry breaking can modulate the relative energy ordering of bright and dark singlet excitons in these monolayers.
conclusion: The work provides design principles for tuning excitonic properties in 2D materials for potential optoelectronic applications.

title: Stationary Densities In A Weakly Nonconserving Asymmetric Exclusion Process With Finite Resources
authors: Sourav Pal And Abhik Basu
abstract:
Author(s): Sourav Pal and Abhik Basu

Inspired by the phenomenologies of an open totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) with Langmuir kinetics (Lk) and finite resources that dynamically control the entry and exit rates of the TASEP lane, we study the stationary densities and phase transitions in a TASEP with Lk connected to…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034121] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies stationary densities and phase transitions in a weakly nonconserving asymmetric exclusion process with Langmuir kinetics and finite resources.
motivation: Inspired by open TASEP with Langmuir kinetics and finite resources that dynamically control entry and exit rates, the work aims to understand how limited resources affect nonequilibrium stationary behavior.
method: The authors analyze a classical driven lattice gas model using theoretical techniques for stochastic interacting particle systems, likely mean-field theory and possibly numerical simulations.
result: They obtain stationary density profiles and identify phase transitions, showing how finite resources modify the phase diagram and density behavior.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into nonequilibrium phase transitions in resource-limited driven diffusive systems, relevant to classical stochastic transport phenomena.

title: Inertial Synchronization Of Networked Oscillators In Arbitrary Dimensions
authors: Kirill Kovalenko, Xiangfeng Dai, Fanshu Fang, Zerong Guo, Haoran Liu, Federico Botta, Charo I. Del Genio, Stefano Boccaletti, And Simona Olmi
abstract:
Author(s): Kirill Kovalenko, Xiangfeng Dai, Fanshu Fang, Zerong Guo, Haoran Liu, Federico Botta, Charo I. del Genio, Stefano Boccaletti, and Simona Olmi

The Kuramoto model provides a paradigmatic framework for studying the synchronization of interacting oscillators, and has been generalized to arbitrary dimensions to describe swarms, flocks, and multidimensional opinion dynamics. Yet, existing formulations neglect inertia, a key mechanism known to e…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034308] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes the Kuramoto model of coupled oscillators to arbitrary dimensions while incorporating inertia, analyzing how inertia affects synchronization in networked oscillator systems.
motivation: While the Kuramoto model and its multidimensional generalizations describe swarms, flocks, and opinion dynamics, existing formulations neglect inertia—a key physical mechanism known to influence synchronization.
method: The authors develop a multidimensional Kuramoto-type model with inertial terms and analyze its synchronization behavior, presumably through mean-field and stability analysis.
result: The study characterizes how inertia modifies the synchronization transition and collective dynamics of networked oscillators in arbitrary dimensions.
conclusion: Inertia plays a significant role in shaping synchronization in multidimensional oscillator networks, extending previous inertia-free formulations.

title: Enhanced Superconductivity In Proximity To Peaks In Densities Of States
authors: Joshua Althüser, Ilya M. Eremin, And Götz S. Uhrig
abstract:
Author(s): Joshua Althüser, Ilya M. Eremin, and Götz S. Uhrig

For the BCS theory of superconductivity, the electron-phonon interaction is transformed to an attractive electron-electron interaction in the vicinity of the Fermi energy only. At the same time, its formal derivation using a unitary transformation reveals that the electrons attract one another whene…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033291] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that BCS superconductivity is enhanced when the Fermi level lies near sharp peaks in the electronic density of states, refining the standard textbook picture that pairing only occurs in a narrow window around the Fermi energy.
motivation: Standard BCS theory restricts the attractive electron-electron interaction to a thin shell around the Fermi energy, so it is unclear how van Hove singularities or other density-of-states peaks might boost pairing strength.
method: A unitary transformation of the electron-phonon interaction is used to derive a more general effective attractive interaction, followed by a BCS-type gap analysis in the presence of peaked densities of states.
result: The derived interaction remains attractive beyond the immediate Fermi surface whenever the density of states is strongly peaked, leading to an enhancement of the superconducting critical temperature and gap near such peaks.
conclusion: Superconductivity can be strengthened by engineering the electronic structure so that the Fermi level sits close to van Hove singularities or other density-of-states maxima.

title: Removing Nodal And Support-Mismatch Pathologies In Variational Monte Carlo Via Blurred Sampling
authors: Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, And Shiwei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, and Shiwei Zhang

A Monte Carlo postprocessing method called blurred sampling eliminates infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031059] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a Monte Carlo postprocessing technique called blurred sampling that removes nodal and support-mismatch pathologies (infinite variance and systematic bias) in variational quantum many-body simulations.
motivation: Variational Monte Carlo methods for strongly correlated quantum many-body systems suffer from infinite variance and systematic bias arising from nodal surface inaccuracies and mismatches between the sampling and trial distributions.
method: The authors develop a blurred-sampling scheme, a stochastic postprocessing approach applied to VMC estimators, designed to regularize the sampling distribution and suppress divergent contributions near nodal regions.
result: The method is demonstrated to eliminate the infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations, yielding improved and more reliable energy estimators.
conclusion: Blurred sampling provides a practical fix for long-standing pathologies in variational Monte Carlo, improving the accuracy and stability of quantum many-body ground-state simulations.

title: Bound States In The Continuum With Vectorial Topological Charge
authors: Wen-Jin Zhang, Ze-Peng Zhuang, Xiao-Dong Chen, And Jian-Wen Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Jin Zhang, Ze-Peng Zhuang, Xiao-Dong Chen, and Jian-Wen Dong

Bound states in the continuum (BICs) have long been recognized as topological singularities of light, yet their descriptions have relied solely on scalar topological charges that trace a polarization angle rotation, leaving their true vectorial topology unexplored. Here, we apply the concept of a ve…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 113803] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: This work introduces a vectorial topological charge to describe bound states in the continuum (BICs) in photonic systems, moving beyond scalar polarization-angle-based descriptions.
motivation: BICs are traditionally characterized by scalar topological charges that only capture polarization angle rotation, leaving their full vectorial topology unexplored.
method: The authors apply a vectorial topological charge framework to analyze BICs in photonic structures, likely using electromagnetic mode analysis and topological invariants.
result: The paper demonstrates that BICs possess a richer vectorial topological structure, providing a more complete understanding of their topological nature.
conclusion: The vectorial topological charge offers a new perspective on BICs, with potential implications for topological photonics and light manipulation.

title: Polaronic Lattice State Hybridization In Reduced Oxide Surface Reconstructions
authors: Ning Xu, Sergey V. Levchenko, Yong Wang, And Zhong-Kang Han

Reduced oxide surfaces often undergo complex reconstructions in which atomic rearrangements and reduction-induced electronic redistribution are strongly coupled, obscuring the electronic principles that govern their stability. Here, we address this problem on the prototypical rutile ${}_…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116201] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A condensed-matter study of how polaronic lattice states hybridize in reduced oxide surface reconstructions, explaining the coupled electronic and atomic rearrangements that stabilize these surfaces.
motivation: Reduced oxide surfaces undergo complex reconstructions where atomic rearrangement and reduction-induced electronic redistribution are strongly coupled, obscuring the electronic principles governing surface stability.
method: First-principles electronic-structure calculations (likely DFT plus polaron modeling) applied to a prototypical rutile oxide surface reconstruction.
result: The work identifies hybridization of polaronic lattice states as a key mechanism controlling the energetics and stability of the reconstructed surface.
conclusion: The study provides electronic-structure principles for understanding reduced oxide surface reconstructions, with implications for catalysis and surface science rather than quantum information.

title: Generalized Theory Of Domain-Wall Width In Multisublattice Heisenberg Magnets
authors: José M. Lendínez, Marta Yanguas, Theodor Griepe, Michael Saur, Rubén M. Otxoa, Levente Rózsa, And Unai Atxitia
abstract:

We propose a general expression for the domain-wall width in generic multisublattice Heisenberg magnets with collinear order and uniaxial anisotropy, applicable to ferro-, antiferro-, and ferrimagnetic orders. The result follows from an exact connection between the domain-wall profile and the long-w…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116707] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a general expression for domain-wall width in multisublattice Heisenberg magnets with collinear order and uniaxial anisotropy, covering ferro-, antiferro-, and ferrimagnetic systems.
motivation: Domain-wall width is a key parameter in magnetic materials, but a unified description across different magnetic orders and sublattice structures was lacking.
method: The authors establish an exact connection between the domain-wall profile and the long-wavelength spin-wave spectrum, then use it to derive a general width formula for multisublattice Heisenberg magnets.
result: A generalized analytic expression for the domain-wall width is obtained, applicable to ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and ferrimagnetic orders with uniaxial anisotropy.
conclusion: The theory provides a common framework for understanding domain-wall widths in diverse magnetic materials and may guide the design of spintronic and magnetic storage devices.

title: Chiral High-Harmonic Generation Via Subcycle Symmetry Engineering
authors: Ya Bai, Hanqing Xu, Ying Ma, Shuo Wang, Jingyuan Niu, Candong Liu, Peng Liu, And Ruxin Li
abstract:

A crystal with special geometric properties can be optically driven to produce an output beam with any desired polarization.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116905] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates chiral high-harmonic generation by engineering subcycle symmetries in a crystal to produce output beams with arbitrary polarization.
motivation: Controlling the polarization and symmetry of high-harmonic emission is important for ultrafast spectroscopy and light-matter interaction studies.
method: A crystal with special geometric properties is optically driven by tailored laser fields to break or impose subcycle symmetries.
result: The generated high harmonics exhibit chiral properties and can be shaped into any desired output polarization.
conclusion: Subcycle symmetry engineering provides a versatile route to chiral high-harmonic generation and polarization control.

title: Envelope-induced Asymmetry Of The Autler-Townes Doublet
authors: Ayoub Ait Elarabi And András Csehi
abstract:
Author(s): Ayoub Ait Elarabi and András Csehi

Due to the recent availability of intense, short, XUV laser pulses, the investigation of the Autler-Townes (AT) doublet in resonant ionization phenomena is experiencing a renaissance. In particular, the asymmetry of the AT doublet was found to be sensitive to numerous physical parameters, providing …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033106] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how the envelope of intense short XUV laser pulses induces asymmetry in the Autler-Townes doublet observed in resonant ionization.
motivation: Recent availability of intense, short XUV pulses has revived interest in Autler-Townes doublets in resonant ionization, whose asymmetry is sensitive to many physical parameters.
method: Theoretical/quantum-optical treatment of a laser-dressed atomic system driven by few-cycle XUV pulses, examining how the pulse envelope modifies the dressed-state structure and ionization spectra.
result: The envelope of the driving pulse is shown to control and induce asymmetry in the Autler-Townes doublet lineshape.
conclusion: The findings clarify how pulse-envelope effects shape Autler-Townes spectra, aiding interpretation of strong-field XUV ionization experiments.

title: Visualizing The Dispersions Of Fermi Polarons And Molecules Via Spin-orbit Coupling
authors: Tingting Shi And Xiaoling Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Tingting Shi and Xiaoling Cui

We propose to measure the dispersions of Fermi polaron and molecule by engineering spin-orbit coupling (SOC) on the impurity, which induces spin flip with finite momentum transfer. The polaron dispersion can be probed at small SOC momentum from the linear response of impurity spin. For molecule, we …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033317] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a scheme to measure the dispersions of Fermi polarons and molecules by engineering spin-orbit coupling on an impurity in an ultracold Fermi gas.
motivation: Fermi polarons and molecules are fundamental quasiparticles in strongly interacting Fermi gases, but their dispersions are challenging to probe directly.
method: Spin-orbit coupling is applied to the impurity, inducing spin flips with finite momentum transfer; the polaron dispersion is extracted from the linear response of the impurity spin at small SOC momentum, and a similar approach is used for molecules.
result: The proposal shows that the polaron dispersion can be probed at small SOC momentum via impurity spin response, and the molecule dispersion can also be visualized with an appropriate SOC scheme.
conclusion: Engineering spin-orbit coupling offers a viable experimental route to visualize the dispersions of Fermi polarons and molecules in ultracold atomic systems.

title: Quantum Metrology Via Adiabatic Control Of Topological Edge States
authors: Xingjian He, Aoqian Shi, Jianjun Liu, And Jiangbin Gong
abstract:
Author(s): Xingjian He, Aoqian Shi, Jianjun Liu, and Jiangbin Gong

Criticality-based quantum sensing exploits hypersensitive response to system parameters near phase transition points. This work uncovers two metrological advantages offered by topological phase transitions when the probe is prepared as topological edge states. First, the order of topological band to…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032205] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that topological edge states, when adiabatically controlled, offer two metrological advantages for criticality-based quantum sensing.
motivation: Criticality-based quantum sensing leverages hypersensitivity near phase transitions, but the role of topological edge states in metrology remains underexplored.
method: The probe is prepared as topological edge states and manipulated via adiabatic control to exploit topological phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation.
result: Two distinct metrological advantages are identified, arising from the order of the topological band and the edge-state response near critical points.
conclusion: Topological phase transitions can provide a novel resource for quantum metrology, potentially improving sensitivity beyond conventional criticality-based schemes.

title: Field-tunable Partially Disordered Antiferromagnetism, Cluster Glass Spin Dynamics, And Large Exchange Bias In The Quasi-one-dimensional Spin-chain Compound ${\mathrm{Ca}}_{3}{\mathrm{CoIrO}}_{6}$
authors: Priyanka Mahalle, A. Kumar, Kumar Bharti, Dipanshu Bansal, P. D. Babu, And S. M. Yusuf
abstract:
