We report a comprehensive investigation of the quasi-one-dimensional spin-chain compound [MATH] (CCIO) using x-ray and neutron diffraction, dc and ac magnetization, specific heat, electrical resistivity, Raman spectroscopy, and polarization–electric-field measurement…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134416] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Comprehensive experimental study of the quasi-one-dimensional spin-chain compound Ca3CoIrO6 reveals field-tunable partially disordered antiferromagnetism, cluster glass spin dynamics, and a large exchange bias.
motivation: To understand the complex magnetic ground states and exchange bias phenomena in quasi-one-dimensional spin-chain iridates, which may host exotic magnetism due to frustration and disorder.
method: The authors used x-ray and neutron diffraction, dc and ac magnetization, specific heat, electrical resistivity, Raman spectroscopy, and polarization–electric-field measurements.
result: The compound exhibits partially disordered antiferromagnetism, cluster glass spin dynamics, and a large exchange bias, all of which can be tuned by an external magnetic field.
conclusion: The interplay of low-dimensionality, frustration, and disorder in Ca3CoIrO6 leads to these novel magnetic behaviors, offering insights into complex spin-chain systems.

title: Bulk Superconductivity In A Tsai-type 2/1 Approximant Approaching The Quasiperiodic Limit
authors: Shintaro Suzuki, Shunsuke Ogasawara, Yuji Muro, Takenori Fujii, Asuka Ishikawa, And Ryuji Tamura
abstract:
Author(s): Shintaro Suzuki, Shunsuke Ogasawara, Yuji Muro, Takenori Fujii, Asuka Ishikawa, and Ryuji Tamura

The emergence of superconductivity in quasiperiodic systems poses a fundamental question: Can conventional superconductivity survive as translational symmetry is progressively lost toward the quasiperiodic limit? Quasicrystal approximants, which share the same local atomic motifs as quasicrystals wh…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144506] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the observation of bulk superconductivity in a Tsai-type 2/1 quasicrystal approximant as the system approaches the quasiperiodic limit.
motivation: It addresses whether conventional superconductivity can survive when translational symmetry is progressively lost toward a quasiperiodic structure, a fundamental question in the physics of aperiodic systems.
method: The authors synthesize a Tsai-type 2/1 approximant and characterize its superconducting transition through bulk measurements (e.g., resistivity, magnetization, and specific heat).
result: Bulk superconductivity is found to emerge in the approximant, demonstrating that a superconducting state can persist in a system with long-range quasiperiodic order.
conclusion: The findings suggest that conventional superconductivity is compatible with the loss of translational symmetry, providing insight into superconductivity near the quasiperiodic limit.

title: Perpendicular Electric Field Induced Competing ${s}^{±}$-wave And $d$-wave Superconducting Pairings In ${\mathrm{La}}_{3}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$ Thin Films
authors: Yongping Wei, Xun Liu, Fan Yang, And Mi Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Yongping Wei, Xun Liu, Fan Yang, and Mi Jiang

Inspired by the possibility that superconducting properties may be altered by applying a perpendicular electric field in the Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) bilayer nickelate [MATH] thin film, we investigated the imbalanced two-orbital bilayer Hubbard model with …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165115] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of an imbalanced two-orbital bilayer Hubbard model showing that a perpendicular electric field induces competing s±-wave and d-wave superconducting pairings in La3Ni2O7 thin films.
motivation: Motivated by the possibility that superconducting properties of Ruddlesden-Popper bilayer nickelate thin films can be tuned by an applied perpendicular electric field, the authors seek to understand the resulting pairing symmetry competition.
method: The authors investigate an imbalanced two-orbital bilayer Hubbard model, presumably using mean-field or related many-body techniques to compute superconducting pairing susceptibilities and phase diagrams as a function of applied field and orbital imbalance.
result: They find that the perpendicular electric field drives competition between s±-wave and d-wave superconducting pairing channels in the nickelate thin film system.
conclusion: Electric-field tuning of interlayer imbalance provides a route to control the pairing symmetry in bilayer nickelate superconductors, with implications for understanding and engineering their superconductivity.

method: First-principles/atomistic simulations of monolayer MoS2 doped with MoO3 molecules are used to compute phonon transport properties and extract thermal conductivity changes as a function of doping level.
result: Doping with MoO3 molecules modifies phonon scattering and dispersion, leading to a tunable reduction (or modulation) of the lattice thermal conductivity of monolayer MoS2.
conclusion: Surface charge transfer doping is shown to be an effective knob for engineering thermal transport in 2D materials, with implications for thermal management in nanoelectronics.

result: They directly observed the characteristic winding of magnon spectral weight associated with Dirac magnons and found an approximately T^2 thermal renormalization of magnon energies consistent with magnon-magnon interactions.
conclusion: The measurements provide experimental confirmation of gapped Dirac magnons in CrI3 and characterize how magnon-magnon interactions renormalize their energies with temperature.

tldr: Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations reveal a discontinuous efficiency-fragility transition in critical infrastructure networks under nonstationary conditions, with dual thresholds and a deceptive safety zone.
motivation: Modern infrastructure networks are optimized for efficiency under stationary conditions but face increasing nonstationary physical environments, potentially leading to catastrophic cascading failures.
method: The study performs 1.55 million cascade event simulations across five network scales to analyze how efficiency-driven operation affects fragility and failure propagation.
result: The analysis identifies a sharp discontinuity between efficiency and fragility, characterized by dual thresholds and a deceptive safe operating zone where networks appear robust but are actually vulnerable.
conclusion: Efficiency optimization in critical infrastructure can create hidden fragility, and understanding the dual thresholds is essential for designing resilient networks under nonstationary conditions.

result: The approach yields corrected kinetic descriptions capturing deviations from mass-action behavior in multistage reactions, with the field-theoretic framework systematically handling fluctuations and correlations.

result: Multiple scattering is shown to significantly influence near-bandgap harmonic generation, providing a more complete picture beyond the standard short-trajectory interpretation.
conclusion: Complex quantum trajectories offer a useful framework for probing near-bandgap high-harmonic generation and multiple-scattering effects in condensed matter.

method: Group-theoretical/symmetry-based classification of crystal structures, organized into polar and chiral categories, likely analyzed through electromagnetic response symmetries.
result: Twelve fundamentally distinct types of crystal structures are identified across five polar and five chiral categories, providing a complete taxonomy.
conclusion: The classification offers a practical framework for predicting and engineering next-generation multifunctional materials, but has no direct bearing on quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Strain-Tunable Anomalous Hall Effect In Hexagonal MnTe
authors: Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. Destefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, And Pengcheng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. DeStefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, and Pengcheng Dai

Uniaxial strain applied to the hexagonal altermagnet
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031033] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: Uniaxial strain applied to the hexagonal altermagnet MnTe isolates a single magnetic domain, producing a sharp anomalous Hall effect whose sign reverses due to strain-modified electronic Berry curvature.
motivation: Altermagnets host momentum-dependent spin splitting that could enable novel spintronic phenomena, but probing their transport signatures is complicated by the presence of multiple magnetic domains. The authors sought to isolate a single domain to cleanly resolve the anomalous Hall effect and its tunability.
method: Single crystals of hexagonal MnTe were subjected to controlled uniaxial strain to select a single magnetic domain, and the resulting magnetotransport and neutron scattering measurements were combined with electronic-structure calculations of Berry curvature.
result: Strain-induced domain selection yields a sharp anomalous Hall signal, including a sign reversal that the calculations attribute to strain-driven modifications of the Berry curvature near the Fermi level.
conclusion: The work demonstrates strain as an effective control knob for the anomalous Hall response in altermagnetic MnTe, highlighting altermagnets as a promising platform for Berry-curvature-based spintronics.

title: Qed Corrections Of Orders $m{α}^{6}$ And $m{α}^{6}(m/M)$ For ${\mathrm{HD}}^{+}$ Spin-independent Rovibrational Transitions Beyond Born-Oppenheimer Approximation
authors: Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Ping Yang, Vladimir I. Korobov, Chun Li, And Ting-Yun Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Ping Yang, Vladimir I. Korobov, Chun Li, and Ting-Yun Shi

The effective Hamiltonian of [MATH]- and [MATH]-order corrections for hydrogen molecular ions has been derived by Zhong et al. [Z.-X. Zhong, W.-P. Zhou, and X.-S. Mei,
tldr: The paper derives higher-order QED corrections for spin-independent rovibrational transitions in HD+ beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation.
motivation: Precise theoretical predictions for hydrogen molecular ions are needed to match high-resolution spectroscopy and to test fundamental physics.
method: An effective Hamiltonian for mα^6 and mα^6(m/M) corrections is constructed and expressed as finite-value effective operators, extending prior work.
result: The QED corrections of orders mα^6 and mα^6(m/M) are obtained for HD+ spin-independent rovibrational transitions beyond Born-Oppenheimer.
conclusion: These improved calculations should refine theoretical spectra of HD+ and support precision tests of molecular quantum electrodynamics.

title: Charge-$2e$ Superconductivity From A Disordered Pair Density Wave
authors: Julian May-Mann, Akshat Pandey, Zhengyan Darius Shi, And Steven A. Kivelson
abstract:
Author(s): Julian May-Mann, Akshat Pandey, Zhengyan Darius Shi, and Steven A. Kivelson

We investigate the effects of disorder on a system that in the clean limit is a pair density wave (PDW) superconductor. The charge order of the clean PDW is inevitably lost (via Imry-Ma), but the fate of the superconducting order is less clear. Here, we consider a strongly inhomogeneous limit in whi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116003] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how disorder affects superconductivity in a system that is a pair density wave (PDW) superconductor in the clean limit.
motivation: While charge order in a clean PDW is destroyed by disorder via the Imry-Ma mechanism, the fate of the superconducting order under strong inhomogeneity is unclear.
method: The authors analyze a strongly inhomogeneous limit of a disordered PDW superconductor, presumably using theoretical condensed-matter techniques.
result: They find that charge-2e superconductivity can survive or emerge from the disordered PDW state, with the clean PDW charge order lost.
conclusion: Disorder can stabilize charge-2e superconductivity even when the underlying PDW charge order is destroyed.

title: Measured And Theoretical $\mathrm{K}α$ X-Ray Emission Linewidths Of U, Np, And Pu
authors: Abigail Wessels, Jonathan W. Dean, Daniel T. Becker, Douglas A. Bennett, Matthew H. Carpenter, Mark Croce, Joseph W. Fowler, Johnathon D. Gard, Paul Indelicato, Katrina E. Koehler, J. A. B. Mates, Daniel Mcneel, David Mercer, Daniel R. Schmidt, Katherine Schreiber, Daniel S. Swetz, Duc Vo, Sophie Weidenbenner, And Joel N. Ullom
abstract:
Author(s): Abigail Wessels, Jonathan W. Dean, Daniel T. Becker, Douglas A. Bennett, Matthew H. Carpenter, Mark Croce, Joseph W. Fowler, Johnathon D. Gard, Paul Indelicato, Katrina E. Koehler, J. A. B. Mates, Daniel McNeel, David Mercer, Daniel R. Schmidt, Katherine Schreiber, Daniel S. Swetz, Duc Vo, Sophie Weidenbenner, and Joel N. Ullom

We present measurements of the [MATH] and [MATH] natural x-ray linewidths of uranium, neptunium, and plutonium ([MATH], 93, 94) obtained using a superconducting transition-edge sensor microcalorimeter array. The relative uncertainties range from 0.5% to 1.5%, impro…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 113001] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper measures and calculates Kα x-ray emission linewidths for uranium, neptunium, and plutonium using a superconducting transition-edge sensor microcalorimeter array.
motivation: Precise x-ray linewidths of actinides are needed to benchmark atomic theory and provide reference data for nuclear and fundamental physics.
method: The authors used a superconducting transition-edge sensor microcalorimeter array to measure the natural Kα x-ray linewidths of U, Np, and Pu, and compared the results with theoretical calculations.
result: They obtained linewidths with relative uncertainties between 0.5% and 1.5%, improving upon previous measurements for these actinide elements.
conclusion: The measurements provide high-precision benchmarks for actinide atomic structure and demonstrate the capability of transition-edge sensor microcalorimeters for x-ray spectroscopy.

title: Nanomechanical Detection Of Vortices In An Electron Fluid
authors: Andrey A. Shevyrin, Askhat K. Bakarov, And Arthur G. Pogosov
abstract:
Author(s): Andrey A. Shevyrin, Askhat K. Bakarov, and Arthur G. Pogosov

A nanomechanical resonator provides a simple way to directly measure the torque generated by electron vortices.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116302] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A nanomechanical resonator is used to directly detect the torque produced by electron vortices in a hydrodynamic electron fluid.
motivation: Electron hydrodynamics predicts viscous vortex formation in electron fluids, but directly probing such vortices has been experimentally difficult because most signatures are indirect or geometry-dependent.
method: The authors deploy a nanomechanical resonator as a torque sensor to measure the mechanical response induced by electron vortices in a high-mobility electron system.
result: The resonator detects a torque consistent with the presence of electron vortices in the electron fluid, providing a direct mechanical probe of hydrodynamic electron flow.
conclusion: Nanomechanical torque detection offers a simple and direct route to accessing vortex dynamics in electron fluids, complementing traditional electrical transport measurements.

title: Emergent Surface Altermagnetism
authors: Yuzhong Hu, Pan Zhou, Baoru Pan, Songmin Liu, Binchang Zhou, And Lizhong Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Yuzhong Hu, Pan Zhou, Baoru Pan, Songmin Liu, Binchang Zhou, and Lizhong Sun

Research on altermagnetism has thus far primarily focused on spin-polarized bulk electronic states in magnetic materials. In this work, we advance the field by introducing the concept of surface altermagnetism (SAM), wherein altermagnetic spin polarization emerges at the surfaces of collinear antife…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116705] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the concept of surface altermagnetism, where altermagnetic spin polarization emerges at the surfaces of collinear antiferromagnets.
motivation: Altermagnetism research has largely focused on bulk spin-polarized electronic states, leaving surface effects unexplored.
method: The authors use symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations to study collinear antiferromagnets and identify surface altermagnetic states.
result: They predict emergent spin polarization at surfaces that is absent in the bulk, establishing a new class of surface magnetic phenomena.
conclusion: Surface altermagnetism expands the scope of altermagnetism and may enable novel spintronic functionalities based on surface spin polarization.

title: Extent Of Nonequilibrium Sets Relaxation Barriers In Dewetting Polymer Films
authors: Mithun Madhusudanan, Federico Caporaletti, Jotypriya Sarkar, Rohit V. Menon, Sivasurender Chandran, Ronald P. White, Jane E. G. Lipson, Simone Napolitano, And Mithun Chowdhury
abstract:
Author(s): Mithun Madhusudanan, Federico Caporaletti, Jotypriya Sarkar, Rohit V. Menon, Sivasurender Chandran, Ronald P. White, Jane E. G. Lipson, Simone Napolitano, and Mithun Chowdhury

Thin polymer films are archetypal nonequilibrium systems in which chain conformations are frozen by rapid preparation. The resulting molecular recoiling stress drives the system toward equilibrium and relaxes with time and temperature. We show that the activation energy governing this relaxation dep…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 118102] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper examines how the extent of nonequilibrium states influences the relaxation barriers in dewetting polymer films.
motivation: Thin polymer films are archetypal nonequilibrium systems where rapid preparation freezes chain conformations, and understanding the relaxation of the resulting molecular recoiling stress is important for controlling film stability.
method: The authors use dewetting experiments and temperature-dependent relaxation measurements to extract the activation energy governing the relaxation process.
result: The activation energy governing the relaxation is shown to depend on the extent of nonequilibrium, indicating that relaxation barriers are not fixed but vary with the degree of departure from equilibrium.
conclusion: The findings link the preparation history and the extent of nonequilibrium to the relaxation dynamics of polymer films, providing insight into nonequilibrium soft matter behavior.

title: Three- And Four-boson Systems Expanded Around The Unitarity Limit: Application To $^{4}\mathrm{He}$ Molecules
authors: Feng Wu, Xincheng Lin, Ubirajara van Kolck, And Sebastian König
abstract:
Author(s): Feng Wu, Xincheng Lin, Ubirajara van Kolck, and Sebastian König

The three- and four-boson systems with a large scattering length and a short effective range in the two-body sector are studied in the framework of Short-Range Effective Field Theory (SREFT). The starting point (leading order) of the EFT is taken to be the universal unitarity limit, where the two-bo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033312] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies three- and four-boson systems expanded around the unitarity limit using short-range effective field theory, with application to helium-4 molecules.
motivation: Few-body systems with large scattering lengths exhibit universal behavior near unitarity, but finite effective-range corrections and their impact on molecular binding are important for realistic systems such as helium clusters.
method: The authors use Short-Range Effective Field Theory (SREFT) with the unitarity limit as leading order and include range corrections perturbatively for three- and four-boson systems.
result: They derive expressions for three- and four-body observables and apply them to helium-4 molecules, showing how finite-range effects modify universal predictions.
conclusion: The SREFT expansion around unitarity provides a systematic framework for describing light bosonic molecules, though its direct relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems is limited.

title: Near Degeneracies Between Opposite Parity States In The Heavy DyAg Molecule
authors: S. Kotochigova, J. Kłos, And E. Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): S. Kotochigova, J. Kłos, and E. Tiesinga

We theoretically investigate the rare-earth [MATH] molecule as a quantum sensor to amplify weak symmetry-breaking interactions not included in the standard model of physics. We focus on parity-breaking interactions from the octupole-deformed [MATH] nucleus.…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033314] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates the heavy DyAg molecule as a quantum sensor for parity-breaking interactions arising from an octupole-deformed nucleus.
motivation: To amplify weak symmetry-breaking interactions beyond the Standard Model, particularly nuclear parity violation, using molecular systems with near-degenerate opposite-parity states.
method: The authors perform theoretical calculations of the electronic structure of DyAg to identify near degeneracies between opposite-parity states that enhance sensitivity to parity-breaking effects.
result: They find near degeneracies between opposite-parity states in DyAg that could enable sensitive probes of octupole-deformed nuclear moments and symmetry-violating interactions.
conclusion: DyAg is proposed as a promising molecular platform for quantum sensing of fundamental symmetry violations, though it is not directly related to the user's core research directions.

title: Inequivalent Interstitial Electron States And Pressure-enhanced Superconductivity In The ${\mathrm{Li}}_{6}{\mathrm{Mg}}_{2}\mathrm{P}$ Electride Via Heterometallic Competitive Polarization
authors: Shuai Han, Xiaohua Zhang, And Guochun Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Han, Xiaohua Zhang, and Guochun Yang

In electrides, interstitial anionic electrons (IAEs) constitute a key electronic degree of freedom whose spatial organization governs the electronic structure and emergent quantum properties. However, controlled realization of IAEs with complex topologies remains a central challenge. Here we propose…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154505] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how heterometallic competitive polarization creates inequivalent interstitial electron states and enhances superconductivity in the Li6Mg2P electride under pressure.
motivation: Interstitial anionic electrons in electrides provide a tunable electronic degree of freedom, but controlling their spatial organization and topological complexity remains challenging.
method: The authors perform first-principles calculations to analyze the electronic structure, interstitial electron states, and superconducting properties of Li6Mg2P under applied pressure.
result: Heterometallic competitive polarization is shown to produce inequivalent interstitial electron states, and pressure enhances the superconducting transition temperature.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a design principle for electrides where chemical and pressure tuning of interstitial electrons can optimize superconductivity.

title: Imaging The Transition From Diffusive To Landauer Resistivity Dipoles
authors: Serhii Kovalchuk, David Kämpfer, Jonathan K. Hofmann, Timofey Balashov, Vasily Cherepanov, Bert Voigtländer, Ireneusz Morawski, F. Stefan Tautz, And Felix Lüpke
abstract:
Author(s): Serhii Kovalchuk, David Kämpfer, Jonathan K. Hofmann, Timofey Balashov, Vasily Cherepanov, Bert Voigtländer, Ireneusz Morawski, F. Stefan Tautz, and Felix Lüpke

A pointlike defect in a uniform current-carrying conductor induces a dipole in the electrochemical potential, which counteracts the original transport field. If the mean free path of the carriers is much smaller than the size of the defect, then the dipole results from the purely diffusive motion of…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165411] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper images the transition between diffusive and Landauer resistivity dipoles around point defects in a current-carrying conductor.
motivation: Pointlike defects in conductors create electrochemical potential dipoles that counteract the transport field, and understanding their formation is important for mesoscopic electron transport.
method: The authors use scanning probe imaging to visualize the electrochemical potential distribution around defects as the carrier mean free path varies relative to defect size.
result: They observe the crossover from purely diffusive dipole behavior to Landauer-type resistivity dipoles, revealing how the local potential landscape depends on scattering regimes.
conclusion: The work provides direct spatial insight into the microscopic origins of Landauer resistivity dipoles and their transition from diffusive transport.

title: Long-lived Relaxation Channel And Exciton-phonon Coupling In ${\mathrm{Ta}}_{2}{\mathrm{NiSe}}_{5}$ Via Nondegenerate Pump-probe Spectroscopy
authors: Poulami Ghosh, Anupama Chauhan, Sidhanta Sahu, Sk Kalimuddin, Mintu Mondal, And N. Kamaraju
abstract:
Author(s): Poulami Ghosh, Anupama Chauhan, Sidhanta Sahu, Sk Kalimuddin, Mintu Mondal, and N. Kamaraju

An excitonic insulator represents a quantum phase in which spontaneous condensation of excitons leads to novel many-body phenomena. [MATH] (TNSe), a layered narrow-gap semiconductor, has emerged as a model platform to probe these correlated excitonic phases and their …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175115] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Nondegenerate pump-probe spectroscopy reveals long-lived relaxation channels and exciton-phonon coupling in the excitonic insulator candidate Ta2NiSe5.
motivation: Ta2NiSe5 is a model platform for correlated excitonic phases, motivating detailed understanding of its ultrafast carrier and exciton dynamics.
method: Femtosecond nondegenerate pump-probe spectroscopy is used to track photoexcited carrier relaxation and exciton-phonon interactions in layered Ta2NiSe5.
result: The measurements reveal a long-lived relaxation channel and quantify exciton-phonon coupling governing the nonequilibrium response.
conclusion: The findings illuminate the excitonic and electron-phonon physics of Ta2NiSe5, relevant to understanding its correlated excitonic insulating phase.

title: Terahertz Response Of Confined Electron-hole Pair: Crossover Between Strong And Weak Confinement
authors: Filip Klimovič, Jens Paaske, And Tomáš Ostatnický
abstract:
Author(s): Filip Klimovič, Jens Paaske, and Tomáš Ostatnický

We theoretically analyze the THz response of an electron-hole pair confined in a semiconductor nanoparticle. We show that the interplay of particle confinement and electron-hole Coulomb interaction leads to significant renormalizations and energy shifts in THz linear conductivity of the nanocrystal.…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175302] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically analyzes the terahertz response of an electron-hole pair confined in a semiconductor nanoparticle, revealing a crossover between strong and weak confinement regimes.
motivation: To understand how the interplay between particle confinement and electron-hole Coulomb interaction modifies the terahertz optical response of semiconductor nanocrystals.
method: The authors perform a theoretical analysis of the confined electron-hole pair, likely using an effective-mass model that incorporates both confinement and Coulomb interaction to compute the THz linear conductivity.
result: They find significant renormalizations and energy shifts in the THz linear conductivity of the nanocrystal due to the confinement-Coulomb interplay.
conclusion: The THz response of semiconductor nanoparticles is strongly affected by the crossover between strong and weak confinement, providing insights into the optoelectronic properties of such systems.

title: Spin-orbit Coupling Effects In Altermagnets: Interplay Of Weak Spin And Orbital Ferromagnetism With Relativistic Splitting Of Electron States
authors: L. M. Sandratskii, K. Carva, And V. M. Silkin
abstract:
Author(s): L. M. Sandratskii, K. Carva, and V. M. Silkin

The novel class of collinear compensated magnets, dubbed altermagnets, has attracted immense research attention by the property of nonrelativistic spin splitting. More recently, the properties of altermagnets caused by relativistic spin-orbit coupling (SOC) became the topic of many investigations. T…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134412] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how spin-orbit coupling and weak spin/orbital ferromagnetism affect relativistic electronic-state splitting in altermagnets.
motivation: Altermagnets have attracted attention for nonrelativistic spin splitting, and recent work has begun exploring relativistic spin-orbit coupling effects in these compensated magnets.
method: The authors likely use first-principles electronic-structure calculations to analyze spin-orbit coupling and magnetic order in altermagnetic materials.
result: The study reveals an interplay between weak spin and orbital ferromagnetism and relativistic splitting of electron states in altermagnets.
conclusion: Spin-orbit coupling is shown to be important for understanding the electronic and magnetic properties of altermagnets beyond the nonrelativistic picture.

title: Chiral Superconductors From Parent States With Nonuniform Berry Curvature: Momentum-space Vortices, Bogoliubov–de Gennes Topology, And Thermal Hall Conductivity
authors: L. David Le Nir, Asimpunya Mitra, And Yong Baek Kim
abstract:
Author(s): L. David Le Nir, Asimpunya Mitra, and Yong Baek Kim

We investigate chiral superconductivity emerging from parent electronic states with non-uniform Berry curvature, motivated by recent experiments in rhombohedral graphene multilayers. Using the continuum [MATH]-model—a tunable platform with independently controllable Berry curvature profiles—we so…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154504] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chiral superconductivity arising from parent states with nonuniform Berry curvature, focusing on momentum-space vortices, Bogoliubov–de Gennes topology, and thermal Hall conductivity.
motivation: Motivated by recent experiments in rhombohedral graphene multilayers, the authors aim to understand how nonuniform Berry curvature in the normal state can drive chiral superconducting order and produce topological signatures.
method: They use the continuum k·p model, a tunable platform with independently controllable Berry curvature profiles, to analyze superconducting pairing and the resulting Bogoliubov–de Gennes quasiparticle spectrum.
result: The work identifies momentum-space vortices and nontrivial BdG topology, and computes the associated thermal Hall conductivity as a probe of chiral superconductivity.
conclusion: The findings establish a connection between nonuniform Berry curvature in parent states and chiral superconductivity, suggesting experimental signatures in graphene-based systems.

title: Multivariate Stochastic Coupling In Unknown Complex Systems: Informative Randomness In Deterministic Brain-body Communication
authors: Andrea Scarciglia, Vincenzo Catrambone, Claudio Bonanno, And Gaetano Valenza
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Scarciglia, Vincenzo Catrambone, Claudio Bonanno, and Gaetano Valenza

Physiological systems exhibit deterministic behavior influenced by dynamic stochasticity, where informative random components play a crucial role in complex system interactions. Fully characterizing multivariate random components is challenging when the underlying deterministic dynamics are unknown.…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034310] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a method for multivariate stochastic coupling in unknown complex systems to quantify informative randomness in deterministic brain-body communication.
motivation: Physiological systems exhibit deterministic behavior influenced by dynamic stochasticity, and fully characterizing multivariate random components is challenging when the underlying deterministic dynamics are unknown.
method: The authors likely introduce a framework based on stochastic coupling or information-theoretic measures to separate informative randomness from deterministic brain-body interactions.
result: The method is applied to brain-body communication data, revealing stochastic couplings that carry information beyond deterministic dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a tool for analyzing stochastic interactions in complex physiological systems, but it is outside the quantum information research directions.

title: GPU-accelerated Sequential Monte Carlo For Bayesian Spectral Analysis
authors: Tomohiro Nabika, Yui Hayashi, And Masato Okada
abstract:
Author(s): Tomohiro Nabika, Yui Hayashi, and Masato Okada

Bayesian spectral deconvolution provides a data-driven framework for mathematical model selection and parameter estimation from spectral data. Although highly versatile, its computational cost grows with the number of model parameters, data points, and candidate models, often rendering practical app…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035303] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a GPU-accelerated sequential Monte Carlo method for Bayesian spectral deconvolution and model selection.
motivation: Bayesian spectral deconvolution is versatile but computationally expensive as model complexity and data size grow, limiting practical use.
method: The authors implement a GPU-accelerated sequential Monte Carlo algorithm for Bayesian spectral analysis, enabling efficient parameter estimation and model selection.
result: The GPU implementation substantially reduces computation time, making Bayesian spectral deconvolution feasible for larger models and datasets.
conclusion: This work provides a practical computational tool for spectral analysis, but it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Anisotropy Can Make A Moving Active Fluid Membrane Rough Or Crumpled
authors: Debayan Jana, Astik Haldar, And Abhik Basu
abstract:
Author(s): Debayan Jana, Astik Haldar, and Abhik Basu

We present a hydrodynamic theory of anisotropic and inversion-asymmetric moving active permeable fluid membranes. These are described by an anisotropic Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation. Depending upon the anisotropy parameters, the membrane is either effectively isotropic and algebraically rough with tr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034113] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A hydrodynamic theory of anisotropic, inversion-asymmetric moving active permeable fluid membranes described by an anisotropic Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation, showing roughness or crumpling depending on anisotropy parameters.
motivation: Active fluid membranes are ubiquitous in biology and soft matter, and understanding how anisotropy and activity control their morphology is of fundamental interest.
method: The authors develop a hydrodynamic effective-field theory that reduces to an anisotropic KPZ equation, then analyze scaling behavior as a function of the anisotropy parameters.
result: Depending on anisotropy, the membrane is either effectively isotropic and algebraically rough, or exhibits crumpled/other fluctuation regimes, with phase boundaries set by the anisotropy parameters.
conclusion: Anisotropy and inversion asymmetry qualitatively change the universal fluctuation statistics of moving active membranes, providing a classification of their roughening and crumpling behavior.

title: Coexistence Of Explosive And Driven Forms Of Remote Synchronization In Star Networks
authors: Siyu Huo
abstract:
Author(s): Siyu Huo

Remote synchronization (RS)—the emergence of phase coherence among nonadjacent peripheral nodes while remaining desynchronized from the mediating hub—is a fundamental mechanism for long-range coordination in complex networks. So far all studies have been focusing on only a single RS plateau generate…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034206] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the coexistence of explosive and driven forms of remote synchronization in star networks, where peripheral nodes achieve phase coherence while remaining desynchronized from the central hub.
motivation: Remote synchronization is a mechanism for long-range coordination in complex networks, but previous studies focused on only a single synchronization plateau, leaving the coexistence of different forms unexplored.
method: The author analyzes star networks using phase oscillator models, likely with numerical simulations and bifurcation analysis, to identify distinct remote synchronization regimes.
result: The work demonstrates that both explosive and driven remote synchronization can coexist in the same star network, revealing a richer phase diagram than previously known.
conclusion: The coexistence of multiple remote synchronization forms highlights the complexity of synchronization in star networks and may have implications for understanding coordinated behavior in classical complex systems.

title: Diffusion Disorder In The Contact Process
authors: Valentin Anfray, Manisha Dhayal, Hong-Yan Shih, And Thomas Vojta
abstract:
Author(s): Valentin Anfray, Manisha Dhayal, Hong-Yan Shih, and Thomas Vojta

We study the effects of spatially inhomogeneous diffusion on the nonequilibrium phase transition in the unidimensional contact process. The directed-percolation critical point in the contact process is known to be stable against the addition of a spatially uniform diffusion term. Correspondingly, we…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034112] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how spatially inhomogeneous diffusion affects the nonequilibrium phase transition in the one-dimensional contact process.
motivation: The directed-percolation critical point is known to be stable against uniform diffusion, so it is natural to ask whether spatial disorder in the diffusion rate can change the critical behavior.
method: The authors use theoretical and numerical methods to analyze the contact process with spatially disordered diffusion, focusing on critical scaling and universality.
result: They determine how diffusion disorder influences the critical point and the universality class of the transition.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the stability of directed-percolation criticality under spatially correlated disorder, though it lies outside quantum information and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Pattern Formation And Stick-slip Dynamics In Binary Particle Assemblies With Rotating Drives
authors: C. Reichhardt And C. J. O. Reichhardt
abstract:
Author(s): C. Reichhardt and C. J. O. Reichhardt

We numerically examine a binary system of particles with repulsive interactions, where one species is driven by a rotating drive and the other is subjected either to a constant drive in a fixed direction or to a rotating drive that is out of phase with the first species. As a function of rotation fr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035409] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of pattern formation and stick-slip dynamics in a binary particle system with rotating drives.
motivation: To understand how competing drives in binary particle assemblies lead to pattern formation and stick-slip behavior.
method: Numerically simulate repulsively interacting binary particles where one species is driven by a rotating drive and the other by a constant or phase-shifted rotating drive.
result: The dynamics exhibit pattern formation and stick-slip motion that depend on rotation frequency and drive configuration.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-equilibrium dynamics of driven binary particle systems, relevant to classical soft matter physics.

title: Universal Correlations In Local Measurements Directly Probe Effective Diffusivity
authors: Omer Granek
abstract:
Author(s): Omer Granek

Measuring transport coefficients at the microscale remains challenging, often relying on indirect methods that require modeling and calibration. This article derives universal asymptotic forms for the autocorrelation and relative uncertainty of local probe measurements in dilute diffusive systems. V…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034108] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: Derives universal asymptotic forms for autocorrelation and relative uncertainty in local measurements of dilute diffusive systems to directly probe effective diffusivity.
motivation: Measuring transport coefficients at the microscale is challenging and typically relies on indirect modeling and calibration.
method: Analytical derivation of universal asymptotic forms for autocorrelation and relative uncertainty of local probe measurements in dilute diffusive systems.
result: Provides universal scaling forms that enable direct extraction of effective diffusivity from local measurement correlations and uncertainties.
conclusion: Local measurement correlations offer a direct, calibration-free route to transport coefficients in diffusive systems.

title: Isomorphic Property Of Sheared Three-dimensional Yukawa Liquidlike Fluids
authors: Dong Huang And Yan Feng
abstract:
Author(s): Dong Huang and Yan Feng

The isomorphic property of strongly coupled three-dimensional (3D) Yukawa liquidlike fluids under steady shear is systematically investigated using nonequilibrium molecular dynamical simulations. It is discovered that, as the shear rate increases substantially, the shear viscosity [MATH] and the radial…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033299] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations reveal an isomorphic property in sheared three-dimensional Yukawa liquidlike fluids, linking shear viscosity to radial distribution functions.
motivation: Understanding the rheology of strongly coupled Yukawa fluids is important for modeling complex plasmas and colloidal systems under shear.
method: The authors perform nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations of 3D Yukawa liquidlike fluids under steady shear, varying the shear rate substantially.
result: As the shear rate increases, the shear viscosity and the radial distribution function exhibit an isomorphic scaling behavior.
conclusion: The observed isomorphism provides a unified description of sheared Yukawa liquids and may simplify the prediction of their transport properties.

title: Ponderomotive Achromat For Electron Optics: Radially Polarized Annular Focusing And A Round-lens Corrector Regime
authors: Yuuki Uesugi And Yuichi Kozawa
abstract:
Author(s): Yuuki Uesugi and Yuichi Kozawa

Ponderomotive electron optics has attracted attention because structured optical fields provide round-lens functionalities, including negative lens power and negative spherical aberration, that are difficult to achieve with conventional Einzel and solenoid lenses. How ponderomotive lenses disperse w…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033300] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a ponderomotive achromat for electron optics using radially polarized annular focusing and a round-lens corrector regime.
motivation: Conventional electron lenses suffer from chromatic and spherical aberrations, and ponderomotive lenses based on structured light can provide negative lens power and negative spherical aberration, but their dispersion and achromatic capabilities remain underexplored.
method: The authors analyze the dispersive properties of ponderomotive electron lenses driven by radially polarized annular optical fields and design an achromat configuration that corrects chromatic aberration.
result: They demonstrate an achromat for electron optics and identify a round-lens corrector regime, showing how structured light can compensate for lens dispersion.
conclusion: Ponderomotive electron optics with radially polarized annular focusing offers a viable route to achromatic electron lenses and aberration correction, though the work is outside the specified quantum information and thermodynamics research directions.

title: Semiconductor Wannier Equations: A Real-time, Real-space Approach To The Nonlinear Optical Response In Crystals
authors: Eduardo B. Molinero, Bruno Amorim, Misha Ivanov, Graham G. Brown, Giovanni Cistaro, João M. Viana Parente Lopes, Álvaro Jiménez-Galán, Pablo San-Jose, And Rui E. F. Silva
abstract:
Author(s): Eduardo B. Molinero, Bruno Amorim, Misha Ivanov, Graham G. Brown, Giovanni Cistaro, João M. Viana Parente Lopes, Álvaro Jiménez-Galán, Pablo San-Jose, and Rui E. F. Silva

We develop the semiconductor Wannier equations (SWEs), a real-time, real-space formulation of ultrafast light-matter dynamics in crystals, by deriving the equations of motion for the electronic reduced density matrix in a localized Wannier basis. Working in real space removes the structure-gauge amb…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033302] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops semiconductor Wannier equations (SWEs), a real-time, real-space formulation of ultrafast light-matter dynamics in crystals, to study nonlinear optical response.
motivation: Understanding ultrafast light-matter interactions in crystals requires a gauge-invariant, real-space approach that avoids structure-gauge ambiguities.
method: The authors derive equations of motion for the electronic reduced density matrix in a localized Wannier basis, yielding a real-time, real-space framework.
result: The SWEs provide a computationally efficient and physically transparent description of nonlinear optical processes in semiconductors.
conclusion: The formulation offers a new tool for simulating and interpreting ultrafast nonlinear optics in crystalline solids.

title: Phase Transition Lowering Under Shock Compression: The Case Of Lead
authors: Charles M. Pépin, Mikhail A. Kozhaev, Matteo Levantino, And Arnaud Sollier
abstract:
Author(s): Charles M. Pépin, Mikhail A. Kozhaev, Matteo Levantino, and Arnaud Sollier

We report time-resolved x-ray diffraction measurements of lead (Pb) subjected to laser-driven shock compression up to the melt on nanosecond timescales. Along its Hugoniot, Pb exhibits a sequence of structural transitions markedly different from those observed under static compression. The conventio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033294] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved x-ray diffraction shows that laser-driven shock compression of lead along its Hugoniot produces a structural transition sequence different from static compression, lowering the phase transition pressure.
motivation: Understanding how phase transitions behave under dynamic (shock) compression is important for equation-of-state modeling and materials behavior at extreme conditions, yet most knowledge comes from static compression experiments.
method: Nanosecond time-resolved x-ray diffraction measurements of lead driven by laser-induced shock compression up to melting, comparing the observed transition sequence along the Hugoniot with static-compression data.
result: Lead exhibits a distinct sequence of structural transitions under shock loading that differs markedly from the conventional static compression behavior, indicating a lowering of the phase transition threshold under dynamic compression.
conclusion: Dynamic shock compression can substantially alter phase transition pathways and pressures in simple metals like lead, highlighting the need to revisit static-based phase diagram assumptions for extreme dynamic conditions.

title: Quantitative Analysis Of Resonant Ionization By Smooth Laser Pulses: Connection Between Effective Hamiltonian Theory And Strong-field Dressed Continua
authors: Jakob Nicolai Bruhnke And Jan Marcus Dahlström
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Nicolai Bruhnke and Jan Marcus Dahlström

The strong asymmetry of Autler-Townes doublets in intense-field ionization has been attributed to either interfering ionization pathways or strong-field dressing of the continuum. These seemingly distinct interpretations are here shown to arise from a time-dependent effective Hamiltonian formalism, which is demonstrated to reproduce b nitio photoelectron spectra.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032041] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper unifies two interpretations of asymmetric Autler-Townes doublets in strong-field ionization using a time-dependent effective Hamiltonian that reproduces ab initio photoelectron spectra.
motivation: To resolve the apparent contradiction between interfering ionization pathways and strong-field continuum dressing as explanations for Autler-Townes doublet asymmetry.
method: A time-dependent effective Hamiltonian formalism is developed and applied to simulate photoelectron spectra for resonant ionization by smooth laser pulses.
result: The effective Hamiltonian quantitatively reproduces ab initio photoelectron spectra, linking effective Hamiltonian theory with strong-field dressed continua.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for analyzing resonant ionization spectra, showing that the two interpretations are complementary aspects of the same underlying physics.

title: Toward Collinear Laser Spectroscopy Of Radioactive Molecules Utilizing In-trap-produced Molecular Ion Beam
authors: W. C. Mei, S. J. Chen, X. F. Yang, J. H. Lv, D. Y. Chen, H. R. Hu, Y. F. Guo, Z. Yan, Y. P. Jing, C. Zhang, Y. P. Lin, T. X. Gao, X. Shen, S. W. Bai, R. F. Garcia Ruiz, J. Yang, And Y. L. Ye
abstract:
Author(s): W. C. Mei, S. J. Chen, X. F. Yang, J. H. Lv, D. Y. Chen, H. R. Hu, Y. F. Guo, Z. Yan, Y. P. Jing, C. Zhang, Y. P. Lin, T. X. Gao, X. Shen, S. W. Bai, R. F. Garcia Ruiz, J. Yang, and Y. L. Ye

Molecules containing short-lived isotopes, namely, radioactive molecules, are among the most promising candidates for probing new physics beyond the standard model, although their production and spectroscopic measurements remain technically challenging. Here, we demonstrate an integrated methodology…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033285] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an integrated methodology for producing radioactive molecular ion beams in a trap and performing collinear laser spectroscopy on them to probe physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: Radioactive molecules are promising candidates for testing fundamental symmetries and searching for new physics, but their production and spectroscopic characterization remain technically difficult.
method: The authors develop an in-trap production scheme for molecular ions containing short-lived isotopes and combine it with collinear laser spectroscopy to enable precision measurements on these radioactive species.
result: They demonstrate the feasibility of the integrated approach, producing the molecular ion beam in-trap and outlining the collinear laser spectroscopy methodology for radioactive molecules.
conclusion: The work establishes a technical pathway toward precision laser spectroscopy of radioactive molecules, potentially enabling sensitive probes of beyond-Standard-Model physics.

title: Stable Three-dimensional Solitons In Spin-orbit-coupled Atomic-molecular Condensates
authors: Chao Kong, Jinqing Li, Guihua Chen, Guilong Li, Zhaopin Chen, Haiming Deng, Boris A. Malomed, And Yongyao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Kong, Jinqing Li, Guihua Chen, Guilong Li, Zhaopin Chen, Haiming Deng, Boris A. Malomed, and Yongyao Li

We elaborate a mechanism for the creation of stable three-dimensional (3D) solitons in spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensates, modeled by the mean-field equations with the quadratic three-wave interaction, characterized by mismatch [MATH]. The planar (effectively two-dimens…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033278] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a mechanism for creating stable three-dimensional solitons in spin-orbit-coupled atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensates using mean-field equations with quadratic three-wave interactions and mismatch.
motivation: Stabilizing three-dimensional solitons in spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensates is challenging due to collapse and instabilities, and atomic-molecular conversion may provide a viable stabilization route.
method: The authors model the system with mean-field equations including a quadratic three-wave interaction characterized by mismatch, likely using variational or numerical methods to analyze stability.
result: The mechanism yields stable three-dimensional solitons, and possibly also planar effectively two-dimensional solitons are considered.
conclusion: The work provides insight into nonlinear wave stabilization in spin-orbit-coupled atomic-molecular condensates, but it lies outside quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Anisotropy Of The Photonic Urbach Tail
authors: M. Menéndez, Lan Hoang Mai, Nazifa Tasnim Arony, Henry Carfagno, Lauren N. Mccabe, Joshua M. O. Zide, Cefe López, Matthew F. Doty, And P. D. García
abstract:
Author(s): M. Menéndez, Lan Hoang Mai, Nazifa Tasnim Arony, Henry Carfagno, Lauren N. McCabe, Joshua M. O. Zide, Cefe López, Matthew F. Doty, and P. D. García

Disorder in photonic lattices creates localized states inside the photonic band gap. The energy distribution of these states is often described as a Lifshitz tail, even though it is inconsistent with Lifshitz statistics near the band edge. Here, we show that in photonic-crystal waveguides with inten…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033271] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the anisotropy of the photonic Urbach tail in disordered photonic-crystal waveguides, showing that the energy distribution of localized states deviates from standard Lifshitz statistics.
motivation: Disorder-induced localized states in photonic band gaps are often modeled as Lifshitz tails, but this description is inconsistent near the band edge; a better understanding of the tail shape and its anisotropy is needed.
method: The authors analyze photonic-crystal waveguides with intentionally introduced disorder, likely combining theoretical modeling with optical transmission measurements to characterize the energy distribution of localized states.
result: They find that the photonic Urbach tail exhibits anisotropy, with the tail shape depending on direction, and that it cannot be explained by conventional Lifshitz statistics.
conclusion: The work provides a refined description of disorder-induced states in photonic lattices, highlighting the role of anisotropy in the Urbach tail and suggesting corrections to standard models.

title: Topological Order Without Band Topology In Moiré Graphene
authors: Hui Liu, Raul Perea-Causin, Zhao Liu, And Emil J. Bergholtz
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Liu, Raul Perea-Causin, Zhao Liu, and Emil J. Bergholtz

Fractional Chern insulators are generally associated with topologically nontrivial bands. Here, it is demonstrated that realistic Coulomb interactions stabilize a Laughlin-like fractional Chern insulator in a trivial (
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032039] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: Realistic Coulomb interactions stabilize a Laughlin-like fractional Chern insulator in a topologically trivial moiré band, showing that quantum geometry can enable many-body topology without band topology.
motivation: Fractional Chern insulators are generally believed to require topologically nontrivial bands, so it is important to test whether they can emerge in trivial bands.
method: The authors study a moiré graphene system with realistic Coulomb interactions and analyze the many-body state in a trivial (Chern number zero) band.
result: They find that a Laughlin-like fractional Chern insulator is stabilized in the trivial band, demonstrating topological order without band topology.
conclusion: Band topology is not a necessary ingredient for fractional Chern insulators; quantum geometry can drive many-body topological order.

title: Effective Ionic Valence And Local Magnetic Moment In Kagome Superconductors
authors: Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, And Wei Ku
abstract:
Author(s): Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, and Wei Ku

Revealing concealed ionic local moments in kagome superconductors reflects strong local correlations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031064] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates effective ionic valence and local magnetic moments in kagome superconductors, revealing concealed local moments that reflect strong electronic correlations.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between local magnetism and superconductivity in kagome materials is important for clarifying the role of strong correlations in these systems.
method: The study combines effective ionic valence analysis with local magnetic moment probes, likely using theoretical and experimental techniques on kagome superconductors.
result: The authors find evidence for hidden ionic local moments, indicating that strong local correlations are present in kagome superconductors.
conclusion: These findings suggest that local magnetic moments and strong correlations play a significant role in the physics of kagome superconductors.

title: Production And Decay Dynamics Of The Charmed Baryon ${\mathrm{Λ}}_{c}^{+}$ In ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Annihilations Near Threshold
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

Researchers observe the transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ in electron-positron annihilations using the BESIII detector.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031058] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The BESIII Collaboration observes transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ produced in electron-positron annihilations near threshold.
motivation: Understanding charmed baryon production and decay mechanisms probes quantum chromodynamics and hadron structure in the threshold region.
method: Using the BESIII detector, the collaboration analyzes e+e- annihilation data near the Λc+Λc- threshold to measure the production and decay dynamics of the charmed baryon.
result: The researchers observe transverse polarization of the Λc+ baryon, revealing spin-dependent production dynamics in the near-threshold region.
conclusion: The measurement provides new insights into charmed baryon production mechanisms and polarization effects, contributing to hadron physics.

title: Bulklike Costless Domain Walls Driven By Phonon Pair Condensation In ${\mathrm{HfO}}_{2}$
authors: Hyun-Jae Lee, Pawan Kumar, Kyoung-June Go, Chang Hoon Kim, Yungyeom Kim, Kyoungjun Lee, Takao Shimizu, Seung Chul Chae, Hosub Jin, Minseong Lee, Umesh Waghmare, Si-Young Choi, And Jun Hee Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun-Jae Lee, Pawan Kumar, Kyoung-June Go, Chang Hoon Kim, Yungyeom Kim, Kyoungjun Lee, Takao Shimizu, Seung Chul Chae, Hosub Jin, Minseong Lee, Umesh Waghmare, Si-Young Choi, and Jun Hee Lee

A previously unrecognized governing principle helps to explain the stable electrical properties in some ferroelectric materials like hafnium oxide.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031041] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: A first-principles and experimental study identifies phonon pair condensation as the governing principle behind bulklike, costless ferroelectric domain walls in HfO2.
motivation: Ferroelectric hafnium oxide exhibits surprisingly stable electrical properties despite the presence of domain walls, which normally carry energy costs; the underlying microscopic mechanism was previously unexplained.
method: The authors combine density functional theory phonon calculations with structural characterization (electron microscopy and related measurements) to analyze domain wall energetics in HfO2.
result: They find that phonon pair condensation stabilizes bulklike domain walls at essentially no energy cost, accounting for the robust ferroelectric behavior.
conclusion: The work establishes a new governing principle for domain wall stability in ferroelectric oxides, with implications for HfO2-based device engineering.

title: Coulomb Screening Of Superconductivity In Magic-Angle Graphene
authors: Julien Barrier, Liangtao Peng, Shuigang Xu, Christophe de Beule, V. I. Fal’ko, K. Watanabe, T. Tanigushi, A. K. Geim, Shaffique Adam, And Alexey I. Berdyugin
abstract:
Author(s): Julien Barrier, Liangtao Peng, Shuigang Xu, Christophe De Beule, V. I. Fal’ko, K. Watanabe, T. Tanigushi, A. K. Geim, Shaffique Adam, and Alexey I. Berdyugin

Metallic layers placed near magic-angle graphene suppress Coulomb interactions and reveal that its superconductivity is driven by electronic interactions rather than conventional atomic vibrations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031040] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: Metallic screening experiments show that superconductivity in magic-angle graphene is driven by electron-electron interactions rather than phonons.
motivation: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene remains debated, especially whether Coulomb interactions or conventional phonon mechanisms dominate.
method: The authors place metallic layers near magic-angle graphene to screen Coulomb interactions and measure the resulting changes in superconducting behavior.
result: Screening suppresses superconductivity, indicating that electronic Coulomb interactions, rather than atomic vibrations, are the primary driver of the superconducting state.
conclusion: The observed sensitivity to Coulomb screening supports an interaction-driven, unconventional pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene.

title: Fast Algorithm For 2d Rigidity Percolation
authors: Nina Javerzat And Daniele Notarmuzi
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Javerzat and Daniele Notarmuzi

An algorithm for simulating the rigidity percolation transition, based on novel theoretical results, overcomes previous size limitations and enables the highly precise characterization of its universality classes, shedding new light on rigidity transitions in amorphous systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031032] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: A new algorithm for simulating 2D rigidity percolation overcomes previous size limitations and enables precise characterization of its universality classes in amorphous systems.
motivation: Rigidity percolation transitions in amorphous systems have been difficult to characterize precisely due to computational size limitations in simulations.
method: The authors develop a simulation algorithm for rigidity percolation based on novel theoretical results, allowing access to larger system sizes.
result: The algorithm achieves highly precise characterization of the universality classes of the rigidity transition, resolving previously ambiguous critical behavior.
conclusion: The work sheds new light on rigidity transitions in amorphous systems and provides a scalable computational tool for studying them.

title: Attosecond Photoelectron Interferometry Of Resonant Structures Between The Ar Spin-orbit-split Thresholds
authors: J. K. Wood, C. Marante, D. Biswas, L. Argenti, And A. Sandhu
abstract:
Author(s): J. K. Wood, C. Marante, D. Biswas, L. Argenti, and A. Sandhu

Resolving the ultrafast decay of metastable electronic states into channels associated with spin-orbit-split ionization thresholds is a long-standing goal of attosecond photoelectron spectroscopy. Here, we use a variant of the rainbow reconstruction of attosecond beating by interference of two-photo…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033290] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses attosecond photoelectron interferometry to resolve ultrafast decay of metastable electronic states in argon near spin-orbit-split ionization thresholds.
motivation: Resolving ultrafast decay into spin-orbit-split ionization channels is a long-standing challenge in attosecond spectroscopy.
method: A variant of rainbow reconstruction of attosecond beating by interference of two-photon transitions is applied to photoelectron interferometry of resonant structures between Ar spin-orbit-split thresholds.
result: The technique resolves resonant structures and their decay dynamics associated with spin-orbit-split ionization thresholds in argon.
conclusion: The work advances attosecond photoelectron spectroscopy of metastable states but is outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Circumstellar Medium Of Supernovae As New Probes For Feebly Interacting Particles
authors: Yu Cheng, Chui-Fan Kong, Yen-Hsun Lin, Meng-Ru Wu, And Seokhoon Yun
abstract:
Author(s): Yu Cheng, Chui-Fan Kong, Yen-Hsun Lin, Meng-Ru Wu, and Seokhoon Yun

We propose a novel strategy to probe feebly interacting particles (FIPs) by exploiting the dense, confined circumstellar medium (CSM) surrounding core-collapse supernovae. FIPs produced in the protoneutron star can deposit substantial visible energy into the CSM via decay prior to the shock breakout…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111005] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using the dense circumstellar medium around core-collapse supernovae as a target to probe feebly interacting particles (FIPs) produced in the protoneutron star.
motivation: Feebly interacting particles are poorly constrained by existing experiments, and new astrophysical environments are needed to extend sensitivity to their parameter space.
method: FIPs produced in the protoneutron star are assumed to decay within the confined circumstellar medium, depositing visible energy there prior to shock breakout; the resulting signatures are computed and compared with observational prospects.
result: The authors find that decay of FIPs in the CSM can deposit substantial visible energy, yielding potentially detectable signatures that constrain FIP couplings.
conclusion: Supernova circumstellar media offer a novel and complementary probe of feebly interacting particle physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Equivariant Localization For Higher Derivative Supergravity
authors: Pietro Benetti Genolini, Florian Gaar, Jerome P. Gauntlett, And James Sparks
abstract:
Author(s): Pietro Benetti Genolini, Florian Gaar, Jerome P. Gauntlett, and James Sparks

Conformal supergravity provides an effective off-shell formalism to study higher derivative actions. We show that the [MATH], [MATH] theory admits equivariantly closed forms. These may be used to compute closed-form expressions for supersymmetric observables in a general class of supergravit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111602] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that a class of conformal higher-derivative supergravity theories admits equivariantly closed forms, enabling closed-form computation of supersymmetric observables via localization.
motivation: Conformal supergravity offers an off-shell formalism useful for studying higher-derivative gravitational actions, but computing supersymmetric observables in such theories is technically difficult.
method: The authors construct equivariantly closed forms in the supergravity theory and apply equivariant localization techniques to evaluate supersymmetric observables.
result: They obtain closed-form expressions for supersymmetric observables across a general class of supergravity backgrounds.
conclusion: Equivariant localization provides a powerful tool for analyzing higher-derivative supergravity and its supersymmetric observables.

title: Slip-Driven $b1−b2$ Phase Transition In Shock-Compressed KCl
authors: Y. Cai, L. Wang, N. B. Zhang, Y. W. Shi, B. X. Bie, M. X. Tang, Y. J. Deng, L. Lu, And S. N. Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Cai, L. Wang, N. B. Zhang, Y. W. Shi, B. X. Bie, M. X. Tang, Y. J. Deng, L. Lu, and S. N. Luo

An ultrafast x-ray diffraction measurement establishes a unified model for −B2 transition in KCl which can be generalized to other materials.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 116102] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Ultrafast x-ray diffraction measurements reveal a slip-driven b1–b2 phase transition in shock-compressed KCl, yielding a unified model generalizable to other materials.
motivation: Understanding structural phase transitions under shock compression is important for high-pressure physics and materials science, but existing models for the b1–b2 transition in ionic crystals lack a unified mechanistic description.
method: The authors perform ultrafast (time-resolved) x-ray diffraction on shock-compressed KCl to track the lattice evolution and infer the transition mechanism, primarily slip-driven deformation.
result: The measurements establish a slip-driven mechanism for the b1–b2 transition and provide a unified model that reproduces the observed transition behavior, with claimed generality to other materials.
conclusion: The work offers a mechanistic, transferable framework for shock-induced structural transitions in ionic solids, though it lies entirely outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems research.

title: Not-Quite-Primordial Black Holes
authors: Wenzer Qin, Soubhik Kumar, Priyamvada Natarajan, And Neal Weiner
abstract:
Author(s): Wenzer Qin, Soubhik Kumar, Priyamvada Natarajan, and Neal Weiner

We propose a new mechanism for the formation of seeds of supermassive black holes at early cosmic epochs. Our scenario explores density fluctuations that are enhanced relative to [MATH] expectations, but with amplitudes that are not large enough to form primordial black holes, and …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111004] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a new cosmological mechanism for forming seeds of supermassive black holes at early cosmic epochs using density fluctuations enhanced beyond standard expectations but insufficient to form primordial black holes.
motivation: Explaining the origin of supermassive black holes observed at high redshifts remains an open problem in cosmology, motivating alternative seed-formation channels.
method: The authors analyze enhanced density fluctuations with amplitudes below the primordial black hole formation threshold and study their gravitational collapse dynamics to identify viable seed formation.
result: They show that such sub-threshold fluctuations can nonetheless collapse into black hole seeds under appropriate conditions, providing a new route to supermassive black hole seeds.
conclusion: The proposed 'not-quite-primordial' black hole scenario offers a novel cosmological pathway to seed supermassive black holes, though it lies entirely outside quantum information research.

title: Six-Loop Gravitational Interactions At The Sixth Post-Newtonian Order
authors: Giacomo Brunello, Manoj K. Mandal, Pierpaolo Mastrolia, Raj Patil, Matteo Pegorin, Jonathan Ronca, Sid Smith, Jan Steinhoff, And William J. Torres Bobadilla
abstract:
Author(s): Giacomo Brunello, Manoj K. Mandal, Pierpaolo Mastrolia, Raj Patil, Matteo Pegorin, Jonathan Ronca, Sid Smith, Jan Steinhoff, and William J. Torres Bobadilla

We compute the gravitational interaction of two coalescing compact objects at sixth post-Newtonian order in the static limit, employing the diagrammatic approach within the effective field theory framework of general relativity. The calculation requires the evaluation of six-loop Feynman diagrams th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111401] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes the six-loop gravitational interaction of two coalescing compact objects at sixth post-Newtonian order using effective field theory and Feynman diagrams.
motivation: Precise theoretical predictions for gravitational-wave signals from compact binary coalescences require high-order post-Newtonian corrections to the two-body gravitational interaction.
method: The authors employ the diagrammatic effective field theory framework of general relativity, evaluating six-loop Feynman diagrams in the static limit.
result: They obtain the sixth post-Newtonian order static gravitational potential, contributing to the state of the art in analytical gravitational-wave modeling.
conclusion: This calculation advances the precision frontier for gravitational-wave astronomy but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Complete Computation Of All Three-Loop Five-Point Massless Planar Integrals
authors: Dmitry Chicherin, Yu Wu, Zihao Wu, Yongqun Xu, Shun-Qing Zhang, And Yang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitry Chicherin, Yu Wu, Zihao Wu, Yongqun Xu, Shun-Qing Zhang, and Yang Zhang

We calculate all three-loop, five-point, massless planar Feynman integral families in the dimensional regularization scheme. This is a new milestone in Feynman integral computations. The analysis covers four distinct families of Feynman integrals for this configuration, for all of which we derive th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111603] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes all three-loop, five-point, massless planar Feynman integral families in dimensional regularization, marking a milestone in perturbative amplitude calculations.
motivation: Higher-order loop integrals are essential for precision predictions in collider physics, particularly for NNLO and N3LO QCD calculations, but three-loop five-point massless planar families had not been fully evaluated.
method: The authors use dimensional regularization and modern integration techniques (likely including canonical differential equations and iterated-integral/function-basis methods) to derive analytic results for four distinct planar integral families.
result: Complete analytic expressions are obtained for all three-loop five-point massless planar Feynman integral families, extending the frontier of multi-loop scattering-amplitude computations.
conclusion: This represents a new milestone in Feynman integral evaluation and provides essential ingredients for state-of-the-art perturbative QCD calculations.

title: Investigation Of Medium Modifications To $^{12}\mathrm{C}$ Structure Functions In The Resonance Region
authors: S. Alsalmi et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): S. Alsalmi et al. (The JUPITER Collaboration: JLab E02-109 E04-001 E06-009)

We present results from a high precision experimental study of the nuclear modification of the longitudinal ([MATH]) to transverse ([MATH]) structure function ratio for bound nucleons in the resonance region. The inclusive electron scattering cross sections were measured in Jefferson Lab Exper…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 112501] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: A high-precision Jefferson Lab measurement of the longitudinal-to-transverse structure function ratio for bound nucleons in carbon reveals medium modifications in the resonance region.
motivation: Understanding how the internal structure of nucleons is modified when embedded in nuclear matter is a long-standing question in nuclear physics, relevant to interpreting neutrino-nucleus scattering and the EMC effect.
method: Inclusive electron scattering cross sections were measured with the JUPITER collaboration at Jefferson Lab, and the separated longitudinal-to-transverse structure function ratio was extracted for carbon-12 in the resonance region and compared to deuterium and models.
result: The measured ratio shows significant deviations from expectations based on free-nucleon models, indicating substantial medium modifications of the nucleon structure functions in the resonance region.
conclusion: The data provide stringent constraints on models of nuclear medium effects and are important for neutrino oscillation experiments that rely on nuclear targets.

title: Pressure-induced Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{CdPSe}}_{3}$
authors: Xu Liu, Boqin Song, Jian-Gang Guo, And Tianping Ying
abstract:
Author(s): Xu Liu, Boqin Song, Jian-gang Guo, and Tianping Ying

Pressure-induced superconductivity in [MATH] was initially attributed to a spin-state transition, drawing parallels with magnetic fluctuation-mediated pairing in iron-based superconductors. This magnetic-centric view was later challenged by the discovery of superconductivity in nonma…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134507] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports pressure-induced superconductivity in CdPSe3 and re-examines whether the pairing mechanism is driven by a spin-state transition or by nonmagnetic mechanisms.
motivation: Early interpretations of superconductivity in CdPSe3 invoked a spin-state transition and magnetic-fluctuation-mediated pairing analogous to iron-based superconductors, motivating a careful test of this magnetic-centric picture.
method: The authors use high-pressure experimental measurements (transport/susceptibility under pressure) combined with structural and electronic characterization to probe the emergence of superconductivity in the nonmagnetic regime.
result: Superconductivity in CdPSe3 is found to persist or emerge in the nonmagnetic regime, challenging the earlier spin-state-transition-based explanation and pointing to alternative pairing mechanisms.
conclusion: The work suggests that magnetic fluctuations are not the primary driver of superconductivity in CdPSe3, reorienting the discussion toward nonmagnetic pairing channels in this material family.

title: Sub-spin-flop Switching Of A Fully Compensated Antiferromagnet By Magnetic Field
authors: Honglin Zhou, Muyu Wang, Yinina Ma, Xiaoyan Ma, Gang Li, Zihao Tao, Xiquan Zheng, Liqin Yan, Yingying Peng, Ding-Fu Shao, Bo Liu, And Shiliang Li
abstract:
Author(s): Honglin Zhou, Muyu Wang, Yinina Ma, Xiaoyan Ma, Gang Li, Zihao Tao, Xiquan Zheng, Liqin Yan, Yingying Peng, Ding-Fu Shao, Bo Liu, and Shiliang Li

The control of antiferromagnets by magnetic fields represents a fundamental challenge in condensed matter physics, owing to their fully compensated magnetic order and vanishing net magnetization. Conventional methods rely on either uncompensated moments or high-field spin-flop transitions. Here, we …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154411] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies magnetic-field-induced switching of a fully compensated antiferromagnet via a sub-spin-flop mechanism.
motivation: Controlling antiferromagnets is challenging because their fully compensated magnetic order yields vanishing net magnetization, and conventional approaches rely on uncompensated moments or high-field spin-flop transitions.
method: The authors perform magnetic-field-dependent measurements on a fully compensated antiferromagnet to characterize a switching process that occurs below the usual spin-flop transition.
result: They identify a sub-spin-flop switching phenomenon driven by magnetic field in a fully compensated antiferromagnet.
conclusion: The work provides an alternative route for antiferromagnet control in condensed matter physics, but it does not address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Microscopic Mechanisms And Dual Pathways Of $5f$ Electron Itinerancy Tuned By Ligand Chemistry And Pressure In Paramagnetic Uranium Dipnictides
authors: Reyhaneh Ebrahimi-Jaberi And S. Jalali-Asadabadi
abstract:
Author(s): Reyhaneh Ebrahimi-Jaberi and S. Jalali-Asadabadi

The dual localized-itinerant character of uranium [MATH] electrons governs the electronic and magnetic properties of many actinide materials, yet the microscopic mechanisms controlling their tunable itinerancy remain incompletely understood. Here we investigate the uranium dipnictides ${X}_{…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175114] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies microscopic mechanisms and dual pathways controlling 5f electron itinerancy in paramagnetic uranium dipnictides under ligand chemistry and pressure.
