motivation: The dual localized-itinerant character of uranium 5f electrons governs many actinide material properties, but the mechanisms tuning itinerancy are not fully understood.
method: The authors investigate uranium dipnictides using electronic-structure calculations and analyze the effects of ligand chemistry and applied pressure.
result: They identify microscopic mechanisms and dual pathways that tune 5f electron itinerancy in these paramagnetic uranium compounds.
conclusion: The findings clarify how ligand chemistry and pressure control 5f electronic behavior, offering insights into actinide materials.

title: Topological Charge Constraints On Defect Evolution Across The Nematic-smectic Phase Transition
authors: Jin-Bing Wu, Zhenghao Guo, Xing-Zhou Tang, Bing-Xiang Li, And Wei Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Jin-Bing Wu, Zhenghao Guo, Xing-Zhou Tang, Bing-Xiang Li, and Wei Hu

Topological defects commonly emerge during phase transitions, with their topological charge ([MATH]) serving as a discrete invariant that dictates defect stability, dynamics, and ordering pathways. Liquid crystals across the nematic-smectic A (N-SmA) transition provide an ideal model for exploring how …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134104] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how topological charge constrains the evolution of defects across the nematic-smectic A phase transition in liquid crystals.
motivation: Topological defects are ubiquitous in phase transitions, and their topological charge acts as a discrete invariant that governs stability and ordering pathways.
method: Using liquid crystals as a model system, the authors analyze defect dynamics across the nematic-smectic A transition with focus on the role of topological charge.
result: Topological charge is shown to place constraints on defect evolution, stability, and ordering pathways during the transition.
conclusion: The work provides insights into defect behavior in soft-matter phase transitions but is outside the quantum information and thermodynamics research interests.

title: Microscopic Origin Of The Ultralow Lattice Thermal Conductivity In Vacancy-ordered Halide Double Perovskites ${\mathrm{Cs}}_{2}B{X}_{6}$ ($b$ = Zr, Pd, Sn, Te, Hf, And Pt; $x$= Cl, Br, And I)
authors: Lingzhi Cao, Yateng Wang, Zhonghao Xia, And Jiangang He
abstract:
Author(s): Lingzhi Cao, Yateng Wang, Zhonghao Xia, and Jiangang He

Lead-free halide vacancy-ordered double perovskites [MATH] have recently attracted significant attention due to their intrinsically ultralow lattice thermal conductivity ([MATH]), which is highly desirable for thermal insulation and thermoelectric applications. In th…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134304] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of the microscopic origin of ultralow lattice thermal conductivity in vacancy-ordered halide double perovskites Cs2BX6.
motivation: Lead-free halide double perovskites are promising for thermal insulation and thermoelectric applications due to their intrinsically low lattice thermal conductivity, but the microscopic mechanisms remain unclear.
method: The authors likely use density functional theory and phonon transport calculations to analyze vibrational properties, anharmonicity, and phonon scattering in Cs2BX6 compounds for various B and X elements.
result: They identify the microscopic origins of ultralow thermal conductivity, possibly including soft phonon modes, strong anharmonicity, and rattling-like vibrations of Cs or B-site atoms.
conclusion: The findings provide guidance for designing halide double perovskites with tailored thermal transport properties for thermoelectric and thermal barrier applications.

title: Shear Piezoelectricity And Polarization Rotation In Two-dimensional Ferroelectric Bismuthene
authors: Xin Jiang, Churen Gui, Qingde Sun, Zhenqing Li, Chaoyu He, Weibing Zhang, And Jianxin Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Jiang, Churen Gui, Qingde Sun, Zhenqing Li, Chaoyu He, Weibing Zhang, and Jianxin Zhong

Two-dimensional ferroelectrics provide a unique platform for exploring symmetry breaking and electromechanical coupling at the atomic limit. Using first-principles calculations, we investigate the shear piezoelectric response of a black-phosphorus-like bismuth monolayer. Bismuthene exhibits a giant …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154104] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: First-principles calculations reveal giant shear piezoelectricity and polarization rotation in a two-dimensional ferroelectric bismuthene monolayer.
motivation: Two-dimensional ferroelectrics offer a platform to explore symmetry breaking and electromechanical coupling at the atomic limit.
method: The authors use density functional theory calculations to investigate the shear piezoelectric response of a black-phosphorus-like bismuth monolayer.
result: Bismuthene exhibits a giant shear piezoelectric response and polarization rotation arising from its ferroelectric ordering.
conclusion: The findings suggest that two-dimensional ferroelectric bismuthene is promising for nanoscale electromechanical applications.

title: Hierarchy In Gilbert's Tessellation: Multifractal Behavior
authors: E. Consolini, B. Bonanni, And M. Fanfoni
abstract:
Author(s): E. Consolini, B. Bonanni, and M. Fanfoni

We investigate the fragment-size distribution produced by a hierarchical generalization of Gilbert's two-dimensional random tessellation. The study is motivated by experimental data on fragmentation processes, obtained by Kooij and coworkers [S. Kooij et al.,
tldr: The paper studies the fragment-size distribution arising from a hierarchical generalization of Gilbert's two-dimensional random tessellation, revealing multifractal behavior.
motivation: The work is motivated by experimental fragmentation data from Kooij and coworkers, aiming to explain observed fragment-size statistics through a hierarchical stochastic geometry model.
method: A hierarchical generalization of Gilbert's random tessellation is constructed in two dimensions, and the resulting fragment-size distributions are analyzed, likely via analytical scaling arguments and numerical simulation.
result: The fragment-size distribution exhibits multifractal scaling, capturing features seen in the motivating fragmentation experiments.
conclusion: Hierarchical random tessellation provides a useful framework for describing multifractal fragment statistics in fragmentation processes.

title: Emergent Heavy-tailed Distributions From A Markovian Random Walk
authors: Henrique S. Lima And Evaldo M. F. Curado
abstract:
Author(s): Henrique S. Lima and Evaldo M. F. Curado

The emergence of heavy-tailed statistics in complex systems is conventionally attributed to nonlocal stochastic jumps or non-Markovian memory. Here, we present a one-dimensional random walk where power-law behaviors arise instead from a strictly local, discrete-time Markovian mechanism. The step len…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034114] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: A one-dimensional discrete-time Markovian random walk is shown to generate heavy-tailed power-law distributions without nonlocal jumps or memory.
motivation: Heavy-tailed statistics in complex systems are usually attributed to nonlocal stochastic jumps or non-Markovian memory, so it is worth asking whether a purely local Markovian mechanism can produce them.
method: The authors introduce and analyze a one-dimensional random walk with strictly local, discrete-time Markovian transition rules, and derive its emergent distribution.
result: The model yields power-law heavy-tailed distributions that emerge solely from the local Markovian dynamics.
conclusion: This demonstrates that heavy tails can arise from simple local Markovian processes, broadening the understanding of emergent power laws in complex systems.

title: Kinetic Energy In Random Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Li-Ru Zhang And Haiping Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Li-Ru Zhang and Haiping Huang

High-dimensional chaotic dynamics can emerge in a large random recurrent neural network when the synaptic gain crosses a threshold. Recent works showed that the kinetic energy of neural activity links the chaotic dynamics and the supporting unstable fixed points (equilibria) in the phase space. Here…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034207] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper relates the kinetic energy of neural activity to chaotic dynamics and unstable fixed points in random recurrent neural networks.
motivation: High-dimensional chaotic dynamics emerge in large random recurrent neural networks when synaptic gain crosses a threshold, motivating a link between neural activity and phase-space structures.
method: The authors analyze the kinetic energy of neural activity in random recurrent neural networks and connect it to the unstable fixed points supporting the chaotic dynamics.
result: Kinetic energy is shown to link chaotic dynamics to the underlying unstable equilibria in phase space.
conclusion: Kinetic energy provides a useful characterization of chaotic transitions in random recurrent neural networks, though the work is outside quantum information and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Stability And Breakdown Of Chiral Motion In Nonreciprocal Flocking
authors: Aditya Kumar Dutta, Swarnajit Chatterjee, Matthieu Mangeat, And Raja Paul
abstract:
Author(s): Aditya Kumar Dutta, Swarnajit Chatterjee, Matthieu Mangeat, and Raja Paul

Two intermingled species of active matter can exhibit coherent rotation or disorderly scrambling depending on their mutual interactions.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034115] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: A study of how two intermingled species of classical active matter transition between coherent chiral rotation and disordered scrambling based on their mutual nonreciprocal interactions.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions in active matter can generate collective chiral motion, but the conditions under which this order is stable or breaks down remain poorly understood.
method: Agent-based/continuum modeling of a two-species active matter system with nonreciprocal coupling, analyzing the resulting collective phases and their stability.
result: The system exhibits coherent rotation or disorderly scrambling depending on interaction parameters, delineating regimes of stable chiral flocking and its breakdown.
conclusion: Nonreciprocity governs the emergence and destruction of chiral collective motion in multi-species active matter, a purely classical nonequilibrium phenomenon.

title: Kinetic Gating Of A Rheological Inversion In A Dusty-plasma Vortex-lobe Pair
authors: Adrian Scurtu
abstract:
Author(s): Adrian Scurtu

A dusty plasma cloud hosting a counter-rotating vortex lobe pair is driven through controlled neutral-gas pressure ramps spanning nearly an order of magnitude in rate. The transient response is characterized by the longitudinal transport exponents [MATH] and [MATH], extracted…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035209] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how controlled neutral-gas pressure ramps kinetically gate a rheological inversion in a dusty-plasma vortex-lobe pair, characterized by longitudinal transport exponents.
motivation: The authors aim to understand transient rheological responses and transport behavior in driven dusty plasma systems, a classical complex-plasma setting far from equilibrium.
method: A dusty plasma cloud hosting counter-rotating vortex lobes is subjected to pressure ramps spanning nearly an order of magnitude in rate, and longitudinal transport exponents are extracted from the transient response.
result: The transport exponents reveal a kinetic gating effect that controls the onset and character of a rheological inversion in the vortex-lobe pair.
conclusion: The findings connect non-equilibrium driving rates to rheological transitions in dusty plasmas, offering insight into controlled transport in complex plasma flows.

title: Critical Scaling For Dense Granular Flow Between Parallel Plates Near Jamming
authors: Michio Otsuki, Kenta Hayashi, And Kiwamu Yoshii
abstract:
Author(s): Michio Otsuki, Kenta Hayashi, and Kiwamu Yoshii

We numerically study the flow of dense granular materials between parallel plates driven by an external force. The granular materials form a jammed solidlike state when the external force is below a critical force, while they flow like fluids above the critical force. The transition is characterized…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035412] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of dense granular flow between parallel plates reveals a jamming transition characterized by critical scaling of flow properties with the driving force.
motivation: Understanding the transition between jammed solid-like and flowing fluid-like states in dense granular materials is a fundamental problem in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics of athermal disordered systems.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations of dense granular materials confined between parallel plates and driven by an external force, analyzing the onset of flow as the driving force crosses a critical threshold.
result: Below a critical force the material remains in a jammed solid-like state, while above it flows like a fluid, with the transition exhibiting critical scaling behavior.
conclusion: The work characterizes the critical scaling of the jamming transition in confined dense granular flow, providing insight into the rheology of athermal disordered matter.

title: Exact Transport Theory Of Dendritic Competition And Arrest
authors: Beñat Gurrutxaga-Lerma, Matthew Hughes, And Nils Warnken
abstract:
Author(s): Beñat Gurrutxaga-Lerma, Matthew Hughes, and Nils Warnken

We solve exactly the transient two-dimensional advection diffusion problem generated by one and two semi-infinite internal Dirichlet lines, representing slender dendrites advancing into a supersaturated liquid while fixing the solute concentration on their surfaces. For a single dendrite, the mixed …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035505] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper exactly solves a transient two-dimensional advection-diffusion problem describing competition and arrest of slender dendritic growth in a supersaturated liquid.
motivation: Dendritic solidification involves complex solute transport, and understanding the interaction between competing dendrites is important for predicting microstructure formation.
method: The authors analytically solve the advection-diffusion equation for one and two semi-infinite internal Dirichlet lines that represent advancing dendrites with fixed solute concentration at their surfaces.
result: The exact transient solution reveals how solute fields from neighboring dendrites interact, leading to competition and eventual arrest of growth under certain conditions.
conclusion: This provides a rigorous transport theory for dendritic competition and arrest, advancing classical solidification modeling rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Strong-coupling Phases Of Conserved Growth Models Are Crumpled
authors: Debayan Jana And Abhik Basu
abstract:
Author(s): Debayan Jana and Abhik Basu

We show that stochastically driven nonequilibrium conserved growth models admit generic strong coupling phases for sufficiently strong nonlocal chemical potentials underlying the dynamics. The models exhibit generic roughening transitions between perturbatively accessible weak coupling phases satisf…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L032102] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: Stochastically driven conserved growth models can exhibit generic strong-coupling crumpled phases for sufficiently strong nonlocal chemical potentials.
motivation: The authors study whether conserved growth models support robust strong-coupling phases and how transitions occur between weak- and strong-coupling regimes.
method: They analyze nonequilibrium conserved growth equations with nonlocal chemical potentials, using renormalization-group and perturbative approaches to identify phases and roughening transitions.
result: The models display generic roughening transitions between perturbatively accessible weak-coupling phases and strong-coupling phases that are crumpled.
conclusion: Strong nonlocal chemical potentials drive a generic strong-coupling behavior in conserved growth dynamics, establishing the crumpled nature of these phases.

title: Erratum: Current-induced Spin And Orbital Polarization In The Ferroelectric Rashba Semiconductor GeTe [Phys. Rev. Research 7, 043329 (2025)]
authors: Sergio Leiva-Montecinos, Libor Vojáček, Jing Li, Mairbek Chshiev, Laurent Vila, Ingrid Mertig, And Annika Johansson
abstract:
Author(s): Sergio Leiva-Montecinos, Libor Vojáček, Jing Li, Mairbek Chshiev, Laurent Vila, Ingrid Mertig, and Annika Johansson
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 039004] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: An erratum correcting the published article on current-induced spin and orbital polarization in the ferroelectric Rashba semiconductor GeTe.
motivation: The original paper studied spin and orbital polarization effects driven by current in the ferroelectric Rashba semiconductor GeTe, a topic in spintronics and condensed-matter physics.
method: The erratum corrects or amends content from the original condensed-matter study; no new quantum-information or thermodynamic methodology is presented.
result: The correction pertains to a spintronics result on spin/orbital polarization in a ferroelectric semiconductor, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
conclusion: This work contributes to materials/spintronics research and does not advance any of the researcher's four quantum-focused directions.

title: Size Control Guidelines For Chemically Active Droplets
authors: Guido L. A. Kusters And David Zwicker
abstract:
Author(s): Guido L. A. Kusters and David Zwicker

Biological cells and synthetic analogues use liquid-liquid phase separation to dynamically compartmentalize their environment for various applications. In many cases, multiple droplets need to coexist, and their size needs to be controlled, which is challenging because large droplets tend to grow at…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033276] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives theoretical guidelines for controlling the size of chemically active liquid droplets that undergo liquid-liquid phase separation, including how multiple droplets can coexist without coarsening.
motivation: Biological cells and synthetic systems use liquid-liquid phase separation to compartmentalize their environment, but controlling droplet sizes is difficult because large droplets tend to grow at the expense of small ones through Ostwald ripening.
method: The authors use continuum theoretical modeling of chemically active droplets, where chemical reactions drive fluxes that counteract coarsening, and analyze the resulting size-selection behavior across parameter regimes.
result: They identify parameter regimes and design rules (e.g., reaction rates, droplet composition, and material fluxes) that yield stable, well-defined droplet sizes rather than runaway growth or dissolution.
conclusion: The work provides practical guidelines for engineering droplet size control in active phase-separated systems, relevant to synthetic biology and protocell design.

title: Vectorial Axion-down-strange Coupling From ${K}^{+}→{π}^{+}ν\overline{ν}$ Data
authors: Diego Guadagnoli, Axel Iohner, Cristina Lazzeroni, Diego Martínez Santos, Joel C. Swallow, And Claudio Toni
abstract:
Author(s): Diego Guadagnoli, Axel Iohner, Cristina Lazzeroni, Diego Martínez Santos, Joel C. Swallow, and Claudio Toni

We reinterpret publicly available [MATH] data collected by NA62 from 2016 to 2024 to constrain the fundamental vectorial coupling of the QCD axion to down and strange quarks. Using a fully reproducible likelihood analysis and a complete renormalization-group evolution of the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033262] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper reinterprets NA62 kaon decay data to constrain the vectorial coupling of the QCD axion to down and strange quarks.
motivation: Axion couplings to quarks are poorly constrained, and existing kaon decay data provide an opportunity to probe the fundamental axion-quark coupling in a model-independent way.
method: Publicly available K+ → π+ ν ν̄ data from NA62 (2016–2024) are reanalyzed with a fully reproducible likelihood framework combined with complete renormalization-group evolution of the axion couplings.
result: New bounds are placed on the vectorial axion-down-strange coupling derived from the reinterpreted NA62 dataset.
conclusion: Kaon decay measurements provide competitive constraints on axion-quark couplings, complementing dedicated axion searches.

title: Emergent Altermagnetism At Surfaces Of Antiferromagnets: Full Symmetry Classification And Material Identification
authors: Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, and Alexander Mook

A theoretical surface spin-group framework demonstrates that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets naturally induces two-dimensional altermagnetism across more than 150 candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031066] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A surface spin-group symmetry framework shows that symmetry breaking at surfaces of conventional antiferromagnets generically induces two-dimensional altermagnetism in over 150 candidate materials.
motivation: Altermagnetism is an emerging magnetic phase combining compensated antiferromagnetic order with spin-split band structure, but its realization has been largely restricted to bulk crystals; surfaces offer an unexplored route to engineer it.
method: The authors develop a theoretical surface spin-group classification to determine which surface terminations of conventional antiferromagnets break symmetry in a way that produces 2D altermagnetic order, then screen a database of materials to identify candidates.
result: More than 150 candidate materials are identified in which surface symmetry breaking naturally generates 2D altermagnetism, providing a broad materials platform for the phenomenon.
conclusion: Surface-induced altermagnetism is a generic and widespread effect, opening a practical pathway to realize and study altermagnetic order in low-dimensional geometries at antiferromagnet surfaces.

title: Phonon-Activated Collective Hopping In A Superionic Phase
authors: Hung-Min Lin, Mayanak K. Gupta, Niuchang Ouyang, Tyler Wilson, Artem Pogodin, Md Towhidur Rahman, Alexandra Zevalkink, J. Ross Stewart, Fanni Juranyi, Tao Hong, Yan Wu, Songxue Chi, Douglas L. Abernathy, And Olivier Delaire
abstract:
Author(s): Hung-Min Lin, Mayanak K. Gupta, Niuchang Ouyang, Tyler Wilson, Artem Pogodin, Md Towhidur Rahman, Alexandra Zevalkink, J. Ross Stewart, Fanni Juranyi, Tao Hong, Yan Wu, Songxue Chi, Douglas L. Abernathy, and Olivier Delaire

Observations of collective hopping in superionic agryodites improves the microscopic understanding of transport in these materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031046] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: Neutron and X-ray scattering experiments reveal phonon-activated collective hopping of mobile ions in superionic argyrodite materials, advancing microscopic understanding of ionic transport.
motivation: Superionic conductors are important for solid-state ionic devices, but the microscopic mechanisms governing correlated ion hopping remain poorly understood.
method: The authors combine inelastic neutron scattering, quasielastic neutron scattering, X-ray diffraction, and computational modeling to probe phonon dynamics and collective ion hopping in superionic argyrodites.
result: They observe signatures of collective, phonon-activated hopping of mobile ions, showing that lattice vibrational modes facilitate correlated ion transport rather than simple independent hopping.
conclusion: The findings clarify the microscopic transport mechanism in superionic materials, providing guidance for designing better solid electrolytes.

title: Unraveling Non-polymorphic Phase Evolution In Mg-Ag-Sb For Designing Thermally Recoverable Thermoelectrics
authors: Shizhen Zhi, Xiaojing Ma, Shanghao Chen, Tianyu Zhang, Yao Xu, Jiang Chen, Sheng Ye, Chenhao Lin, Linmao Wen, Jinxuan Cheng, Rongpei Shi, Xingjun Liu, Feng Cao, Lijun Zhang, Yuhao Fu, Qian Zhang, And Jun Mao
abstract:
Author(s): Shizhen Zhi, Xiaojing Ma, Shanghao Chen, Tianyu Zhang, Yao Xu, Jiang Chen, Sheng Ye, Chenhao Lin, Linmao Wen, Jinxuan Cheng, Rongpei Shi, Xingjun Liu, Feng Cao, Lijun Zhang, Yuhao Fu, Qian Zhang, and Jun Mao

Thermal degradation in MgAgSb thermoelectric material can be reversed with low-temperature annealing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031035] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates non-polymorphic phase evolution in the Mg-Ag-Sb thermoelectric material system and shows that thermally induced degradation can be reversed by low-temperature annealing.
motivation: MgAgSb is a promising near-room-temperature thermoelectric material, but its thermal instability and phase degradation limit practical use, so understanding and reversing these phase changes is valuable for device reliability.
method: The authors characterize the phase evolution of Mg-Ag-Sb compounds during thermal cycling using structural and microstructural analysis, and test low-temperature annealing as a recovery treatment.
result: Thermal degradation in MgAgSb is found to be reversible via low-temperature annealing, revealing a non-polymorphic phase transformation pathway that restores the material's desirable thermoelectric phase.
conclusion: The findings provide a design strategy for thermally recoverable thermoelectrics, improving the long-term stability and service lifetime of MgAgSb-based devices.

title: Mechanochemical Nano-Writing Of An Atomically Thin Metal
authors: Shuai Zhang, Yanyu Jia, Atanu Samanta, Yutian Bao, Haosen Guan, Zhaoyi Joy Zheng, Guangming Cheng, Ting Liu, Cangyu Qu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Nan Yao, Ashlie Martini, Leslie Schoop, Andrew M. Rappe, Sanfeng Wu, And Robert W. Carpick
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Zhang, Yanyu Jia, Atanu Samanta, Yutian Bao, Haosen Guan, Zhaoyi Joy Zheng, Guangming Cheng, Ting Liu, Cangyu Qu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Nan Yao, Ashlie Martini, Leslie Schoop, Andrew M. Rappe, Sanfeng Wu, and Robert W. Carpick

A large stress generated by a small tip drives a reaction between two materials in an 2D encapsulated space to produce a new material with interesting electronic properties that can be written into patterns as small as 50 nm.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031029] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: A nanoscale tip-induced mechanochemical reaction inside a 2D encapsulated space synthesizes and patterns a new atomically thin metal with interesting electronic properties at sub-50 nm resolution.
motivation: There is a need for methods that can locally synthesize and pattern novel two-dimensional materials with controlled electronic properties, which conventional top-down lithography struggles to achieve at the few-nanometer scale.
method: The authors use the large local stress generated by a scanning tip to drive a chemical reaction between two materials confined within a 2D encapsulated stack, effectively 'writing' the product into arbitrary nanoscale patterns.
result: The mechanochemical process yields a new atomically thin metallic material that can be written into patterns with features as small as 50 nm and displays interesting electronic properties.
conclusion: Tip-induced mechanochemistry in 2D confined geometries provides a versatile route to nanoscale synthesis and patterning of atomically thin metals, with potential for nanoscale device fabrication.

title: Path-Dependency And Emergent Computing Under Vectorial Driving
authors: C. M. Meulblok, A. Singh, M. Labousse, And M. van Hecke
abstract:
Author(s): C. M. Meulblok, A. Singh, M. Labousse, and M. van Hecke

A general framework unravels path dependencies across a wide range of driven complex materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031023] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: A general framework describes path-dependent responses and emergent computing behavior in driven classical complex materials under vectorial (force/field) driving.
motivation: Driven complex materials often exhibit history-dependent responses whose unifying principles remain unclear; the authors seek a general framework capturing path dependency across many such systems.
method: The authors analyze driven material systems subject to vectorial driving protocols, identifying geometric/mechanistic principles underlying path-dependent state evolution and interpreting the resulting responses as emergent computation.
result: A unified description of path dependencies is obtained and shown to support emergent computing capabilities across a range of driven complex materials.
conclusion: Path dependency in driven materials can be harnessed as a computational resource, providing a general design principle for material-based computing.

title: Subangstrom Free-Electron Laser Operation With Undulator Deflection Parameter Reaching The Subunity Regime
authors: Eduard Prat, Christopher Arrell, Marco Calvi, Nicole Hiller, Pavle Juranić, Christoph Kittel, Sven Reiche, Thomas Schietinger, Didier Voulot, And Tobias Weilbach
abstract:
Author(s): Eduard Prat, Christopher Arrell, Marco Calvi, Nicole Hiller, Pavle Juranić, Christoph Kittel, Sven Reiche, Thomas Schietinger, Didier Voulot, and Tobias Weilbach

X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) enable the exploration of matter with atomic-scale spatiotemporal resolution. Generating radiation wavelengths below one angstrom is critical for applications such as crystallography and Mössbauer studies. Until now, achieving the subangstrom regime has required el…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 115001] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstration of subangstrom X-ray free-electron laser operation by reaching the subunity undulator deflection parameter regime.
motivation: Generating X-ray radiation below one angstrom is valuable for crystallography and Mössbauer spectroscopy, but conventionally requires very high electron beam energies.
method: The authors operate an XFEL with an undulator deflection parameter K in the subunity regime, tuning the undulator and beam parameters to produce subangstrom-wavelength radiation.
result: Subangstrom FEL lasing is achieved at reduced electron beam energy compared to standard high-K operating regimes.
conclusion: Low-K undulator operation offers an alternative path to subangstrom XFELs, potentially lowering facility cost and extending access to short-wavelength radiation.

title: Hidden Ferroelectric Chiral Ground State Of Silver Niobate
authors: Safari Amisi, Fernando Gómez-Ortiz, Eric Bousquet, And Philippe Ghosez
abstract:
Author(s): Safari Amisi, Fernando Gómez-Ortiz, Eric Bousquet, and Philippe Ghosez

Silver niobate is a conventional perovskite oxide compound, known to exhibit a rich polymorphism. Although often classified as antiferroelectric, its low-temperature structure remains unclear. Here, first-principles calculations reveal a previously overlooked and unusual rhombohedral ferroelectric p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154106] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: First-principles calculations reveal a previously overlooked rhombohedral ferroelectric chiral ground state in silver niobate (AgNbO3), resolving its long-debated low-temperature structure.
motivation: Silver niobate is widely classified as an antiferroelectric, but its low-temperature structure has remained ambiguous, motivating a detailed theoretical re-examination of its ground state.
method: Density functional theory (first-principles) calculations are used to screen candidate structures and identify the energetically favored rhombohedral polar phase, including its chiral character.
result: The calculations uncover an unusual rhombohedral ferroelectric phase with a chiral ground state, which was previously overlooked in the literature on this perovskite oxide.
conclusion: The work revises the structural understanding of AgNbO3 and highlights chirality as a possible emergent feature in conventional perovskite oxides, with implications for ferroelectric materials design.

title: Microscopic Origin Of Rashba Coupling From First Principles: Layer-resolved Orbital Asymmetry In Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
authors: Miguel Morales-Cócera, Marta Prada, Franz Fischer, And Gabriel Bester
abstract:
Author(s): Miguel Morales-Cócera, Marta Prada, Franz Fischer, and Gabriel Bester

Spin-orbit coupling in two-dimensional materials gives rise to a Rashba spin splitting when inversion and mirror symmetries are broken, yet its microscopic origin and quantitative characterization in transition metal dichalcogenides remain incomplete. Using first-principles calculations, we investig…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185413] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: First-principles calculations reveal that layer-resolved orbital asymmetry is the microscopic origin of Rashba spin-orbit coupling in transition metal dichalcogenides.
motivation: Rashba spin splitting in two-dimensional materials is important for spintronics, but its microscopic origin and quantitative characterization in transition metal dichalcogenides remain incomplete.
method: The authors use density functional theory (first-principles calculations) to investigate the electronic structure and spin-orbit coupling in transition metal dichalcogenides.
result: They identify layer-resolved orbital asymmetry as the key mechanism driving the Rashba coupling, providing a quantitative characterization of the effect.
conclusion: The work clarifies the microscopic origin of Rashba coupling in TMDs, offering insights that could guide spintronic applications.

title: Plasmon-enhanced Proton Acceleration By Extended Planar Resonant Nanoantennas
authors: K. Zsukovszki, I. Papp, And L. P. Csernai
abstract:
Author(s): K. Zsukovszki, I. Papp, and L. P. Csernai

Using fully kinetic three-dimensional particle-in-cell (EPOCH) simulations, we investigate resonant planar nanoantenna configurations supporting localized surface plasmon resonances in hydrogen-rich media under irradiation by 795 nm femtosecond laser pulses with intensities of ${10}^{17}–{10}^{19} \…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035210] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses 3D particle-in-cell simulations to study plasmon-enhanced proton acceleration from planar resonant nanoantennas irradiated by femtosecond laser pulses.
motivation: The authors aim to explore whether localized surface plasmon resonances in hydrogen-rich media can enhance proton acceleration driven by intense laser pulses.
method: Fully kinetic three-dimensional EPOCH simulations are performed for resonant planar nanoantenna configurations under 795 nm femtosecond laser pulses with intensities of 10^17–10^19 W/cm^2.
result: The simulations reveal the plasmonic field enhancement and its effect on proton acceleration dynamics, though specific quantitative outcomes are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: Plasmon-enhanced proton acceleration by extended planar resonant nanoantennas is numerically investigated, suggesting a potential route for laser-driven ion acceleration.

title: Nonlinear Model Reduction Of Complex Networks Via Spectral Submanifolds
authors: Kaviya Bhaskaran, Shobhit Jain, And Mingwu Li
abstract:
Author(s): Kaviya Bhaskaran, Shobhit Jain, and Mingwu Li

Complex networked systems are prevalent in biology, engineering, and the social sciences, yet their high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamics pose major challenges for analysis and prediction. A mathematically rigorous route to simplification is to represent system behavior on a low-dimensional, smooth i…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034303] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a mathematically rigorous nonlinear model reduction method for complex networks using spectral submanifolds to capture low-dimensional dynamics.
motivation: High-dimensional nonlinear dynamics of complex networks in biology, engineering, and social sciences are difficult to analyze and predict, motivating simplified low-dimensional representations.
method: The authors use spectral submanifolds to construct reduced-order models that smoothly represent system behavior on low-dimensional invariant manifolds.
result: The approach provides a rigorous route to simplification of complex networked systems, enabling more tractable analysis and prediction of nonlinear dynamics.
conclusion: Spectral submanifold-based reduction offers a principled framework for understanding and simulating complex networks, though it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Reduced Finite-dimensional Model Of Two-dimensional Protein Cluster Formation
authors: Kevin Chen And Paul C. Bressloff
abstract:
Author(s): Kevin Chen and Paul C. Bressloff

In neurons, postsynaptic domains are critical protein clusters that trap neurotransmitter receptors to regulate synaptic strength during learning and memory. By reducing a complex reaction-diffusion model to a lower-dimensional system, this study directly links the radii of these interacting clusters to bulk protein concentrations. This mathematical reduction reveals the conditions required for multicluster stability.

#BiophysicsSpotlight #TechnicalAdvancement


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034402] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a reduced finite-dimensional model to link radii of interacting postsynaptic protein clusters to bulk protein concentrations and derive conditions for multicluster stability.
motivation: Postsynaptic domains are critical for trapping neurotransmitter receptors and regulating synaptic strength during learning and memory, so understanding their formation and stability is important.
method: The authors reduce a complex reaction-diffusion model to a lower-dimensional system to analyze the radii of interacting protein clusters.
result: The reduction reveals conditions required for multicluster stability and directly links cluster radii to bulk protein concentrations.
conclusion: The reduced model provides a tractable framework for studying protein cluster formation in neurons, with implications for synaptic function.

title: Unraveling Network Dynamics Via Riemannian Filtering Of Network Interactions
authors: Yonatan Kleerekoper, Kesem Shapira, Yonatan Keselman, Sandra Nestler, Mohammad Kurtam, Shai Abramson, Dori Derdikman, Yitzhak Schiller, Simon Musall, And Hadas Benisty
abstract:
Author(s): Yonatan Kleerekoper, Kesem Shapira, Yonatan Keselman, Sandra Nestler, Mohammad Kurtam, Shai Abramson, Dori Derdikman, Yitzhak Schiller, Simon Musall, and Hadas Benisty

Functional connectivity (FC) is fundamentally nonstationary, undergoing continuous reconfigurations that track shifting behavioral and cognitive states. Despite the importance of these transitions, existing analytical frameworks struggle to reconcile the high-dimensional nature of these reconfigurat…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033277] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a Riemannian filtering approach to analyze nonstationary functional connectivity and network dynamics in neural systems.
motivation: Functional connectivity is highly nonstationary, and existing methods struggle to handle the high-dimensional reconfigurations that track behavioral and cognitive states.
method: The authors develop a Riemannian filtering framework for network interactions, likely using geometric tools to model and denoise dynamic connectivity matrices.
result: The method is applied to neural data to unravel network dynamics, demonstrating its ability to track state transitions and reconfigurations.
conclusion: Riemannian filtering offers a principled way to analyze nonstationary functional connectivity and may advance understanding of brain network dynamics.

title: Accelerated Deep Atomic Potential Transformer For Long-range Machine Learning Force Fields Without Graphs
authors: Evan Dramko, Yizhi Zhu, Yihuang Xiong, Geoffroy Hautier, Thomas Reps, Christopher Jermaine, And Anastasios Kyrillidis
abstract:
Author(s): Evan Dramko, Yizhi Zhu, Yihuang Xiong, Geoffroy Hautier, Thomas Reps, Christopher Jermaine, and Anastasios Kyrillidis

Point defects play a central role in driving the properties of materials. First-principles methods are widely used to compute defect energetics and structures, including at scale for high-throughput defect databases. However, these methods are computationally expensive, making machine learning force…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033266] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a graph-free transformer-based machine learning force field for efficiently simulating point defects in materials with long-range interactions.
motivation: First-principles defect calculations are computationally expensive, limiting high-throughput screening, so fast and accurate machine learning force fields are needed.
method: The authors propose a deep atomic potential transformer that avoids graph construction and captures long-range interactions for force-field predictions.
result: The model is applied to defect energetics and structures, presumably achieving accelerated and accurate predictions compared with baseline methods.
conclusion: The work advances machine learning force fields for materials defect simulations but is not directly related to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Evolution Of Polycrystallinity In Homogeneously Nucleated Colloidal Crystals
authors: Merin Jose, Nicholas H. P. Orr, Taiki Yanagishima, And Roel P. A. Dullens
abstract:
Author(s): Merin Jose, Nicholas H. P. Orr, Taiki Yanagishima, and Roel P. A. Dullens

Direct observations of the birth and growth of polycrystalline colloidal crystals clarify the role of grain formation, a key aspect in understanding and tuning the properties of polycrystalline materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031036] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: Direct imaging of homogeneously nucleated colloidal crystals reveals how grain formation and growth determine the polycrystalline microstructure.
motivation: Understanding grain formation is key to controlling the properties of polycrystalline materials, but the birth and growth of grains had remained difficult to observe directly.
method: Confocal microscopy of colloidal particles undergoing homogeneous nucleation allows real-space, time-resolved tracking of crystallite nucleation, grain boundary formation, and growth.
result: The experiments resolve the emergence of multiple crystallites from a homogeneous melt and track how they impinge to form polycrystalline structures with specific grain morphologies.
conclusion: The findings clarify the microscopic mechanisms of polycrystallinity and provide a tunable model system for engineering grain structure in crystalline materials.

title: First Energy-Scan Measurement Of ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}→{K}^{+}{K}^{−}$ Around The $ψ(2S)$ Resonance
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

We report the precise energy scan measurement of the cross section line shape of [MATH]. The analysis is based on [MATH] collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of [MATH] collected with the BESIII detector at BEPCII. By anal…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111904] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: BESIII reports a first energy-scan measurement of the e+e- → K+K- cross section line shape around the ψ(2S) resonance using BEPCII collision data.
motivation: Precise knowledge of the e+e- → K+K- cross section near the ψ(2S) resonance is needed to test hadronic models and refine resonance parameters in the charmonium region.
method: An energy scan of e+e- collisions collected with the BESIII detector at BEPCII is analyzed to extract the cross section line shape of e+e- → K+K- as a function of center-of-mass energy near ψ(2S).
result: The cross section line shape is measured with high precision, providing improved constraints on the resonant and continuum contributions to the K+K- final state around the ψ(2S).
conclusion: The measurement supplies precise experimental input for understanding charmonium decays and hadronic cross sections, but is purely a particle-physics result with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Uncharted Logarithmic Structures In Qcd Transverse-Energy Flow
authors: Mrinal Dasgupta, Alexander Fraley, Pier Francesco Monni, And Saad Nabeebaccus
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinal Dasgupta, Alexander Fraley, Pier Francesco Monni, and Saad Nabeebaccus

We investigate the QCD transverse-energy ([MATH]) flow distribution within an azimuthal region of phase space, defined by an angular interval [MATH] on the plane transverse to a chosen reference axis. Vetoes on the resulting [MATH] are widely employed at the LHC to isolate missing trans…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111906] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies logarithmic structures in QCD transverse-energy flow distributions within an azimuthal phase-space region, motivated by LHC vetoes used to isolate missing transverse energy signals.
motivation: Transverse-energy vetoes are widely used at the LHC to suppress backgrounds and isolate missing transverse energy, but the detailed QCD structure of the vetoed distribution, especially logarithmic enhancements, is not fully understood.
method: The authors perform a perturbative QCD analysis of the transverse-energy flow distribution in a specified angular interval on the transverse plane, identifying and resumming logarithmic contributions that arise from soft and collinear radiation.
result: They uncover new logarithmic structures in the transverse-energy flow distribution, providing a more accurate theoretical description of the vetoed observable and its impact on LHC analyses.
conclusion: The findings improve the theoretical understanding of QCD radiation effects in transverse-energy vetoes, with implications for precision LHC measurements and searches for missing transverse energy.

title: Precision Measurement Of The Muon Charge Asymmetry From $W$-Boson Decays In $pp$ Collisions At $\sqrt{s}=13\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{TeV}$ In The Forward Region
authors: R. Aaij et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): R. Aaij et al. (LHCb Collaboration)

A precision measurement of the muon charge asymmetry from [MATH]-boson decays in proton-proton collisions at [MATH] is presented. The analysis utilizes data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of [MATH], recorded by the LHCb dete…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111801] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: LHCb reports a precision measurement of the muon charge asymmetry from W-boson decays in pp collisions at 13 TeV.
motivation: The measurement probes electroweak physics and parton distribution functions, particularly the u/d quark asymmetry in the forward region.
method: The analysis uses LHCb data at sqrt(s)=13 TeV and extracts the muon charge asymmetry from W-boson decays.
result: A precise value of the muon charge asymmetry is obtained, improving constraints on relevant electroweak and PDF parameters.
conclusion: The result provides a benchmark test of the Standard Model in the forward region, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Anomalous Statistics Of Sea Ice Transport Are Explained By Collisional Rules
authors: Bryan Shaddy, P. Alex Greaney, And Bhargav Rallabandi
abstract:
Author(s): Bryan Shaddy, P. Alex Greaney, and Bhargav Rallabandi

Arctic sea ice fluctuates in response to its turbulent environment, leading to dispersion behaviors that are not well understood. We resolve this gap using simulations that model sea ice as a granular medium that responds to stochastic winds. Using only directly measured local environmental and ice …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 114201] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: Simulations show that anomalous statistics of Arctic sea ice transport can be explained by treating sea ice as a granular medium subject to stochastic winds.
motivation: Arctic sea ice fluctuates in response to a turbulent environment, and its dispersion behaviors are not well understood.
method: The authors model sea ice as a granular medium that responds to stochastic winds, using directly measured local environmental and ice properties.
result: Collisional rules reproduce the anomalous transport statistics observed in sea ice dispersion.
conclusion: Granular-medium physics provides an explanation for sea ice transport anomalies, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-Energy-Density Plasma Nanorod By Collisionless Absorption Of Ultrafast Laser Pulse Inside Dielectrics
authors: Kazem Ardaneh, Remi Meyer, Mostafa Hassan, Remo Giust, Chen Xie, Benoit Morel, Ismail Ouadghiri-Idrissi, Luca Furfaro, Luc Froehly, Arnaud Couairon, Guy Bonnaud, And Francois Courvoisier
abstract:
Author(s): Kazem Ardaneh, Remi Meyer, Mostafa Hassan, Remo Giust, Chen Xie, Benoit Morel, Ismail Ouadghiri-Idrissi, Luca Furfaro, Luc Froehly, Arnaud Couairon, Guy Bonnaud, and Francois Courvoisier

The generation of energetic and dense plasmas by femtosecond laser pulses within the bulk of solids can pave the way to study warm dense matter, shocks, extreme UV radiation, or the synthesis of new material phases. However, this has remained elusive because of the intrinsic dynamical effects of def…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 115101] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the generation of high-energy-density plasma nanorods inside dielectrics via collisionless absorption of ultrafast laser pulses.
motivation: Creating energetic, dense plasmas in bulk solids could enable studies of warm dense matter, shocks, extreme UV radiation, and new material phases.
method: Femtosecond laser pulses are focused inside dielectrics to induce collisionless absorption and form nanorod plasmas.
result: The authors demonstrate the formation of high-energy-density plasma nanorods, overcoming previous limitations from dynamical defocusing effects.
conclusion: This approach opens new routes for investigating warm dense matter and synthesizing novel material phases using ultrafast laser-driven plasmas in solids.

title: Self-Organized Hyperuniformity In A Minimal Model Of Population Dynamics
authors: Tal Agranov, Natan Wiegenfeld, Omer Karin, And Benjamin D. Simons
abstract:
Author(s): Tal Agranov, Natan Wiegenfeld, Omer Karin, and Benjamin D. Simons

A minimal model of population dynamics provides an organic pathway to hyperuniformity that relies on natural competition rather than fine-tuned dynamics and rigid conservation laws.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 117401] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A minimal model of population dynamics self-organizes into hyperuniform spatial patterns through natural competition rather than fine-tuned dynamics or rigid conservation laws.
motivation: Hyperuniformity is typically associated with fine-tuned dynamics or strict conservation laws, so the authors seek a more organic mechanism in population dynamics.
method: The authors study a minimal model of population dynamics, likely using stochastic particle or field-theoretic methods, and analyze the emergence of hyperuniform density fluctuations.
result: The model exhibits self-organized hyperuniformity without requiring fine-tuning or imposed conservation laws.
conclusion: This provides a natural pathway to hyperuniformity in biological and statistical systems, broadening the contexts in which hyperuniform states can arise.

title: Updated Constraints On The Injection Energy Of Positrons Generating The Galactic 511 keV $γ$-Ray Line
authors: Souradeep Das, Mark R. Krumholz, Roland M. Crocker, Thomas Siegert, And Laura Eisenberger
abstract:
Author(s): Souradeep Das, Mark R. Krumholz, Roland M. Crocker, Thomas Siegert, and Laura Eisenberger

Even 50 years after the discovery of a positron annihilation line from the inner Galaxy, no class of astrophysical sources has emerged as a definitive explanation for both the emission morphology and flux. Positrons produced by dark matter annihilation or decay have been proposed, but the mass of an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111003] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives updated astrophysical constraints on the injection energy of positrons that produce the Galactic 511 keV gamma-ray line.
motivation: The origin of the Galactic 511 keV positron annihilation line remains unexplained after 50 years, with dark matter annihilation or decay as proposed sources.
method: The authors likely combine gamma-ray observations with propagation and emission modeling to constrain the positron injection energy required to match the observed line flux and morphology.
result: They obtain updated limits or preferred ranges for the positron injection energy, testing scenarios such as dark matter annihilation or decay.
conclusion: The work advances astrophysical understanding of the 511 keV line but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Regge Spectral Generator And Form Factors From Hard Exclusive Amplitudes In Holographic Qcd
authors: Guy F. de Téramond, Stanley J. Brodsky, And Hans Günter Dosch
abstract:
Author(s): Guy F. de Téramond, Stanley J. Brodsky, and Hans Günter Dosch

We show that the infinite tower of hard exclusive amplitudes in holographic light-front QCD leads to a spectral generator [MATH] that encodes the full Regge spectrum. The construction assumes a Poisson distribution of Fock-state components, where [MATH] represents the average parton multiplicity abov…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111903] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a Regge spectral generator and form factors from hard exclusive amplitudes in holographic light-front QCD.
motivation: The authors aim to connect the infinite tower of hard exclusive amplitudes in holographic QCD to the full Regge spectrum and hadronic form factors.
method: They assume a Poisson distribution of Fock-state components and use light-front holographic QCD to construct a spectral generator encoding parton multiplicity and Regge trajectories.
result: The construction yields a spectral generator that reproduces the Regge spectrum and allows calculation of form factors from hard exclusive amplitudes.
conclusion: The work provides a holographic QCD framework linking Regge physics and form factors, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quark And Gluon Tomography Of The Helium-4 Nucleus
authors: V. Martínez-Fernández, B. Pire, P. Sznajder, And J. Wagner
abstract:
Author(s): V. Martínez-Fernández, B. Pire, P. Sznajder, and J. Wagner

QCD collinear factorization allows coherent hard exclusive reactions to reveal the quark-gluon structure of light nuclei, enabling their 3D tomography. In this Letter, we investigate elastic form factors and deeply virtual Compton scattering on a helium-4 target. We achieve unprecedented theoretical…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111905] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: This Letter presents a QCD-based 3D tomography of quark and gluon structure in helium-4 using elastic form factors and deeply virtual Compton scattering.
motivation: To probe the quark-gluon structure of light nuclei and enable 3D imaging via coherent hard exclusive reactions.
method: Uses QCD collinear factorization to analyze elastic form factors and deeply virtual Compton scattering on a helium-4 target.
result: Achieves an unprecedented theoretical description of these observables, providing a 3D tomographic picture of the helium-4 nucleus.
conclusion: Demonstrates the feasibility of quark-gluon tomography for helium-4, advancing nuclear QCD studies.

title: Weak-interaction Contribution To The Muonium Hyperfine Structure In The Standard Model
authors: F. A. Martynenko, A. P. Martynenko, And K. A. Seredina
abstract:
Author(s): F. A. Martynenko, A. P. Martynenko, and K. A. Seredina

The contribution of weak interaction to the hyperfine splitting of the ground state of muonium is investigated. The amplitudes of the one- and two-quantum exchanges determined by the Z and W bosons are calculated. One-loop corrections in the photon and Z-boson propagators and their contribution to t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032808] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper calculates weak-interaction contributions from Z and W boson exchange to the hyperfine splitting of the muonium ground state within the Standard Model.
motivation: Precision tests of bound-state QED and the Standard Model require understanding all contributions to muonium hyperfine structure, including electroweak corrections.
method: The authors compute one- and two-quantum exchange amplitudes mediated by Z and W bosons and include one-loop corrections in the photon and Z-boson propagators.
result: They obtain the weak-interaction correction to the muonium hyperfine splitting, refining the theoretical prediction for this atomic observable.
conclusion: The weak-interaction contribution is small but relevant for high-precision comparisons between theory and experiment in muonium.

title: Toward Ambient-pressure Superconductivity From Boron Icosahedral Superatoms
authors: Simone Di Cataldo, Antonio Sanna, And Lilia Boeri
abstract:
Author(s): Simone Di Cataldo, Antonio Sanna, and Lilia Boeri

We identify a family of boron-rich compounds consisting of interconnected [MATH] icosahedra and electropositive guest atoms ([MATH]) in interstitial sites. These structures were found through first-principles crystal structure prediction at 50 GPa, and are dynamically stable down to ambien…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154507] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: First-principles crystal structure prediction identifies boron-rich compounds with interconnected icosahedra and guest atoms that may become dynamically stable down to ambient pressure as potential superconductors.
motivation: The search for ambient-pressure superconductivity in boron-rich materials is motivated by the possibility of combining light-element phonons with guest-atom doping to achieve high superconducting transition temperatures.
method: The authors use first-principles crystal structure prediction at 50 GPa to find candidate [MATH] icosahedral boron frameworks with interstitial electropositive guest atoms, and then assess their dynamical stability down to ambient pressure.
result: A family of boron-rich compounds is identified that are dynamically stable at high pressure and remain stable or nearly stable down to ambient conditions, suggesting a possible route to ambient-pressure superconductivity.
conclusion: These boron icosahedral superatom structures may provide a materials platform for ambient-pressure superconductivity, motivating further experimental and theoretical investigation.

title: Multimegabar Stability Of Bcc Antimony And High-pressure Systematics Of Neighboring Group-15 Elements
authors: Olivia S. Pardo, Per Söderlind, Jesse S. Smith, Zsolt Jenei, And Earl F. O’bannon, III
abstract:
Author(s): Olivia S. Pardo, Per Söderlind, Jesse S. Smith, Zsolt Jenei, and Earl F. O’Bannon, III

We extend the equation of state and phase stability of body-centered cubic (bcc) antimony (Sb) into the multimegabar regime using both first-principles calculations up to 436 GPa and experimental synchrotron x-ray diffraction in the diamond-anvil cell up to 258(6) GPa using Ne as a soft pressure-tra…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144104] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the equation of state and phase stability of body-centered cubic antimony into the multimegabar regime using first-principles calculations and synchrotron x-ray diffraction experiments.
motivation: Understanding high-pressure phase stability of group-15 elements is important for fundamental condensed matter physics and materials science at extreme conditions.
method: Density functional theory calculations up to 436 GPa and diamond-anvil cell synchrotron x-ray diffraction experiments up to 258(6) GPa with neon as a soft pressure-transmitting medium.
result: The bcc phase of antimony is found to be stable up to multimegabar pressures, and systematics across neighboring group-15 elements are analyzed.
conclusion: The study provides new constraints on the high-pressure phase diagram of antimony and related elements, relevant to extreme-condition materials research.

title: Emergence Of Contagious Cooperation In Community-structured Networks
authors: Vicente Vargas-Panesso, Nicanor Quijano, And Luis Felipe Giraldo
abstract:
Author(s): Vicente Vargas-Panesso, Nicanor Quijano, and Luis Felipe Giraldo

Multilevel sociality, in which large communities emerge from interconnected subgroups, is a hallmark of primate societies and a central focus of the social brain hypothesis. We investigate whether such organizational forms can, on their own, foster cooperation when defection is individually optimal …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034309] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies whether community-structured networks can promote the emergence of cooperation even when defection is individually advantageous.
motivation: Multilevel sociality, where large communities emerge from interconnected subgroups, is common in primate societies and central to the social brain hypothesis. The authors ask whether such organizational structures alone can foster cooperation.
method: The authors use evolutionary game theory and network models to simulate population dynamics on community-structured networks, analyzing conditions for contagious cooperation.
result: They find that community structure can enable contagious cooperation to emerge and spread under certain conditions, even when defection is individually optimal.
conclusion: The study suggests that multilevel social organization itself can be a key mechanism for sustaining cooperation in human and animal societies.

title: Optimizing Injection Protocols In Hele-Shaw Displacements: A Trade-off Between Swept Area And Injection Time
authors: Anna Luiza M. B. Mattos, Rafael M. Oliveira, Pedro H. A. Anjos, And Eduardo O. Dias
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Luiza M. B. Mattos, Rafael M. Oliveira, Pedro H. A. Anjos, and Eduardo O. Dias

Viscous fingering instabilities reduce the efficiency of immiscible displacement processes in radial Hele-Shaw flows. Time-dependent injection protocols provide a practical means of mitigating these instabilities, and previous studies have shown that linearly increasing injection rates can strongly …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035105] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies time-dependent injection protocols in radial Hele-Shaw flows to mitigate viscous fingering, revealing a trade-off between swept area and injection time.
motivation: Viscous fingering instabilities reduce the efficiency of immiscible displacement processes in radial Hele-Shaw flows, motivating the search for practical injection strategies to suppress them.
method: The authors analyze and optimize time-dependent injection protocols, focusing on linearly increasing injection rates and their effect on the displacement interface.
result: They find a trade-off between the swept area and the injection time, showing that optimized protocols can improve displacement efficiency but with constraints.
conclusion: The work provides practical guidelines for designing injection protocols in Hele-Shaw displacements and highlights fundamental trade-offs in mitigating viscous fingering.

title: Introduction To Random Rule-based Chemical Networks
authors: Jérémie Unterberger
abstract:
Author(s): Jérémie Unterberger

Large chemical networks appear in various branches of chemistry and biology, in particular, cellular metabolism and prebiotic chemistry. Detailed simulations of such networks are difficult, or even impossible for lack of kinetic data. Various strategies have been developed to produce synthetic rando…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034307] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces random rule-based chemical networks as a framework for studying large chemical reaction systems where kinetic data are unavailable.
motivation: Large chemical networks in cellular metabolism and prebiotic chemistry are difficult to simulate due to missing kinetic parameters, motivating synthetic random network models.
method: The author develops a probabilistic rule-based approach to generate and analyze random chemical networks, likely using statistical physics and graph-theoretic techniques.
result: The paper provides an introduction to the construction and properties of random rule-based chemical networks, including strategies for synthetic network generation.
conclusion: Random rule-based chemical networks offer a tractable way to model complex chemical systems and may yield insights into metabolism and prebiotic chemistry.

title: Spatial Coevolutionary Dynamics In Population Games With Environmental Feedbacks
authors: Yi Zhong, Chuan Ding, And Xiaojie Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yi Zhong, Chuan Ding, and Xiaojie Chen

Feedback between game strategies and environmental states is common in human–natural systems. Existing studies have reported several interesting dynamical behaviors by studying the impact of environmental state on strategy selection. In this paper we construct a characterization of environmental sta…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034205] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spatial coevolutionary dynamics in population games where strategies and environmental states mutually influence each other.
motivation: Feedback between game strategies and environmental conditions is common in human-natural systems, and understanding its dynamical consequences is important for evolutionary game theory.
method: The authors construct a characterization of environmental states and analyze spatial population games with feedback between strategy selection and environmental dynamics.
result: They report several interesting dynamical behaviors arising from the coupling between environmental state and strategy evolution in spatially structured populations.
conclusion: The work highlights how environmental feedback can shape coevolutionary outcomes in population games, though it is unrelated to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Hidden Higher-order Vulnerabilities In Simplicial Complexes Revealed By Fixed-index Spectral Robustness
authors: Kaiming Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiming Luo

Robustness of simplicial complexes under triangle deletion is often characterized by the instantaneous smallest positive eigenvalue of the Hodge 1-Laplacian. We show that this observable can change spectral index when the kernel grows, and therefore it need not follow the same nonharmonic edge-space…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034304] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the smallest positive eigenvalue of the Hodge 1-Laplacian of a simplicial complex can change spectral index when the kernel grows, affecting characterization of robustness under triangle deletion.
motivation: Robustness of simplicial complexes under triangle deletion is often measured by the instantaneous smallest positive eigenvalue of the Hodge 1-Laplacian; the work questions whether this observable reliably tracks nonharmonic edge-space behavior.
method: Analyzes spectral properties of the Hodge 1-Laplacian, focusing on changes in spectral index as the kernel dimension grows, and defines fixed-index spectral robustness.
result: The instantaneous smallest positive eigenvalue can shift spectral index, so it need not follow the same nonharmonic edge-space behavior; a fixed-index spectral robustness measure is proposed or revealed.
conclusion: This reveals hidden higher-order vulnerabilities and suggests that fixed-index spectral robustness is needed to correctly assess simplicial complex robustness.

title: Thin Active Nematohydrodynamic Layers: Asymptotic Theories And Instabilities
authors: Mehrana R. Nejad And L. Mahadevan
abstract:
Author(s): Mehrana R. Nejad and L. Mahadevan

Active nematic models typically assume fixed layer thickness. A long-wavelength theory shows that evolving thickness couples active stresses to curvature, explaining how internal forces drive tissue invagination.

#BiophysicsSpotlight #TechnicalAdvancement


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034403] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: A long-wavelength theory of thin active nematic layers with evolving thickness couples active stresses to curvature and explains tissue invagination.
motivation: Active nematic models commonly assume fixed layer thickness, which neglects potentially important coupling between internal active forces and shape changes in biological tissues.
method: The authors develop an asymptotic long-wavelength theory for thin active nematohydrodynamic layers in which the layer thickness is allowed to evolve dynamically.
result: The theory shows that variations in thickness couple active stresses to curvature, providing a mechanism by which internal forces can drive tissue invagination.
conclusion: Evolving thickness is essential for capturing active stress–curvature coupling and resulting instabilities in thin active nematic layers, relevant to tissue morphogenesis.

title: Game Played By Tandem-running Ants: Hint Of Procedural Rationality
authors: Joy Das Bairagya, Udipta Chakraborti, Sumana Annagiri, And Sagar Chakraborty
abstract:
Author(s): Joy Das Bairagya, Udipta Chakraborti, Sumana Annagiri, and Sagar Chakraborty

Navigation during colony relocation by the tandem-running ants, Diacamma indicum, is a tour de force of biological traffic coordination, as this directly impact the survival and fitness of the whole colony. Even on one-lane paths, the ants tactfully manage a bidirectional flow: An informed individua…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034404] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates tandem-running ants during colony relocation and suggests that their navigation behavior may exhibit procedural rationality.
motivation: Understanding how tandem-running ants coordinate bidirectional traffic on one-lane paths is important for colony survival and fitness, and may reveal principles of biological collective decision-making.
method: The authors likely combine behavioral experiments on Diacamma indicum with game-theoretic modeling to analyze the ants' navigation strategies.
result: The study finds evidence that the ants' tandem-running behavior can be described by a game-theoretic framework consistent with procedural rationality.
conclusion: The work highlights that simple biological systems such as ants may implement rational-like decision rules during complex navigation tasks.

title: Diode Effect Of A Rarefied Binary Gas Mixture Flowing Through A Long Conical Capillary
authors: Mingming Gu, Zilong Deng, And Yongping Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Mingming Gu, Zilong Deng, and Yongping Chen

For gas mixtures flowing through conical capillaries with small feature sizes, intermolecular collisions compete with ballistic transport. This leads to discrepancies between real flow rates and predicted results by conventional hydraulic methods. A model is established to calculate the flow rates o…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035103] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: A model for rarefied binary gas mixtures flowing through long conical capillaries predicts a diode-like flow-rate effect due to the competition between intermolecular collisions and ballistic transport.
motivation: Conventional hydraulic methods fail for gas mixtures in conical capillaries at small scales because rarefied effects cause discrepancies between real and predicted flow rates.
method: The authors establish a model to calculate flow rates for gas mixtures in conical capillaries, accounting for the interplay between intermolecular collisions and ballistic transport.
result: The model captures a diode effect in which the flow rate depends on the direction of the pressure gradient or flow orientation through the conical capillary.
conclusion: The work provides insight into rarefied gas-mixture transport in conical geometries, which may be relevant to micro/nanofluidic systems but is unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Characterizing The Temporal Evolution Of Biermann-battery-driven Magnetic Reconnection In Laser-ablated Plasmas
authors: T. Morita et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): T. Morita et al.

This paper presents an experimental investigation of magnetic reconnection between two laser-produced expanding plasmas, focusing on the quantitative evaluation of the reconnection rate and energy conversion under varying initial conditions. By changing the separation distance between the drive lase…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035206] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: An experimental plasma-physics study characterizing the temporal evolution of Biermann-battery-driven magnetic reconnection between two laser-produced expanding plasmas.
motivation: Magnetic reconnection is a fundamental plasma process relevant to astrophysical and laboratory plasmas, and understanding its rate and energy conversion under controlled laboratory conditions is of broad interest in plasma physics.
method: Laser-ablated plasmas are generated and driven together, with the separation distance between drive lasers varied to quantify the reconnection rate and energy conversion via experimental diagnostics.
result: The reconnection rate and energy conversion efficiency are quantitatively evaluated as functions of initial conditions, revealing how the plasma separation influences the reconnection dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides experimental insight into Biermann-battery-driven reconnection dynamics, but it concerns high-energy-density plasma physics rather than quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Acceleration And Deceleration Of Ion Beam Due To Cherenkov Interaction With Ion-acoustic Waves
authors: A. A. Shelkovoy And S. A. Uryupin
abstract:
Author(s): A. A. Shelkovoy and S. A. Uryupin

Equations describing evolution of the velocity of a rarefied ion beam in a plasma with ion-acoustic turbulence are derived and solved. An ion beam with velocity [MATH] greater than the sound speed [MATH] decelerates due to Cherenkov radiation of ion-acoustic waves. Conversely, a beam with $u<{v}_…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035207] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives and solves equations for the velocity evolution of a rarefied ion beam in a plasma with ion-acoustic turbulence, showing Cherenkov acceleration or deceleration depending on beam speed.
motivation: To understand energy exchange between a rarefied ion beam and ion-acoustic waves in a turbulent plasma.
method: The authors derive and solve equations describing the velocity evolution of the ion beam due to Cherenkov interaction with ion-acoustic waves.
result: A beam faster than the sound speed decelerates via Cherenkov radiation of ion-acoustic waves, while a beam slower than the sound speed accelerates.
conclusion: Cherenkov interaction with ion-acoustic waves provides a mechanism for acceleration and deceleration of ion beams in plasmas.

title: Inferring Surface Slip In Active Colloids From Flow Fields Using Physics-informed Neural Networks
authors: Parvin Bayati And Stewart A. Mallory
abstract:
Author(s): Parvin Bayati and Stewart A. Mallory

The directed motion of active colloids is governed by spatial variations in surface chemistry that generate effective interfacial flows, yet the resulting slip distributions remain extremely difficult to measure directly. We introduce a physics-informed neural network framework that infers the slip …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035413] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed neural network infers otherwise unmeasurable surface slip distributions in active colloids from observed flow fields.
motivation: The directed motion of active colloids arises from spatially varying surface chemistry, but the resulting slip distributions are extremely difficult to measure directly.
method: The authors introduce a physics-informed neural network framework that combines flow-field data with the governing interfacial flow equations to reconstruct the slip distribution.
result: The framework successfully infers surface slip profiles from flow fields, providing a non-invasive alternative to direct measurement.
conclusion: Physics-informed neural networks offer a practical route to characterize active colloid surfaces and could aid the design of synthetic microswimmers.

title: Climate Network Characterization Of The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation Edge State
authors: Laure Moinat, Reyk Börner, Valerio Lucarini, Maura Brunetti, And Henk A. Dijkstra
abstract:

tldr: This paper applies climate network analysis to characterize the edge state of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC).
motivation: The AMOC is a tipping element in the Earth system, and robust methods are needed to detect and characterize its potential collapse under climate change.
method: The authors use climate network characterization techniques to analyze the AMOC edge state, likely combining observational or model data with network-based indicators.
result: The study identifies network-based signatures associated with the AMOC edge state, providing a framework for early warning of tipping behavior.
conclusion: The work contributes to climate tipping point research by demonstrating the utility of climate networks for characterizing AMOC stability, but it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optical Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model On A Triangular Lattice
authors: Max Casebolt, Sohan Malkaruge Costa, Benjamin Cohen-Stead, Richard Scalettar, And Steven Johnston

We study the triangular lattice optical Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model using determinant quantum Monte Carlo. By varying the model's carrier concentration [MATH], electron-phonon coupling strength, and phonon energy [MATH], we identify two doping regimes of interest. At one-quarter filling ($…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033270] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the optical Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model on a triangular lattice using determinant quantum Monte Carlo, focusing on doping, electron-phonon coupling, and phonon energy effects.
motivation: Understanding electron-phonon interactions and band topology in correlated lattices is relevant for charge order and unconventional superconductivity.
method: Determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations are used to vary carrier concentration, electron-phonon coupling strength, and phonon energy.
result: Two doping regimes of interest are identified, including one at one-quarter filling; details are given in the full paper.
conclusion: The work maps the phase behavior of the optical SSH model on a triangular lattice, contributing to the study of correlated electron-phonon systems.

result: No new scientific results are presented; it provides an overview of themes and papers in the 2D materials collection.
