title: High-Dimensional Dynamics In Low-Dimensional Networks
authors: Yue Wan And Robert Rosenbaum
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Wan and Robert Rosenbaum

The relationship between the dimensionality of a network’s structure and its dynamics is investigated, showing that networks with low-dimensional structures can produce either high- or low-dimensional responses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031025] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that networks with low-dimensional structural connectivity can nonetheless generate either high- or low-dimensional dynamical responses, depending on network parameters.
motivation: Understanding the link between the dimensionality of a network's structure and the dimensionality of its dynamics is important for interpreting activity in complex systems such as neuronal circuits.
method: The authors analyze network models with low-dimensional (e.g., low-rank or structured) connectivity and characterize the effective dimensionality of the resulting dynamics, likely using linearization and random matrix/spectral techniques.
result: Low-dimensional network structure does not uniquely constrain the dimensionality of the dynamics: such networks can exhibit either high- or low-dimensional responses depending on the regime considered.
conclusion: Structure–dynamics relationships are non-trivial, so inferring a network's effective dimensionality from structural low-dimensionality (or vice versa) is generally unwarranted.

title: Unlocking Emergent Resilience In Amorphous Metamaterials Via A Physics-Constrained Energy-Based Framework
authors: Lingyu Jia, Changliang Zhu, Qiaozhi Lei, Hua Tong, Jinkui Meng, Chengyan Xu, Xiangying Shen, And Lei Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Lingyu Jia, Changliang Zhu, Qiaozhi Lei, Hua Tong, Jinkui Meng, Chengyan Xu, Xiangying Shen, and Lei Xu

A physics-constrained design framework may aid the search for lightweight but resilient material.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031024] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: A physics-constrained, energy-based design framework is introduced to discover amorphous metamaterials that are both lightweight and mechanically resilient.
motivation: Designing lightweight yet resilient materials is challenging because conventional optimization approaches struggle to navigate the complex design space of disordered metamaterials. A physics-constrained framework could guide the search more efficiently.
method: The authors develop an energy-based, physics-constrained computational framework to design and optimize amorphous metamaterial architectures, using simulations and possibly experiments to validate mechanical performance.
result: The framework yields amorphous metamaterials exhibiting emergent resilience and favorable strength-to-weight characteristics beyond conventional designs.
conclusion: Physics-constrained energy-based design offers a promising route to lightweight, resilient metamaterials, though the work lies entirely within classical materials mechanics.

title: Predicting Liquid Properties And Behavior Via Droplet Pinch-off And Machine Learning

A powerful method allows hard to measure properties like viscosity and surface tension to be determined from a single, high-speed snapshot.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031021] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: A machine-learning method infers hard-to-measure liquid properties such as viscosity and surface tension from a single high-speed snapshot of droplet pinch-off.
motivation: Conventional measurement of liquid properties like viscosity and surface tension requires dedicated apparatus and controlled conditions, which can be impractical for limited samples or in situ settings.
method: The authors combine high-speed imaging of droplet pinch-off dynamics with machine-learning models trained to map the observed pinch-off behavior to the underlying liquid properties.
result: The trained models can recover viscosity and surface tension values from single-snapshot images of the pinch-off process with good accuracy.
conclusion: Droplet pinch-off coupled with machine learning offers a simple, fast route to characterizing liquid properties, though it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Generalized Lawson-Cordey-Mills Accessibility Of Fusion Ignition
authors: Luis F. Delgado-Aparicio, Masayuki Ono, And Jonathan E. Menard
abstract:
Author(s): Luis F. Delgado-Aparicio, Masayuki Ono, and Jonathan E. Menard

A generalized ignition-accessibility framework is developed that unifies Lawson power balance, Cordey accessibility, the marginal ignition ridge, ignition entry points, and Mills thermal-runaway dynamics into a single self-consistent description of reactor-relevant burning plasmas. The 0D analysis r…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 115102] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a generalized 0D framework unifying Lawson power balance, Cordey accessibility, marginal ignition ridge, ignition entry points, and Mills thermal-runaway dynamics for reactor-relevant burning plasmas.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a self-consistent description of ignition accessibility and burning-plasma behavior in fusion reactors, integrating several previously separate ignition criteria and dynamical models.
method: A 0D power-balance and accessibility analysis is constructed that generalizes Lawson and Cordey conditions and incorporates thermal-runaway dynamics to map ignition entry points and marginal ignition ridges.
result: The framework yields unified ignition-accessibility criteria and identifies conditions for entering and sustaining fusion ignition in reactor-relevant regimes.
conclusion: The generalized accessibility formulation may serve as a compact tool for assessing fusion ignition margins and burning-plasma operation, though it is outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Order Parameter For Morphodynamic Transitions In Braided Rivers: A Stochastic Compositional Framework
authors: Samuele de Bartolo And Carlo de Michele
abstract:
Author(s): Samuele De Bartolo and Carlo De Michele

We develop a stochastic simplex framework for width partitioning in braided river cross sections, modeling normalized channel widths as random compositional vectors. Two complementary models are introduced: the symmetric Dirichlet distribution, which models width allocation as exchangeable stochasti…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034305] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a stochastic simplex framework using Dirichlet-type models to describe width partitioning in braided river cross sections as random compositional vectors.
motivation: Braided river morphology lacks order parameters and statistical tools that properly respect the compositional (sum-constrained) nature of width partitioning across channels.
method: Normalized channel widths are treated as random compositional vectors and modeled with a symmetric Dirichlet distribution (exchangeable allocation) plus a complementary model capturing non-exchangeable structure.
result: The framework yields an order parameter characterizing morphodynamic transitions between braided river states, with the compositional statistics distinguishing different channel-width regimes.
conclusion: The stochastic compositional approach provides a principled statistical description of braided river morphodynamics, offering a quantitative order parameter for transitions in width partitioning.

title: Nonlinear Viscoelastoplastic Rheology Of A Viscous Vertex Model
authors: Shalabh K. Anand And Matthias Merkel
abstract:
Author(s): Shalabh K. Anand and Matthias Merkel

Morphogenesis involves complex shape changes of biological tissues. Yet, tissue shape changes depend on tissue rheology, which in turn arises from the interplay of large numbers of cells. Here, we link cell- and tissue-scale mechanics by constructing mean-field rheological relations for the vertex m…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033263] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs mean-field rheological relations linking cell-scale mechanics to tissue-scale viscoelastoplastic behavior in a viscous vertex model of biological tissue morphogenesis.
motivation: Tissue shape changes during morphogenesis depend on tissue rheology, which emerges from the collective mechanics of many cells, so a connection between cell- and tissue-scale mechanics is needed.
method: The authors derive mean-field rheological relations for a viscous vertex model, characterizing nonlinear viscoelastoplastic responses of the model tissue.
result: They obtain analytical relations describing the tissue's nonlinear viscoelastic and plastic behavior as a function of cell-level parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding how cellular mechanics give rise to macroscopic tissue rheology relevant to biological morphogenesis.

tldr: The paper uses real-space microscopy to visualize intrinsic aging and defect relaxation in n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 thermoelectric materials over long timescales.
motivation: Spontaneous property degradation in thermoelectric materials is typically attributed to external stimuli, but the authors argue intrinsic defect relaxation may govern long-timescale evolution.
method: Real-space visualization techniques (microscopy and structural/chemical characterization) are used to track defect relaxation in n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 thermoelectrics.
result: The study demonstrates that intrinsic defect relaxations, rather than external stimuli, drive spontaneous degradation of the thermoelectric material's properties.
conclusion: Understanding intrinsic aging mechanisms is essential for the long-term stability of Mg3(Sb,Bi)2-based thermoelectric devices.

title: Time-dependent Pore-network Modeling Of Ostwald Ripening In Porous Media
authors: Ademola Isaac Adebimpe, Sajjad Foroughi, Branko Bijeljic, And Martin J. Blunt

We present a time-dependent pore-network model that couples transient mass transfer in the aqueous phase, capillary pressure heterogeneity, and realistic pore-throat geometries to capture the dynamic evolution of gas clusters during Ostwald ripening in porous media. The model is applied to Bentheime…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035104] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: A time-dependent pore-network model is developed to simulate Ostwald ripening and gas cluster evolution in porous media.
motivation: Ostwald ripening controls gas cluster dynamics in porous media, but existing models often lack realistic pore geometry, capillary heterogeneity, and transient mass transfer.
method: The authors couple transient aqueous-phase mass transfer, capillary pressure heterogeneity, and realistic pore-throat geometries in a time-dependent pore-network model applied to Bentheimer sandstone.
result: The model captures the dynamic evolution of gas clusters during Ostwald ripening and demonstrates the influence of pore-scale geometry and capillary heterogeneity on ripening rates.
conclusion: Pore-network modeling with coupled transient mass transfer and realistic geometry provides a more accurate description of Ostwald ripening in porous media.

title: Wall-enhanced Dendritic Growth: An Exact Wiener-Hopf-Hankel Solution For Oblique Reflection

tldr: This paper derives an exact Wiener-Hopf-Hankel solution for dendritic solidification growth near an oblique impermeable wall.
motivation: The authors aim to capture wall effects on a dendrite's diffusive depletion field, including unsteady gap closure, which quasistatic frozen approximations cannot describe.
method: They formulate and solve an exact Wiener-Hopf-Hankel boundary-value problem for oblique reflection of the diffusion field from an impermeable wall.
result: The solution quantifies how wall obliquity and unsteady kinematics enhance dendritic growth through reflected depletion fields.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous mathematical treatment of wall-enhanced dendritic growth relevant to solidification microstructure modeling.
